documents.title: Sex and Lucía
documents.overview: Various lives converge on an isolated island, all connected by an author whose novel has become inextricably entwined with his own life.
documents.plot:
Sex and Lucía (Lucía y el sexo) is a 2001 Spanish drama written and directed by Julio Medem. Paz Vega and Tristán Ulloa lead a cast that also includes Najwa Nimri, Daniel Freire, Javier Cámara, Silvia Llanos and Elena Anaya.

Lucía, a waitress, is on the phone with her boyfriend Lorenzo, a novelist sunk in a long depression, after a bitter fight. Worried, she returns home to find the apartment empty and a suicide note. When the police call, she hangs up in dread, ignores their second call, packs a bag and flees to the Balearic island Lorenzo used to talk about.

The story then moves back in time. Six years earlier, on a moonlit night, Lorenzo has a fleeting sexual encounter in the sea with Elena, a woman he has just met. She later finds she is pregnant but cannot trace him. Some time after, while Lorenzo is struggling with writer's block, Lucía approaches him in a restaurant and confesses that since reading his latest book she has followed him and fallen in love. She soon moves in with him, and the film begins to blend their life with scenes from the novel he is writing.

Lorenzo eventually learns he has a daughter, Luna, and starts watching her outside her school, where he meets her babysitter Belén. Her provocative talk feeds his fiction, which Lucía reads as pure invention. One night Belén invites him to Elena's house. While the two are having sex, Luna is killed by the family's Rottweiler. Grief-stricken, Lorenzo falls into despair, his writing turns towards death, and he anonymously sends Elena, now running an inn on the island, a consoling story about a child who loves the sea. His guilt slowly breaks down his relationship with Lucía.

In the present, Lucía befriends a diver named Carlos and then Elena, and the two women gradually realize what links them. Meanwhile, Lorenzo recovers in hospital after an "accident". When his editor says Lucía probably believes he is dead, Lorenzo guesses where she has gone and travels to the island, where the three finally face what connects them.

Sogecine produced the film, shooting in Fuerteventura and Madrid. The lighthouse at Cap de Barbaria on Formentera became a central image. Critics were generally favorable: Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said that beneath its gratuitous nudity lies a complex and visually striking film.

documents.title: Monster's Ball
documents.tagline: A lifetime of change can happen in a single moment.
documents.overview: Set in the southern USA, a racist white man, Hank, falls in love with a black woman named Leticia. Ironically, Hank is a prison guard working on Death Row who executed Leticia's husband. Hank and Leticia's inter-racial affair leads to confusion and new ideas for the two unlikely lovers.
documents.plot: A prison guard begins a tentative romance with the unsuspecting widow of a man whose execution he presided over.

documents.title: Blood Diamond
documents.tagline: It will cost you everything.
documents.overview: An ex-mercenary turned smuggler. A Mende fisherman. Amid the explosive civil war overtaking 1999 Sierra Leone, these men join for two desperate missions: recovering a rare pink diamond of immense value and rescuing the fisherman's son, conscripted as a child soldier into the brutal rebel forces ripping a swath of torture and bloodshed countrywide.
documents.plot:
In 1999, Sierra Leone is ravaged by civil war. The Revolutionary United Front terrorizes the countryside and enslaves many locals to harvest diamonds, which fund their increasingly successful war effort. Solomon Vandy, a Mende fisherman from Shenge, is separated from his family and assigned to a workforce overseen by Captain Poison, a ruthless warlord.
While mining a river, Vandy discovers an enormous pink diamond. Captain Poison tries to take the stone, but the area is suddenly raided by government troops. Vandy buries the stone before being captured. Vandy and Poison are incarcerated in Freetown with Danny Archer, a white Rhodesian gunrunner and Angola War veteran jailed for trying to smuggle diamonds into Liberia. The diamonds were intended for Rudolph van de Kaap, a corrupt Afrikaner mining executive from South Africa.
Hearing of the pink diamond in prison, Archer arranges for him and Vandy to be freed. He travels to Cape Town to meet his employer: Colonel Coetzee, an Afrikaner formerly with the apartheid-era South African Defence Force (whom Archer also served under in the 32 Battalion), which now commands a private military company. Archer wants the diamond so he can sell it to Van de Kaap and retire, but Coetzee wants it as compensation for Archer's botched smuggling mission. Archer returns to Sierra Leone, locates Vandy, and offers to help him find his family if he will help recover the diamond.
The RUF conquers Freetown, while Vandy's son Dia is captured to serve as a child soldier under a liberated Captain Poison. Archer and Vandy narrowly escape to Lungi, where they plan to reach Kono with the help of an American journalist, Maddy Bowen, in exchange for Archer providing evidence of the illicit diamond trade. Maddy helps Vandy locate his remaining family at a refugee camp in Guinea. While they travel, Archer reveals to Maddy that his parents were brutally killed by Black rebels after the fall of Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe). As a child, he fled to South Africa, where he eventually joined the military and served in Angola. Eventually, the trio arrive in Kono after a harrowing journey, where Coetzee and his private army—contracted by the Sierra Leone government—prepares to repulse the rebel offensive.
While Maddy gets out with her story, the two men set out for Captain Poison's encampment. Dia, stationed with the RUF garrison there, is confronted by Vandy, but having been brainwashed he refuses to acknowledge his father. Archer radios the site's coordinates to Coetzee, who directs a combined air and ground assault on the camp. Vandy finds Captain Poison and beats him to death with a shovel as the mercenaries overwhelm the RUF defenders.
Coetzee then forces Vandy to produce the diamond, but is killed by Archer, who realizes Coetzee would eventually kill them both. Dia briefly holds the pair at gunpoint, but Vandy confronts him again and renews their familial bond.
production_companies: Lonely Film Productions GmbH & Co. KG.

documents.title: Rocky IV
documents.tagline: Get ready for the next world war.
documents.overview: Rocky Balboa proudly holds the world heavyweight boxing championship, but a new challenger has stepped forward: Drago, a six-foot-four, 261-pound fighter who has the backing of the Soviet Union.
documents.plot:
Rocky IV is a 1985 American sports drama film directed by Sylvester Stallone and starring Sylvester Stallone, Talia Shire, Carl Weathers, and Dolph Lundgren. The film is the fourth installment in the Rocky franchise.

The movie begins with Rocky Balboa (Sylvester Stallone) training for his upcoming fight against Ivan Drago (Dolph Lundgren), a formidable Soviet boxer who has been dominating the ring since he was a child. As Rocky prepares for the big match, he also deals with personal struggles, including the death of his friend and trainer, Mickey Goldmill's (Burgess Meredith) brother, Paulie.

Meanwhile, Ivan Drago is introduced as a ruthless and efficient fighter who is trained by the Soviet Union to crush American spirit and pride. The two fighters engage in a heated rivalry, with Rocky determined to defeat Drago and prove that he is still a force to be reckoned with in the ring.

As the fight approaches, Rocky's wife Adrian (Talia Shire) becomes increasingly concerned about his safety, while Rocky's friend Apollo Creed's (Carl Weathers) widow, Brigitte (Brigitte Nielsen), tries to persuade Rocky to retire from boxing. However, Rocky is determined to face Drago and prove that he can overcome any obstacle.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Ivan Drago kills Apollo Creed in the ring during their fight, which sparks outrage across America. Rocky sees this as an opportunity to avenge his friend's death and defeat Drago in the ring.

The climactic final fight between Rocky and Drago is intense and brutal, with both fighters giving it their all. In the end, Rocky emerges victorious, but not without suffering severe injuries. The film ends with Rocky standing over Drago's defeated body, having avenged Apollo Creed's death and proved that he still has what it takes to be a champion.

Throughout the film, Sylvester Stallone delivers a powerful performance as Rocky Balboa, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Dolph Lundgren is equally impressive as Ivan Drago, conveying the Soviet boxer's ruthless efficiency and determination. The film's themes of patriotism, loyalty, and redemption are timeless and continue to resonate with audiences today.

Overall, Rocky IV is a classic sports drama that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and emotional depth. With its iconic performances, memorable characters, and thrilling plot twists, it remains one of the most beloved films in the Rocky franchise.

documents.title: The Fountain
documents.tagline: Death is the road to awe
documents.overview: Spanning over one thousand years, and three parallel stories, The Fountain is a story of love, death, spirituality, and the fragility of our existence in this world.
documents.plot: Spanning over one thousand years, and three parallel stories, The Fountain is a story of love, death, spirituality, and the fragility of our existence in this world.

documents.title: Stalker
documents.tagline: There's no need to speak. You must only...concentrate and recall all your past life. When a man thinks of the past, he becomes kinder.
documents.overview: Near a gray and unnamed city is the Zone, a place guarded by barbed wire and soldiers, and where the normal laws of physics are victim to frequent anomalies. A stalker guides two men into the Zone, specifically to an area in which deep-seated desires are granted.
documents.plot:
"The Zone" is a huge tract of open land where the normal laws of physics supposedly do not apply, containing supernatural hazards. At the heart of the Zone lies a "Room" that is said to grant the wishes of anyone who steps inside. The government has fenced off the Zone, subjecting "Stalkers", people who illegally guide others through the Zone, to harsh prison time if caught crossing the border.
One Stalker has just returned from a long prison sentence to his wife and daughter. To his wife's horror, a disaffected writer and a physics professor immediately hire the Stalker to take them through the Zone. Needing the money, he meets the Writer and Professor in a rundown bar-café, warning them that they must do what he says to survive the dangers that lie ahead. He explains that the Zone is a living thing that visitors must respect.
The trio evades the Zone's military guards by following a train through the gate, riding through the Zone's vast wilderness on a railway work car. The Zone contains such human remnants as old abandoned industrial facilities, corpses, guns, and tanks. The Stalker cautiously tests for anomalies as they painstakingly make their way toward the Room, though nothing unusual occurs.
The three men discuss their reasons for wanting to visit the Room as they travel: the Writer fears losing his inspiration, the calm Professor hopes to analyze the Zone in order to win a Nobel Prize, and the Stalker insists he has no motive beyond the altruistic aim of aiding the desperate to their desires. He mentions that his mentor, another Stalker named "Porcupine", obtained great riches by entering the Room but then hanged himself when he returned home.
The trio draw lots to determine that the Writer will go first through an especially long, dark, ominous passageway that the Stalker calls the "meat grinder". Nervously, the Writer passes through without harm, shocking the Stalker, who reveals that the meat grinder kills anyone the Zone deems morally unworthy. The Writer forges ahead and delivers a soliloquy directly to camera about the futility of knowledge and feeling overwhelmed and criticized by other people. He returns to the others, and the Stalker reveals that Porcupine sent a brother ahead of him into the meat grinder, where the brother was killed. The Stalker then recites a poem about never being satisfied, and the Writer rages at the Stalker for assuming he was morally unworthy.
Suddenly, a phone in the antechamber rings. The surprised Professor uses it to call an old enemy scientist, gloating about finding a bomb the scientist had hidden, which the Professor previously worked on. As the trio prepare to enter the Room, the Professor reveals he has brought the 20-kiloton bomb in his backpack to destroy the Room and therefore prevent evil men from abusing it for gain. He blames the Room, the Stalkers, and their clients for the recent rise of crime, political strife, and destructive science.

documents.title: The Pursuit of Happyness
documents.tagline: For his son, one man will reach for the impossible.
documents.overview: A struggling salesman takes custody of his son as he's poised to begin a life-changing professional career.
documents.plot:
The Pursuit of Happyness is a biographical drama film directed by Gabriele Muccino, released in 2006 by Columbia Pictures. The movie is based on the true story of Chris Gardner, a struggling single father who becomes homeless with his young son.

The film begins with Chris Gardner (played by Will Smith), a determined and ambitious stockbroker who has just lost his job due to the financial crisis. Despite having no income, Chris decides to move to San Francisco with his 5-year-old son Christopher (played by Jaden Smith) in order to pursue a career in finance.

Initially, Chris faces numerous challenges as he struggles to find a new job and make ends meet. He is forced to sleep on the streets, often sharing a bench or a park bench with other homeless people. Despite his hardships, Chris remains optimistic and determined to provide a better life for himself and his son.

As Chris navigates the harsh realities of homelessness, he also faces personal struggles as a single father. His relationship with Christopher is put to the test as they face poverty, hunger, and uncertainty about their future. However, Chris's love and dedication to his son keep him going, and he finds ways to make ends meet by selling blood plasma and applying for jobs.

Meanwhile, Chris meets a social worker named Dr. Seuss (played by Thandie Newton), who helps him navigate the system and find temporary housing. He also befriends a homeless man named John (played by Brian Howe), who becomes a source of inspiration and support for Chris.

As the story unfolds, Chris's determination and perseverance begin to pay off. He lands an internship at a prestigious brokerage firm, Dean Witter Reynolds, where he meets a mentor named Jim (played by Jon Voight). With Jim's guidance, Chris is able to secure a full-time job offer and eventually becomes a successful stockbroker.

The film's climax features Chris's emotional reunion with Christopher, who has been struggling to cope with his father's absence. The two share a heartwarming moment as they finally find stability and security together.

Throughout the movie, Will Smith delivers a powerful performance that showcases his range as an actor. His portrayal of Chris Gardner is both nuanced and authentic, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of a man who has faced unimaginable hardship.

The Pursuit of Happyness is a testament to the human spirit's capacity for resilience and determination. The film's themes of hope, perseverance, and the importance of family are timeless and universal, making it a must-see for audiences worldwide.

documents.title: La Vie en Rose
documents.tagline: The Extraordinary Story of Edith Piaf.
documents.overview: From the mean streets of the Belleville district of Paris to the dazzling limelight of New York's most famous concert halls, Edith Piaf's life was a constant battle to sing and survive, to live and love. Raised in her grandmother's brothel, Piaf was discovered in 1935 by nightclub owner Louis Leplee, who persuaded her to sing despite her extreme nervousness. Piaf became one of France's immortal icons, her voice one of the indelible signatures of the 20th century.
documents.plot:
The film is structured as a largely non-linear series of key events from the life of Édith Piaf. The film begins with elements from her childhood, and at the end with the events prior to and surrounding her death, poignantly juxtaposed by a performance of her song, "Non, je ne regrette rien" (No, I do not Regret Anything).
Beginning in 1918, young Édith suffers a chaotic childhood and is eventually sent to live with her paternal-grandmother, who runs a brothel in Normandy. Édith witnesses the brutal business of prostitution. When she suffers an episode of keratitis-induced blindness, a kind-hearted sex worker named Titine tenderly cares for Édith.
Édith's World War I veteran father collects her to accompany him while he works as a circus acrobat. One night, Édith sees a vision of St Thérèse in a fire eater's flames. St Thérèse says she will always be with Édith—a belief that she carries for the rest of her life. When Édith is nine years old, her father leaves the circus and performs on the streets of Paris. During a lackluster performance, a passerby asks if Édith is part of the show. She spontaneously sings "La Marseillaise" with raw emotion, mesmerizing the street crowd.
Years later, nightclub owner Louis Leplée hires Édith to sing at his club and gives her the stage surname of Piaf, a colloquialism for sparrow that is inspired by her diminutive height of only 1.47m (4 ft 8in). However, Leplée is soon shot dead and the police suspect it is due to Édith's connections to the mafia. When she next attempts a show at a cabaret, she is jeered off the stage by a hostile crowd. Things go from bad to worse when her best friend, Mômone, is forcibly taken to a convent. Desperate, Édith turns to Raymond Asso, a songwriter and accompanist. Through harsh means, he enlivens her stage presence with hand gestures, better enunciation, and other lessons.
Édith's career progresses and she achieves fame. While performing in New York City, Édith meets Marcel Cerdan, a fellow French national and a middleweight boxer competing for the World Champion title. Despite him being married, Édith believes she is falling in love with Marcel. An affair ensues and, while it is supposedly a secret, "La Vie En Rose" is played for Marcel wherever he goes. Édith persuades Marcel to fly from Paris to join her in New York, and he wakes her up in her bedroom with a kiss. She goes to get coffee and is informed by her entourage that Marcel was killed when his plane crashed. Édith hysterically searches for his ghost.
The narrative bookends scenes from Édith's middle life with repeated vignettes. One set of memories shows Édith with short curly hair, singing on stage and collapsing. She develops arthritis, as well as a severe morphine addiction. Her husband, Jacques Pills, persuades her to enter drug rehabilitation, and she travels to California with him. A now-sober but manic Édith drives around in a convertible while joking and teasing her compatriots.

documents.title: Pan's Labyrinth
documents.tagline: What happens when make-believe believes it's real?
documents.overview: Living with her tyrannical stepfather in a new home with her pregnant mother, 10-year-old Ofelia feels alone until she explores a decaying labyrinth guarded by a mysterious faun who claims to know her destiny. If she wishes to return to her real father, Ofelia must complete three terrifying tasks.
documents.plot:
Pan's Labyrinth (El laberinto del fauno) is a Spanish-language dark fantasy film of 2006 written, produced and directed by Guillermo del Toro, set in Francoist Spain in 1944. Ivana Baquero stars as Ofelia, a girl drawn into a mythical world, with Sergi López as her brutal stepfather Captain Vidal, Maribel Verdú as the housekeeper Mercedes, Doug Jones as both the Faun and the child-eating Pale Man and Ariadna Gil as Ofelia's mother Carmen.

A fable tells of Princess Moanna, daughter of the king of the underworld, who visited the human world, lost her memory in the sunlight and died as a mortal; her father built labyrinths across the world as portals for her spirit's return. Ofelia travels with her pregnant, ailing mother to a rural outpost commanded by Vidal, a fanatical Francoist officer hunting the Maquis resistance. An insect she takes for a fairy leads her to an ancient stone labyrinth, where a faun tells her she is the reincarnated princess and gives her a book revealing three tasks she must perform to return to her kingdom. Meanwhile Mercedes secretly aids her brother Pedro and the guerrillas.

Ofelia retrieves a key from the belly of a giant toad, and the faun gives her a mandrake root to keep beneath her mother's bed, easing her illness. In the second task she takes a dagger from the lair of the Pale Man but, ignoring the faun's warning, eats two grapes; the monster wakes and devours two fairies, and the furious faun abandons her. Vidal's cruelty escalates as he murders two farmers and tortures a captured guerrilla, whom Ferreiro mercifully kills before Vidal shoots the doctor. When Carmen burns the mandrake, she dies giving birth to Vidal's son. Exposed as a spy, Mercedes slashes Vidal's face and escapes. The faun returns with a final task: bring her baby brother into the labyrinth. There he asks for a drop of the infant's blood, but Ofelia refuses to harm him. Vidal, who cannot see the faun, takes the baby and shoots her. At the labyrinth's entrance he is surrounded by the Maquis; Mercedes tells him his son will never know his name, and Pedro kills him. As Ofelia dies, her blood falls onto an altar, and she awakens in a golden throne room, where her father the king tells her she passed the last test by shedding her own blood rather than an innocent's, and she takes her place beside him and her mother.

Premiering at Cannes in May 2006, the film grossed $83 million worldwide and won three Academy Awards and three BAFTAs. It scored 98 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Breakfast on Pluto
documents.tagline: Same world. Different planet.
documents.overview: In the 1970s, a foundling lass, Patrick "Kitten" Braden, comes of age by leaving her Irish town for London, in part to look for her mother and in part because her transgender nature is beyond the town's understanding.
documents.plot:
In 1958, in the fictional small Irish town of Tyrellin, County Cavan, Eily Bergin leaves her newborn baby, Patrick Braden, on the doorstep of the local parochial house, where the baby's father, Father Liam, lives. Patrick is placed with an unloving foster mother. Young Patrick dons a dress and lipstick, which angers his foster family. Patrick is accepted by his close friends Charlie, Irwin and Lawrence, as well as by Lawrence's father, who tells Patrick that Eily resembled American actress Mitzi Gaynor.
In his late teens in the 1970s, Patrick gets into trouble in school for writing an explicit story imagining how he was conceived by his parents and inquiring about where to undergo a sex change. Patrick comes out as transgender and renames herself Patricia "Kitten" Braden. In confession, she asks Father Liam about Eily but is rebuffed.
Kitten runs away from home, getting a ride with a glam rock band, Billy Hatchet and the Mohawks, and flirting with frontman Billy. He sets Kitten up in a trailer, where she discovers he is hiding guns for the IRA. Meanwhile, Irwin has begun to work with the IRA, much to his now-girlfriend Charlie's dismay. Kitten scoffs at Irwin's politics, but after Lawrence is killed by police detonating a suspected loyalist car bomb, she tosses their gun cache into a lake. Billy abandons Kitten to flee the IRA, forcing her to face the IRA men alone. Her lack of connection to their politics saves her from being murdered.
Kitten heads to London in search of Eily, but initial inquiries prove fruitless. Penniless, she finds shelter in a tiny cottage in a park, only to find that it is a Wombles children's theme park. Kitten takes a job as a singing and dancing Womble, but immediately loses it when her sponsor and co-worker punches their boss. Forced into prostitution, she is strangled by her first client, narrowly escaping by spraying Chanel No. 5 in his eyes.
At a diner, mild-mannered magician Bertie Vaughan asks Kitten what she is writing in her notebook. She explains it is a story about the mother she is seeking, whom Kitten dubs the "Phantom Lady". Intrigued, Bertie hires her as his assistant, turning her life story into a hypnosis act. One day, Bertie tries to kiss Kitten, and she explains that she is transgender, something he already knew. Soon, Charlie finds Bertie's show and takes Kitten away.
While dancing with an English soldier at a nightclub, Kitten is injured when the club is bombed by the IRA. After the police discover that Kitten is transgender and Irish, she is arrested on suspicion of terrorism. At the police station, Wallis beats her up while Routledge urges her to make a statement; Kitten fabricates a story about how she infiltrated a terrorist cell, dressed in black leather and armed with a Chanel spray bottle. Realising she is innocent, the police release her a week later.
Kitten is again forced to turn to prostitution until Wallis sympathetically brings her to a peep show, where she dons a blonde wig.

documents.title: The Departed
documents.tagline: Lies. Betrayal. Sacrifice. How far will you take it?
documents.overview: To take down South Boston's Irish Mafia, the police send in one of their own to infiltrate the underworld, not realizing the syndicate has done likewise. While an undercover cop curries favor with the mob kingpin, a career criminal rises through the police ranks. But both sides soon discover there's a mole among them.
documents.plot:
Colin Sullivan, first introduced to Boston Irish mob boss Frank Costello in the 1980s, has been groomed for years as Costello's spy inside the Massachusetts State Police (MSP). Sullivan is assigned to the Special Investigation Unit, where Captain Queenan and Sergeant Dignam assign another police academy recruit, Billy Costigan, to infiltrate Costello's organization.
Costigan, serving a prison term as cover, draws Costello's attention by committing several crimes and is recruited into Costello's gang. Costigan's mental health declines from increasing involvement in Costello's violent criminal activities, but Queenan and Dignam convince him to remain undercover. Sullivan begins dating police psychiatrist Madolyn Madden, who becomes Costigan's court-ordered therapist.
Costigan notifies the MSP that Costello will be selling stolen microprocessors to Chinese mobsters. When Sullivan helps thwart the attempted sting operation, Costello and the MSP realize they've been compromised. Costigan and Sullivan are each tasked to find the opposing mole. Costigan and Queenan learn that Costello is a protected FBI informant. Costigan begins an affair with Madden.
Costigan follows Costello and sees him pass Sullivan information on his crew. Costigan is unable to identify Sullivan, who realizes he is being followed and mistakenly stabs a passerby before fleeing. Lying to his fellow officers to have Queenan followed, Sullivan realizes Queenan is meeting with his mole and informs Costello's gang.
Costigan, fearing discovery as the mole, meets with Queenan to abort the operation. Queenan helps Costigan escape, but Costello's men arrive and throw Queenan from the building to his death. Fatally wounded in the ensuing firefight with police, Costello's henchman Timothy Delahunt tells Costigan that he knows he's the mole before dying.
Following Queenan's murder, Dignam is suspended after confronting Sullivan about cooperating with the FBI. A news report identifies Delahunt as a Boston Police Department undercover officer, but Costello suspects it's a ruse to protect the real mole. Sullivan directs the MSP to tail Costello, resulting in a gunfight that kills most of Costello's crew. Sullivan confronts a wounded Costello, who admits to being an informant before Sullivan kills him.
His assignment finished, Costigan reveals himself to Sullivan but recognizes Costello's envelope on his desk and deduces that Sullivan is Costello's mole. Costigan flees, and Sullivan realizes he has discovered the truth. Sullivan deletes Costigan's police records. Costigan leaves an envelope of evidence with Madden, who finds a recording of Sullivan's incriminating conversations with Costello.
Meeting Sullivan on the rooftop where Queenan was killed, Costigan arrests him. Trooper Brown, Costigan's police academy classmate, arrives as Costigan holds Sullivan at gunpoint, declaring he has evidence tying Sullivan to Costello.

documents.title: Perfume: The Story of a Murderer
documents.original_title: Perfume: The Story of a Murderer
documents.tagline: Based on the best-selling novel
documents.overview: Jean-Baptiste Grenouille, born in the stench of 18th century Paris, develops a superior olfactory sense, which he uses to create the world's finest perfumes. However, his work takes a dark turn as he tries to preserve scents in the search for the ultimate perfume.
documents.plot:
Perfume: The Story of a Murderer is a 2006 period psychological thriller film directed by Tom Tykwer, who wrote the screenplay with Andrew Birkin and Bernd Eichinger, based on Patrick Süskind's 1985 novel. Set in 18th-century France, it stars Ben Whishaw as Jean-Baptiste Grenouille, a man with an extraordinary sense of smell whose search for the perfect scent turns murderous, alongside Alan Rickman, Rachel Hurd-Wood and Dustin Hoffman.

The story unfolds in flashback from Grenouille's sentencing before a furious mob. Born amid the stalls of a Paris fish market and abandoned by his mother, who is hanged for it, he grows up in an orphanage and later works for a tanner. On a delivery into the city he becomes entranced by the scent of a young plum seller and, trying to keep her quiet, accidentally smothers her; her fading aroma haunts him. He then astonishes the declining perfumer Giuseppe Baldini with his ability to create fragrances, revives his business, and learns distillation, but discovers it cannot capture the scent of people. Baldini directs him to Grasse, where other methods are practiced. On the way Grenouille retreats to a cave and realizes that he himself has no scent at all.

In Grasse he fixes on Laure Richis, the daughter of the wealthy Antoine Richis, as the essential final note of a supreme perfume. After learning enfleurage and experimenting on murder victims, he kills a series of young women, preserving their scents while their bodies spread terror through the town. Richis flees with Laure, but Grenouille tracks her to an inn, murders her and completes his perfume before soldiers seize him. At his execution he wears the fragrance, and the crowd, overwhelmed, proclaims him innocent and falls into an orgy; even Richis embraces him. Free but realizing the perfume cannot make him love or be loved, Grenouille returns to his Paris birthplace, pours the rest over himself, and is consumed by the crowd it draws.

Eichinger acquired the rights in 2000 after Süskind long refused to sell, and the film was shot in Spain, Germany and France on a budget of about €50 million. It topped the German box office for three weeks after opening there in September 2006 and grossed about $135 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 59% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 56; critics admired its visual richness while finding its antihero impossible to sympathize with.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union

documents.title: Once Upon a Time in Mexico
documents.original_title: Once Upon a Time in Mexico
documents.tagline: The Time Has Come.
documents.overview: Hitman "El Mariachi" becomes involved in international espionage involving a psychotic CIA agent and a corrupt Mexican general.
documents.plot:
Once Upon a Time in Mexico is a 2003 American crime drama film directed by Robert Rodriguez, written by Robert Rodriguez and Shiny Rodriguez, and starring Antonio Banderas, Johnny Depp, and Salma Hayek.

The film takes place after the events of El Mariachi (1992) and Desperado (1995), and serves as a sequel to both films. The story follows El Mariachi (Antonio Banderas), a Mexican musician who becomes embroiled in a violent struggle between rival cartels, led by the ruthless Don Carlos (Javier Bardem).

The film begins with El Mariachi performing at a bar in Mexico City, where he is mistaken for a famous singer. He soon finds himself caught up in a complex web of violence and deception as he tries to uncover the truth about his past and the identity of the mysterious woman who has been following him.

As El Mariachi delves deeper into the world of organized crime, he becomes embroiled in a cat-and-mouse game with Don Carlos, who will stop at nothing to eliminate him. Along the way, he meets a beautiful woman named Carolina (Salma Hayek), who is being pursued by Don Carlos' henchmen.

The plot thickens as El Mariachi discovers that Carolina is actually the daughter of Don Carlos, and that she has been trying to escape her father's clutches. As the stakes grow higher, El Mariachi finds himself in a desperate bid for survival, using his wits and his musical talents to outsmart his enemies.

Meanwhile, Johnny Depp plays Jack Buechner, an American hitman who is hired by Don Carlos to eliminate El Mariachi. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jack's true loyalties lie with Carolina, and he finds himself torn between his duty to Don Carlos and his growing feelings for the beautiful woman.

As the film hurtles towards its climax, El Mariachi and Jack engage in a series of intense battles, using everything from guns to musical instruments to try and outmaneuver each other. In the end, it is up to El Mariachi to use all his cunning and resourcefulness to defeat Don Carlos and bring peace to the troubled region.

Throughout the film, Robert Rodriguez pays homage to classic Westerns and Mexican cinema, incorporating a range of clever references and Easter eggs into the narrative. The result is a thrilling and entertaining ride that combines action, drama, and music in a way that is both unique and captivating.

Overall, Once Upon a Time in Mexico is a gripping and stylish film that showcases the talents of its cast and crew. With its intricate plot, memorable characters, and stunning visuals, it is a must-see for fans of Robert Rodriguez and anyone who loves a good action movie.

documents.title: 25th Hour
documents.tagline: Can you change your whole life in one day?
documents.overview: In New York City in the days following the events of 9/11, Monty Brogan is a convicted drug dealer about to start a seven-year prison sentence, and his final hours of freedom are devoted to hanging out with his closest buddies and trying to prepare his girlfriend for his extended absence.
documents.plot: On the eve of a seven-year prison sentence, a New York drug dealer spends his final day of freedom confronting his past, his relationships, and the choices that led to his downfall in a city still reeling from 9/11.

documents.title: The Devil's Backbone
documents.tagline: What is a ghost?
documents.overview: Spain, 1939. In the last days of the Spanish Civil War, the young Carlos arrives at the Santa Lucía orphanage, where he will make friends and enemies as he follows the quiet footsteps of a mysterious presence eager for revenge.
documents.plot:
The Devil's Backbone is a 2001 Spanish horror film directed by Guillermo del Toro, produced by El Deseo, and written by Guillermo del Toro and David Benioff. The film is set during the Spanish Civil War (1936-1939) and tells the story of a young boy named Carlos, who is sent to an orphanage called San Miguel de Allende.

The story begins with Carlos, a 10-year-old boy, being forced to leave his home in Madrid due to the war. He is sent to the orphanage, where he meets a mysterious and ghostly presence that seems to be connected to the death of a fellow student, Santi. As Carlos tries to adjust to his new life at the orphanage, he begins to experience strange occurrences, including finding Santi's belongings in different parts of the building.

Carlos soon discovers that the orphanage is haunted by the ghost of Santi, who died under mysterious circumstances. The ghost is believed to be a manifestation of the guilt and trauma experienced by the orphanage's caretaker, Captain Cánovas, who was responsible for Santi's death. As Carlos delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a dark secret about the orphanage's past and the true identity of the ghost.

Throughout the film, Carlos forms a close bond with his friend Jacinta, an older girl who is also living at the orphanage. Together, they try to uncover the truth behind Santi's death and the haunting of the orphanage. Along the way, they encounter various characters, including Captain Cánovas, who becomes increasingly unhinged as the story unfolds.

As the story progresses, Carlos learns that Santi was killed by Captain Cánovas in a fit of rage after discovering that he had been hiding a Jewish girl, Jacinta's sister, at the orphanage. The ghostly presence is revealed to be Santi's spirit, who is trapped between the world of the living and the dead.

In the climax of the film, Carlos confronts Captain Cánovas, who has become increasingly unhinged due to his guilt and paranoia. In a dramatic confrontation, Carlos exposes the truth about Santi's death and the haunting of the orphanage. The ghostly presence is finally laid to rest, and Carlos is able to find closure and move on from his experiences.

The Devil's Backbone is a haunting and atmospheric film that explores themes of trauma, guilt, and redemption. The film features stunning visuals and a powerful performance from Fernando Tielve as Carlos. The film's use of practical effects and set design creates a sense of realism and immersion, drawing the viewer into the world of the orphanage.

Overall, The Devil's Backbone is a masterful horror film that tells a haunting and atmospheric story about trauma, guilt, and redemption.

documents.title: The Contract
documents.tagline: Every killer meets his equal.
documents.overview: Attempting to recover from a recent family trauma by escaping into the woods for a peaceful hiking trip, an ex-lawman and his young son stumble across a dangerous contract killer.
documents.plot:
The Contract is a German-American action thriller of 2006 directed by Bruce Beresford and written by the television writer Stephen Katz and John Darrouzet. Morgan Freeman stars as the professional assassin Frank Carden and John Cusack as Ray Keene, a teacher who becomes entangled in Carden's latest job during a camping trip with his son. Jamie Anderson, Alice Krige, Megan Dodds and Corey Johnson co-star.

Carden has been hired to kill Lydell Hammond Sr., a reclusive billionaire and outspoken opponent of stem cell research, but his plan collapses when he is hurt in a car crash. Hospital staff find his gun, and federal marshals come for him. Meanwhile Ray, a widower, ex-cop and awkward gym teacher, takes Chris on a wilderness hike to reconnect after catching him smoking marijuana. In the same forest, Carden's men ambush the marshals' convoy; the last survivor, before he dies, asks Ray to deliver the prisoner to the authorities.

Ray and Chris set out to march Carden out of the wilderness, pursued by his crew of highly trained former soldiers. The chase draws in a couple, Sandra and Lochlan, and Lochlan is killed. In a tense standoff at a cabin, Ray agrees to release Carden, but when one of the gunmen strikes Chris, Ray kills him and Sandra shoots another. Local police rescue Ray and Sandra, but Carden escapes, taking Chris as a hostage. Miles then orders Davis, Carden's newest recruit, to kill Carden and the boy and pin the blame on Carden, and to eliminate Ray too in case he knows anything.

Back home, Ray sees a news report describing Carden as someone who removes obstacles to progress, which helps him deduce the target. He goes to the funeral of Hammond's son to intercept Carden and unwittingly saves him from Davis, whom Carden kills with his own sniper rifle. The fight costs Carden his chance at Hammond, and he hands Ray the keys to the hotel room where Chris is being held before vanishing. In Washington, D.C., Carden confronts Miles, letting her know he is aware she ordered his death and warning her to leave Ray's family alone. Two weeks later, Ray is seeing Sandra, and during a barbecue a radio bulletin reports that Hammond has died in a boating accident; Ray realizes that Carden has completed his contract.

The film was shot almost entirely in Bulgaria, with the headquarters of DSK Bank among its main sets and scenes filmed on the Vitosha mountain. Despite its cast, it went direct to video in the United States and Europe, and reviews were negative.

documents.title: The Virgin Suicides
documents.tagline: Beautiful, mysterious, haunting, invariably fatal. Just like life.
documents.overview: A group of male friends become obsessed with five mysterious sisters who are sheltered by their strict, religious parents.
documents.plot: A group of male friends become obsessed with five mysterious sisters who are sheltered by their strict, religious parents.

documents.title: Blood: The Last Vampire
documents.tagline: Where evil grows, she preys.
documents.overview: On the surface, Saya is a stunning 16-year-old, but that youthful exterior hides the tormented soul of a 400-year-old "halfling". Born to a human father and a vampire mother, she has for centuries been a loner obsessed with using her samurai skills to rid the world of vampires, all the while knowing that she herself can survive only on blood like those she hunts.
documents.plot:
In 1970s Tokyo, Saya is a 400-year-old half human-half vampire who hunts vampires. Raised by a man named Kato, she works loosely with an organisation known as "The Council", a secret society that has been hunting vampires for centuries. Saya's motivation goes beyond duty; she wants revenge: Onigen, the oldest of the vampires, murdered her father. For her next mission, she goes undercover as a student at Kanto High School on an American air base near Fussa.
When she is introduced in her class, Saya's appearance quickly attracts the negative attention of a female classmate, Sharon. The daughter of the base's general, Alice McKee, is also bothered with the attention. At her school, she finds herself being mocked. Alice is asked by her Kendo instructor Powell to stay for the Kendo practice due to her poor performance. As soon as the teacher leaves, she finds herself at the mercy of Sharon and her sidekick friend who wield sharp bladed katanas to taunt and torment her. Saya shows up just in time to stop Sharon from slashing Alice's throat. Despite Saya's effort to disguise her activity, Alice sees Sharon and her friend being butchered. However it is soon revealed that Sharon and her friend are vampires in disguise.
Because "The Council" cleans up the bodies of the demons, Alice's father does not believe her story. Determined to make her own investigation, Alice goes to the bar where her Kendo instructor usually hangs out. To her horror her instructor, as well as the rest of the people in the bar, turn out to be vampires. Once again Saya comes to her rescue and has to fight off hordes of vampires surrounding them.
General McKee investigates "The Council", who disguise themselves as CIA. Alice arrives just in time to witness her father's death. Her dying father gives her Saya's address. With nowhere else to go, Alice decides to seek Saya's help. Fortunately Saya has never sworn loyalty to "The Council" and protects Alice instead. The two of them flee the area and go off to the mountains to find and slay Onigen.
In their pursuit, Alice and Saya are run off the side of the road by an attacking demon and they fall into a ravine. When Alice and Saya awaken they are in Ancient Japan where Saya was raised. Onigen appears, reveals her true identity as Saya's mother, and fights Saya. Saya slays Onigen. Alice, who is injured during the fighting, wakes up to find herself at the wreckage of the truck and being carried into an ambulance. Later she is interviewed about the events surrounding her father's death, but her interviewer does not believe her story about the vampires or the Council. When asked about where Saya is, Alice answers that she is "searching for a way back from the other side of the looking glass".
production_companies: Beijing Happy Pictures Cultural Communications Co.

documents.title: Superman Returns
documents.tagline: You’ll Believe A Man Can Fly Again!
documents.overview: Superman returns to discover his 5-year absence has allowed Lex Luthor to walk free, and that those he was closest to felt abandoned and have moved on. Luthor plots his ultimate revenge that could see millions killed and change the face of the planet forever, as well as ridding himself of the Man of Steel.
documents.plot:
Superman Returns is a 2006 superhero film directed by Bryan Singer and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie is a sequel to the classic Superman films from the 1970s and 1980s, specifically Superman (1978) and Superman II (1980).

The story begins with Superman (Brandon Routh), who has been living on Earth for about five years, trying to live a normal life as Clark Kent. However, his secret identity is threatened when Lois Lane (Kate Bosworth), the Daily Planet's top reporter, starts to investigate a series of mysterious events in Metropolis.

Meanwhile, Lex Luthor (Kevin Spacey) returns from the dead, having been presumed dead after Superman defeated him in their previous battle. Lex has created an army of robotic duplicates of himself, known as the "Super-Soldiers," which he plans to use to take over the world.

As Superman tries to stop Lex's plan, he also has to deal with his feelings for Lois and his desire to reconnect with her. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that Lois is now working at a rival newspaper, the Daily Planet's competitor, the New York Daily.

The plot thickens when it is revealed that Lex's plan involves using the Super-Soldiers to destroy Metropolis and then blaming Superman for the destruction. The government, led by President Nathan Hardy (James Marsden), is skeptical of Superman's intentions and wants him to be held accountable for the damage caused by the Super-Soldiers.

As the story unfolds, Superman must confront his own doubts and fears about his role as a hero and his place in the world. He also has to face off against Lex, who reveals that he has been working with General Zod (Marlon Brando), a Kryptonian villain who was thought to be dead.

In the climactic final battle, Superman faces off against both Lex and General Zod, who is revealed to have been manipulating events from behind the scenes. With the help of Lois and his friends, including Perry White (Frank Langella) and Jimmy Olsen (Samuel L. Jackson), Superman is able to defeat both villains and save Metropolis.

In the end, Superman and Lois share a romantic moment, and he finally finds a sense of belonging on Earth. The movie ends with Superman flying off into the sky, ready to face new challenges as the Man of Steel.

Overall, Superman Returns is a nostalgic and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, duty, and the complexities of being a hero. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a beloved entry in the Superman franchise.

documents.title: Hellboy
documents.tagline: From the dark side to our side.
documents.overview: In the final days of World War II, the Nazis attempt to use black magic to aid their dying cause. The Allies raid the camp where the ceremony is taking place, but not before they summon a baby demon who is rescued by Allied forces and dubbed "Hellboy". Sixty years later, Hellboy serves the cause of good rather than evil as an agent in the Bureau of Paranormal Research & Defense, along with Abe Sapien - a merman with psychic powers, and Liz Sherman - a woman with pyrokinesis, protecting America against dark forces.
documents.plot:
Hellboy is a 2004 American superhero film directed by Guillermo del Toro, based on the Dark Horse Comics series of the same name created by Mike Mignola. The movie follows the story of Hellboy, a demon who is raised by humans and becomes a member of a secret organization known as BPRDD (Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense).

The film begins with a dramatic opening sequence showing the destruction of Nazi Germany during World War II. We see a young boy, Ben Daimio (Lance Henriksen), being rescued from a burning building by a mysterious figure who turns out to be Hellboy (Ron Perlman). The boy is taken in by Professor Trevor "Broom" Bruttenholm (John Hurt) and his team at the BPRDD.

As Hellboy grows up, he struggles with his demonic nature and his desire to fit in with human society. He becomes a skilled fighter and uses his powers to protect humanity from supernatural threats. However, Hellboy's past eventually catches up with him, and he is forced to confront his own identity and the evil forces that seek to destroy him.

The main antagonist of the film is Grigori Rasputin (Cradle Will Rock's John Hurt), a powerful demon who was once a human but has since become a servant of the dark gods. Rasputin seeks to bring about the apocalypse by summoning the ancient evil known as the Blood Queen, who will grant him immense power and control over the world.

As Hellboy delves deeper into the mystery of Rasputin's plans, he must also navigate his complicated relationships with his human friends and allies, including Liz Sherman (Selma Blair), a pyrokinetic woman who becomes his love interest. Meanwhile, the villainous Nazi scientist Dr. Wernher von Croy (Cradle Will Rock's Peter Stormare) seeks to exploit Rasputin's powers for his own gain.

The film builds towards an epic showdown between Hellboy and Rasputin, with the fate of humanity hanging in the balance. Along the way, Hellboy must confront his own demons and learn to accept his true nature as a demon. In the end, he emerges victorious, but not without scars and a newfound understanding of himself.

Throughout the film, del Toro's signature visual style and sense of wonder bring the world of Hellboy to life, blending horror, fantasy, and action elements in a way that is both thrilling and emotionally resonant. The cast delivers strong performances, with Perlman bringing depth and nuance to the titular character.

Overall, Hellboy (2004) is a visually stunning and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, acceptance, and the struggle between good and evil. While it received mixed reviews at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic and a beloved entry in the superhero genre.

documents.title: The Illusionist
documents.tagline: Nothing is what it seems
documents.overview: With his eye on a lovely aristocrat, a gifted illusionist named Eisenheim uses his powers to win her away from her betrothed, a crown prince. But Eisenheim's scheme creates tumult within the monarchy and ignites the suspicion of a dogged inspector.
documents.plot:
The Illusionist is a 2006 mystery drama film directed by Neil Burger, produced by Michael London Productions, and written by Jeremy Leven. The movie stars Edward Norton as Eisenheim, a talented illusionist who becomes embroiled in a murder mystery.

Beginning:
The film opens with Eisenheim (Edward Norton) performing his magic show in Vienna, Austria, where he is a celebrated illusionist. He meets Sophie (Jessica Biel), the daughter of a wealthy and influential man, Baron Wesenfeld (Paul Giamatti). The two fall deeply in love, but their social differences make their relationship impossible.

Plot Development:
When Sophie's father dies under mysterious circumstances, Eisenheim becomes the prime suspect. As he tries to clear his name, he discovers that Sophie is being blackmailed by a man named Duke Leopold (Rufus Sewell), who has been using her as leverage to get to her father's fortune.

Eisenheim uses his skills as an illusionist to gather clues and uncover the truth behind Sophie's father's death. Along the way, he meets Tanne (Paul Anderson), a young man who becomes his apprentice and helps him in his investigation.

As Eisenheim delves deeper into the mystery, he realizes that Duke Leopold is not just any ordinary blackmailer, but a master manipulator with a dark past. The more Eisenheim learns about Duke Leopold's true identity, the more he becomes convinced that Sophie's father was murdered to cover up a much larger conspiracy.

Ending:
In the end, Eisenheim uses his illusions to expose Duke Leopold's true identity and bring him to justice. However, in doing so, he also puts himself in danger, as Duke Leopold is willing to do whatever it takes to keep his secrets safe.

The film ends with Eisenheim and Sophie reunited, but not without scars from their ordeal. The final shot of the movie shows Eisenheim performing one last illusion for Sophie, a symbol of their love and the power of magic to bring people together.

Overall, The Illusionist is a complex and engaging mystery that explores themes of love, deception, and the power of the human spirit. With its intricate plot and memorable performances, it's no wonder this film has become a modern classic.

documents.title: Miss Congeniality
documents.tagline: Never Mess With An Agent In A Dress.
documents.overview: When the local FBI office receives a letter from a terrorist known only as 'The Citizen', it's quickly determined that he's planning his next act at the Miss America beauty pageant. Because tough-as-nails Gracie Hart is the only female Agent at the office, she's chosen to go undercover as the contestant from New Jersey.
documents.plot:
In 1982, 10-year-old Gracie Hart breaks up a school fight between two boys, one of whom is a bully and the other, her crush. The boy she likes feels humiliated, as he was saved by a girl and he rudely rejects her, so she punches him and calls him a wimp.
18 years later, 28-year-old Gracie is a tough but uncouth special agent for the FBI. During a sting against Russian mobsters, she ignores protocol to save a mob boss who appears to be choking, causing one of her fellow FBI agents to be shot. As a result of this, she is demoted to a desk job.
Soon, the agency receives news of a bomb threat from notorious domestic terrorist "the Citizen", alluding to an act of terrorism at the upcoming Miss United States beauty pageant in San Antonio, Texas. Gracie's partner, Eric Matthews, is put in charge of the mission and he relies on her suggestions, only to take the credit himself.
One of Gracie's ideas is to plant an agent undercover at the event which is agreed upon. When all potential candidates are deemed unsuitable, Eric suggests that Gracie takes the role, replacing Miss New Jersey, who was to be disqualified for acting in a pornographic film.
Beauty pageant coach Victor Melling teaches Gracie how to dress, walk and behave in a conventionally ladylike manner. Although she is initially appalled, she comes to appreciate Victor's thoroughness, and she enters the pageant as "Gracie Lou Freebush", representing New Jersey. She soon becomes friends with awkward and unconfident Cheryl Frasier, Miss Rhode Island. As the competition begins, she impresses the judges during the talent competition with her glass harp skills.
Several suspects are identified who could be "the Citizen", including the current competition director and former pageant winner Kathy Morningside; her assistant Frank Tobin; veteran MC Stan Fields; and even Cheryl, who has a history of involvement with an animal rights activist group.
Gracie convinces Cheryl and the other contestants to go out one night and drink, using the chance to pry into Cheryl's past. She learns however, that Kathy's past as a pageant contestant is suspicious, including the fact that the year she won, the original winner came down with food poisoning.
Gracie deduces that Kathy is a "Citizen" copycat, but when she reports this to Eric and the team, she learns that "the Citizen" has been arrested on an unrelated charge. As there is no perceived threat, their superior, Harry McDonald, pulls the mission. Gracie insists that something isn't right, but Eric and the team still leave.
While on their way home, Victor mentions to Eric that Frank is actually Kathy's son, a fact they had tried to hide from the FBI because of his criminal record. Eric returns to Texas to help continue the investigation, against FBI orders.
In the final round of the pageant, Gracie is stunned when she is named runner-up. Cheryl is named Miss United States, but as she goes to accept the tiara, Gracie realizes that the bomb is in the crown.

documents.title: Curse of the Golden Flower
documents.tagline: Unspeakable secrets are hidden within the Forbidden City.
documents.overview: During China's Tang dynasty the emperor has taken the princess of a neighboring province as his wife. She has borne him two sons and raised his eldest. Now his control over his dominion is complete, including the royal family itself.
documents.plot:
Curse of the Golden Flower is a 2006 Chinese epic wuxia drama film written and directed by Zhang Yimou, based on Cao Yu's 1934 play Thunderstorm but set in imperial China. Chow Yun-fat stars as Emperor Ping and Gong Li as Empress Phoenix, with Jay Chou as their son Prince Jai, Liu Ye as Crown Prince Wan, Qin Junjie as Prince Yu, Ni Dahong as the Imperial Physician Jiang and Li Man as his daughter Jiang Chan. Costing US$45 million, it was then the most expensive Chinese film.

On the eve of the Double Ninth Festival, the Emperor and his second son, Prince Jai, return from a military campaign to celebrate with the family. The Empress has been having an affair with Crown Prince Wan, the Emperor's son by a previous wife, while Wan loves Jiang Chan and hopes to run away with her. Jai notices that his mother's health is failing and is puzzled by her sudden interest in chrysanthemums. She reveals that the Emperor has been poisoning her tea for some time and that she is planning a rebellion, which Jai agrees to lead. A mysterious woman the Empress hires to identify the poison is caught by Wan and brought to the Emperor; she is Jiang Shi, the physician's wife, once imprisoned by the Emperor and believed dead. When Wan learns from Jiang Chan that the Empress has had 10,000 scarves made bearing golden flower emblems, he confronts her and, anguished by her plot, tries to kill himself but survives. After the Emperor sends the physician to a new post as governor, assassins kill him on the road, and when Jiang Shi and her daughter return to confront him, the Empress reveals that Jiang Shi was the Emperor's first wife and Wan's mother, making Wan and Jiang Chan half-siblings. Both women are then murdered. The youngest prince, Yu, then kills Wan and demands the throne, and the Emperor beats him to death. Jai leads 10,000 soldiers bearing golden flower emblems into the palace, only to see them massacred by the Emperor's reserve army, and servants erase every trace of the battle before the midnight festival. Offered a pardon if he helps poison his mother, Jai kills himself instead, and the Empress hurls away the poisoned tea, which eats into the golden flower carved in the table.

China's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, it received an Oscar nomination for costume design and won four Hong Kong Film Awards, including Best Actress for Gong Li. It grossed over $78 million worldwide and holds a 65% Rotten Tomatoes rating.
production_companies: Beijing New Picture Film Co. Ltd.

documents.title: The Last King of Scotland
documents.tagline: Charming. Magnetic. Murderous.
documents.overview: Young Scottish doctor, Nicholas Garrigan decides it's time for an adventure after he finishes his formal education, so he decides to try his luck in Uganda, and arrives during the downfall of President Obote. General Idi Amin comes to power and asks Garrigan to become his personal doctor.
documents.plot: Young Scottish doctor, Nicholas Garrigan decides it's time for an adventure after he finishes his formal education, so he decides to try his luck in Uganda, and arrives during the downfall of President Obote. General Idi Amin comes to power and asks Garrigan to become his personal doctor.

documents.title: Pathfinder
documents.tagline: Two Worlds, One War. The Ultimate Battle Begins.
documents.overview: A Viking boy is left behind after his clan battles a Native American tribe. Raised within the tribe, he ultimately becomes their savior in a fight against the Norsemen.
documents.plot: A Viking boy is left behind after his clan battles a Native American tribe. Raised within the tribe, he ultimately becomes their savior in a fight against the Norsemen.

documents.title: Spy Game
documents.tagline: It's not how you play the game. It's how the game plays you.
documents.overview: On the day of his retirement, a veteran CIA agent learns that his former protégé has been arrested in China, is sentenced to die the next morning in Beijing, and that the CIA is considering letting that happen to avoid an international scandal.
documents.plot:
In 1991, the United States and China are close to a major trade agreement, with the President due to visit China to seal the deal. The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) learns that its asset Tom Bishop has been arrested at a People's Liberation Army prison in Suzhou and will be executed in 24 hours unless the U.S. government claims him and bargains for his release. Bishop's actions, unsanctioned by the CIA, risk jeopardizing the agreement. A group of CIA executives summons Nathan Muir, a veteran case officer and Bishop's mentor, who plans to retire from the Agency at the end of the day. While purportedly interviewing Muir to learn his history with Bishop, the executives seek a pretext for not intervening on Bishop's imprisonment. Unknown to them, Muir was tipped off about Bishop's capture by fellow CIA veteran Harry Duncan, the Hong Kong Station Chief.
Muir leaks the story to CNN through an MI6 contact, Digby 'Digger' Gibson in Hong Kong, believing that public pressure would force American intervention. They are stalled briefly before a phone call to the FCC from Deputy Director for Operations Charles Harker results in CNN retracting the story as a hoax. Through a series of flashbacks, it is revealed that Muir met Bishop in 1975 when Bishop was a United States Marine Corps Scout Sniper during the Vietnam War. Muir gave Bishop a mission to eliminate a high-ranking Laotian Army officer. Bishop and his spotter, Tran, assassinate the target despite being compromised, and Bishop downs a pursuing enemy attack helicopter. Bishop escorts the now wounded Tran to safety, impressing Muir. In 1976, Muir recruited Bishop as a CIA asset in West Berlin, where Bishop was tasked with procuring assets in East Germany. Then he discusses Bishop's spy work in Beirut in 1985, during the War of the Camps, which was their last mission together.
Bishop is troubled by Muir's conviction that civilian "assets" who endangered a mission should be sacrificed to preserve the "greater good." After Bishop attempts to countermand Muir during a mission to save the life of an asset, Muir emphasizes that he will not tolerate dissent, and would not rescue Bishop if he was captured going "off the reservation". During a mission in Lebanon, Bishop, posing as a photojournalist, meets relief worker Elizabeth Hadley. While using her to connect with an asset for the mission, they become romantically involved. Muir distrusts Hadley and reveals to Bishop that she was exiled from the United Kingdom. Hadley later confesses to Bishop that she was involved in the bombing of a Chinese building in Britain, which was supposed to be empty but contained Chinese nationals. Bishop reveals to Hadley his true identity. Muir elects again to sacrifice a civilian asset for the sake of their mission, and Bishop cuts professional ties with Muir. Muir, fearing that Hadley could threaten the Agency and potentially Bishop, makes a deal with the Chinese, exchanging Hadley in return for an arrested U.S. diplomat.

documents.title: Changing Lanes
documents.tagline: One wrong turn deserves another.
documents.overview: A rush-hour fender-bender on New York City's crowded FDR Drive, under most circumstances, wouldn't set off a chain reaction that could decimate two people's lives. But on this day, at this time, a minor collision will turn two complete strangers into vicious adversaries. Their means of destroying each other might be different, but their goals, ultimately, will be the same: Each will systematically try to dismantle the other's life in a reckless effort to reclaim something he has lost.
documents.plot:
Changing Lanes is a 2002 American legal thriller directed by Roger Michell, starring Ben Affleck as a young Wall Street lawyer and Samuel L. Jackson as an insurance salesman whose lives collide after a car accident. Toni Collette, Sydney Pollack, William Hurt, Amanda Peet and Kim Staunton co-star. Paramount Pictures released it in North America on April 12, 2002, and it earned nearly 95 million dollars worldwide on a 45 million dollar budget.

On a busy morning in New York, two men are racing to court. Doyle Gipson, a recovering alcoholic, is heading to a custody hearing where he hopes to keep his estranged wife from moving to Oregon with their sons, having arranged to buy a house nearby for the family. Gavin Banek, an ambitious lawyer at a prestigious firm, is rushing to file a document proving that a dead philanthropist signed control of his foundation over to the firm. On the FDR Drive, Banek's car collides with Gipson's. Instead of exchanging insurance details, Banek offers a blank cheque and drives off, leaving Gipson stranded with the words "better luck next time."

Gipson arrives late to find that the judge has ruled against him in his absence, granting his wife sole custody. Banek reaches court only to realise that the crucial file was left behind on the highway, and the judge allows him until the close of business to produce it. Gipson has the file but, bitter at what he has lost, refuses at first to return it.

The feud escalates. Banek pays a shady fixer to wreck Gipson's credit rating, destroying his chances of getting a mortgage, which drives Gipson to the brink of drinking again. In revenge, Gipson loosens the wheel nuts on Banek's car, causing a crash. Banek then calls Gipson's sons' school and claims that their father plans to abduct them, and Gipson is arrested, while his wife vows he will never see the children again. Along the way, Banek discovers that his own firm, including his boss and father-in-law, has been involved in fraud.

Shaken by what they have done, both men step back from their vendetta and apologise to each other. Gipson returns the file, which Banek uses to force his boss to run the firm honestly and to let him represent Gipson without charge. Banek also visits Gipson's wife and asks for five minutes of her time, and the next day Gipson sees his wife and sons smiling at him from across the street. The film was well reviewed, with 77% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Collateral
documents.tagline: It started like any other night.
documents.overview: Cab driver Max picks up a man who offers him $600 to drive him around. But the promise of easy money sours when Max realizes his fare is an assassin.
documents.plot:
Collateral is a 2004 American neo-noir crime thriller film directed by Christopher McQuarrie and written by Brian Helgeland. The movie stars Tom Cruise as Vincent, a hitman, and Jamie Foxx as Max, a taxi driver.

The story begins with Max Durocher (Jamie Foxx), a struggling taxi driver who is trying to make ends meet in Los Angeles. One night, he picks up a mysterious passenger, Vincent (Tom Cruise), who is revealed to be a professional hitman. Despite his initial reservations, Max agrees to drive Vincent around the city for the night.

As they drive through the city, Vincent reveals that he has a job to complete and needs Max's help to get in and out of a location without being detected. Max is initially hesitant but eventually becomes entangled in Vincent's plans. Throughout the night, Max tries to navigate his way through the complex web of Vincent's life, while also trying to protect himself from becoming involved in any potential danger.

As the night progresses, Max learns more about Vincent's profession and the nature of their relationship. He discovers that Vincent is a highly skilled and ruthless hitman who has no qualms about killing people. Despite this, Max finds himself drawn to Vincent's charismatic personality and begins to see him as a person rather than just a killer.

The plot thickens when Max learns that Vincent's target is a wealthy businessman named Juniper (Peter Stormare), who is involved in some shady dealings. As they get closer to their destination, Max realizes that he has become an unwitting participant in Vincent's hitman game.

In the climax of the movie, Max and Vincent engage in a tense standoff with Juniper and his henchmen. Despite being outnumbered, Max uses his wits and resourcefulness to help Vincent take down his targets. In the end, they successfully complete their mission, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

Throughout the movie, there are several themes that emerge, including the nature of morality and the consequences of violence. The film also explores the complex relationship between Max and Vincent, who begin as adversaries but eventually develop a begrudging respect for each other.

Overall, Collateral is a gripping and intense thriller that features strong performances from Tom Cruise and Jamie Foxx. The movie's tense atmosphere and intricate plot make it a compelling watch, even if some viewers may find the subject matter disturbing.

documents.title: 28 Weeks Later
documents.tagline: When days turn to weeks... the horror returns.
documents.overview: The inhabitants of the British Isles have lost their battle against the onslaught of disease, as the deadly rage virus has killed every citizen there. Six months later, a group of Americans dare to set foot on the isles, convinced the danger has come and gone. But it soon becomes all too clear that the scourge continues to live, waiting to pounce on its next victims.
documents.plot:
28 Weeks Later is a 2007 British post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Juan Carlos Fresnadillo and written by Rowan Joffe, Jesús Olmo, and Diego Sanjuán. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2002 film 28 Days Later.

The story takes place six months after the events of the first film. The UK government has established a quarantine zone in London, where a small group of survivors lives under strict military rule. The city remains in a state of lockdown, with a curfew and strict controls on movement.

The movie begins with Don (Robert Carlyle), a survivor who has been living in the quarantine zone, trying to rebuild his life. He is visited by his friend, Jim (Clemence Poesy), who brings news that her sister, Scarlet (Imogen Poots), has gone missing. Scarlet was one of the few people allowed to leave the quarantine zone for a medical experiment.

As Don and Jim search for Scarlet, they discover that she has been infected with the rage virus, which caused the initial outbreak in London. The virus is highly contagious and turns its victims into violent, zombie-like creatures.

The group soon realizes that the virus has mutated, making it even more deadly and aggressive. They also learn that a new strain of the virus has emerged, which can be transmitted through casual contact, rather than just through bites or scratches.

As the situation spirals out of control, Don and Jim must navigate the treacherous landscape of London to find Scarlet and prevent the spread of the virus. Along the way, they encounter other survivors who are struggling to cope with the new reality.

The movie's plot is driven by a sense of urgency and desperation, as the characters try to survive in a world that has been turned upside down. The film's climax features an intense and violent confrontation between Don and Scarlet, which ultimately leads to her downfall.

Throughout the movie, there are themes of grief, loss, and redemption. Don's character is particularly well-developed, as he grapples with the guilt of surviving while others have died. His relationship with Jim adds a human element to the story, and their bond helps to drive the plot forward.

Overall, 28 Weeks Later is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores the consequences of a global pandemic. The movie's use of practical effects and its focus on character development make it a standout in the horror genre.

documents.title: Live Free or Die Hard
documents.tagline: The old school cop is back!
documents.overview: John McClane is back and badder than ever, and this time he's working for Homeland Security. He calls on the services of a young hacker in his bid to stop a ring of Internet terrorists intent on taking control of America's computer infrastructure.
documents.plot:
Live Free or Die Hard is a 2007 American action thriller film directed by Len Wiseman and written by Mark Boal, based on the novel "Nothing Lasts Forever" by Roderick Thorp. The movie stars Bruce Willis as John McClane, a retired New York City police detective who finds himself in the middle of a terrorist plot to destroy the United States.

The story begins with John McClane (Bruce Willis), a divorced and retired cop from New York City, visiting his estranged wife, Lucy (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), in Los Angeles for her birthday. However, their reunion is cut short when a group of terrorists, led by Thomas Gabriel (Timothy Olyphant), infiltrate the city's computer systems and begin to wreak havoc.

Gabriel, a former hacker turned terrorist, has created a sophisticated virus that can destroy any computer system connected to the internet. He plans to use this virus to hold the United States hostage and force the government to meet his demands. The FBI is unable to stop Gabriel, and it becomes clear that he has infiltrated every level of the country's infrastructure.

As McClane tries to reconnect with Lucy, he discovers that she is being held by Gabriel's team, who are using her as leverage to get to him. McClane soon finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with Gabriel's henchmen, who are determined to kill him.

McClane teams up with a young hacker, Matt Farrell (Justin Long), who helps him navigate the complex world of computer viruses and cyber-terrorism. Together, they embark on a mission to stop Gabriel and his team before it's too late.

As the story unfolds, McClane and Farrell find themselves in a series of intense battles against Gabriel's henchmen, from a high-speed car chase through Los Angeles to a showdown at a skyscraper under construction. Along the way, McClane must confront his own personal demons and learn to adapt to a new generation of technology.

In the end, McClane and Farrell successfully stop Gabriel and destroy the virus, saving the country from destruction. However, not before Gabriel reveals that he has one final trick up his sleeve - a plan to use the virus to take control of the entire country's infrastructure.

The movie ends with McClane and Lucy reunited, but not without scars. McClane has come to terms with his past and found a new sense of purpose as a retired cop who can still make a difference in the world. The film concludes on a hopeful note, with McClane looking out over the city, ready for whatever challenges come next.

Overall, Live Free or Die Hard is an action-packed thrill ride that explores the intersection of technology and terrorism. With its breakneck pace and witty banter, the movie delivers non-stop excitement from start to finish.
