documents.title: Revolutionary Road
documents.tagline: How do you break free without breaking apart?
documents.overview: A young couple living in a Connecticut suburb during the mid-1950s struggle to come to terms with their personal problems while trying to raise their two children. Based on a novel by Richard Yates.
documents.plot:
Revolutionary Road is a 2008 romantic drama directed by Sam Mendes and written by Justin Haythe, based on the 1961 novel by Richard Yates. It stars Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet as Frank and April Wheeler, with Michael Shannon, Kathryn Hahn, David Harbour and Kathy Bates in supporting roles. The film reunited DiCaprio, Winslet and Bates, who had previously appeared together in Titanic, and it was scored by Thomas Newman.

In 1947, Frank Wheeler meets April, an aspiring actress, at a party. They marry, Frank takes a sales job at a company called Knox Machines, and when April becomes pregnant the couple move into a house on Revolutionary Road in suburban Connecticut. To their neighbors and friends, including the real estate agent Helen Givings and the couple Milly and Shep Campbell, the Wheelers seem perfect, but their marriage is troubled. April's acting ambitions have come to nothing, and Frank is bored by his job and begins an affair with a secretary.

Hoping to escape the emptiness of suburban life, April proposes that the family move to Paris, where she would work and Frank would be free to discover what he truly wants to do. Frank is won over, and the couple announce their plans, which are met with skepticism by everyone except John Givings, Helen's mentally ill son, who sees through the conformity around them. But when Frank is offered a promotion and April becomes pregnant again, the dream begins to fall apart. Frank decides to stay, April sinks into despair, and the couple's arguments grow increasingly bitter, leading to a tragedy.

The film is a portrait of the stifling conformity of 1950s American suburbia and of a marriage destroyed by disappointment and unfulfilled dreams.

Revolutionary Road was released in December 2008 and grossed more than 79.5 million dollars worldwide. It received generally positive reviews, with praise for the performances of Winslet, DiCaprio and Shannon. Winslet won the Golden Globe for Best Actress, and the film earned three Academy Award nominations, including Best Supporting Actor for Shannon.

documents.title: Shriek If You Know What I Did Last Friday the Thirteenth
documents.original_title: Shriek If You Know What I Did Last Friday the Thirteenth
documents.tagline: No shame. No mercy. No brains.
documents.overview: In this horror parody, a masked serial killer menaces the town of Bulimia Falls with various sharp objects. Attention-seeking television personality Hagitha Utslay is soon on the scene, reporting on the ever-growing body count. Former mall security guard Doughy shows up to protect the teenage population, but he's clearly not much help, allowing the murderer to pick off even more hapless kids as numerous scary movies are referenced.
documents.plot:
Shriek If You Know What I Did Last Friday the Thirteenth is a 2000 American made-for-television parody slasher film directed by John Blanchard. The cast is led by Tiffani-Amber Thiessen, Tom Arnold, Coolio and Majandra Delfino, with Julie Benz, Harley Cross, Simon Rex, Danny Strong and Shirley Jones also appearing. Released only a few months after Scary Movie, the film mocks the wave of self-aware teen horror pictures of the late 1990s, and it follows the outline of Scream especially closely while also lampooning Friday the 13th, Halloween, A Nightmare on Elm Street and I Know What You Did Last Summer.

The film opens with a teenager alone at home being stalked by a masked killer, only for her to die by accident before he can strike, leaving him frustrated. His hockey mask melts after he lights a cigarette and turns into a ghostly screaming face, a joke about how one horror icon gave way to another. The next day Dawson Deery, a new student, arrives at Bulimia Falls High School and falls in with a group of friends that includes the hapless Boner, the jock Slab, the vain Barbara and Martina, a girl Dawson likes but who he suspects may not be interested in boys.

As students start dying around them, the group stays sure that they are safe, failing to notice the chaos unfolding in the background of nearly every scene. They are dogged by Hagitha Utslay, a pushy reporter for a music television news channel who has already written a best-selling pop-up book about the killings and who accuses Dawson of being the murderer. Barbara's brother Doughy, a clumsy security guard who has lost his job at a shopping mall, appoints himself the town's investigator. Soon each friend receives a note revealing that the killer knows their secret: one night, while driving drunk, they hit a deer and dumped it in the sea. The revelation sets up a string of gags parodying the conventions of slasher sequels, from absurd red herrings to a climactic unmasking.

The film premiered on television and was later released on home video. It drew comparisons with Scary Movie, but was produced on a much smaller budget and with a broader, sketch-like approach to its humor, relying heavily on rapid visual jokes and pop-culture references from the turn of the millennium.

documents.title: Scream 2
documents.tagline: Someone has taken their love of sequels one step too far.
documents.overview: Two years after the terrifying events that occurred in Woodsboro, Sidney is now attending Windsor College in Cincinnati, and Gale Weathers' best selling book on Sidney's life has now been made into a major motion picture. When two college students are killed in a theatre while watching the new film 'Stab', Sidney knows deep down that history is repeating itself.
documents.plot:
Scream 2 is a 1997 American slasher film directed by Wes Craven and written by Kevin Williamson. The movie takes place one year after the events of the first film, where Sidney Prescott (Neve Campbell) has become a bestselling author due to her book about her experiences with Ghostface.

The story begins with a series of murders taking place at Windsor College, where Sidney is now a professor of English literature. A copycat killer, known as "Ghostface," starts sending threatening messages and committing murders on campus, targeting students and faculty members. The main suspect is Mickey Altieri (Timothy Olyphant), a former student who was obsessed with Sidney in the first film.

As the bodies pile up, Sidney becomes increasingly paranoid and isolated, struggling to cope with her newfound fame and the pressure of being a professor. She also starts to investigate the murders herself, teaming up with her friends Randy Meeks (Jamie Kennedy) and Tatum Riley (Lori Petty).

The plot thickens when it's revealed that the copycat killer is actually a student who was inspired by Sidney's book and the events of the first film. The killer's motive is to recreate the original murders, but with a twist: they're targeting people who were involved in the original film.

As the body count rises, Sidney and her friends must navigate the complex web of relationships and alliances on campus to uncover the identity of the killer. Along the way, they discover that the killer is not just a copycat, but someone who has a personal connection to Sidney's past.

The climax of the movie takes place in a dramatic showdown between Sidney and the killer, which ultimately leads to a surprising twist: the killer is revealed to be Mickey Altieri, who had been manipulating events from behind the scenes. However, it's later revealed that Mickey was not acting alone, but rather was part of a larger conspiracy involving several students who were inspired by Sidney's book.

In the end, Sidney and her friends manage to outsmart the killers and bring them to justice. The movie ends with Sidney reflecting on the events of the past year and the impact they've had on her life, as well as the realization that she must be more careful about how she uses her fame and influence.

Overall, Scream 2 is a clever and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of celebrity culture, media manipulation, and the consequences of violence. The movie's self-aware, meta approach to horror pays off in spades, making it a standout entry in the Scream franchise.

documents.title: Scream 3
documents.tagline: Someone has taken their love of trilogies one step too far.
documents.overview: As bodies begin dropping around the set of ‘Stab 3’ — a movie sequel based on the gruesome Woodsboro killings — Sidney, Gale and Dewey are once again drawn into a game of horror movie mayhem.
documents.plot:
Scream 3 is a 2000 American slasher film directed by Wes Craven and written by Ehren Kruger, Kevin Williamson, and J. Mackye Gruber. The movie takes place three years after the events of Scream (1996) and follows Sidney Prescott (Neve Campbell), who has become a successful author, as she returns to Hollywood to promote her new book.

The film begins with a series of seemingly unrelated murders in Los Angeles, where a group of aspiring actors are being killed by a masked killer. The main character, Roman Bridger (Scott Foley), is the son of a famous actor and a student at Columbia University's film school. As the bodies pile up, Sidney becomes aware that the killings may be connected to her own past and the events of the previous films.

Sidney soon discovers that the murders are linked to a movie studio called Hollywood High, which is being renovated into a new film set. The killer, known as Ghostface, begins to target people associated with the film industry, including actors, directors, and writers. Sidney teams up with her friends, including Deputy Dewey Riley (David Arquette), Randy Meeks (Jamie Kennedy), and Tatum Riley (Rose McGowan), to uncover the identity of the killer.

As the body count rises, Sidney becomes increasingly paranoid and isolated, suspecting that someone close to her may be behind the murders. The group discovers that the killings are not just random acts of violence but are also connected to a deeper conspiracy involving the film industry and Hollywood High.

The plot thickens as Sidney's past is revealed to be more closely tied to the events than she initially thought. The killer, it turns out, is someone who has been manipulating events from behind the scenes, using the murders to exact revenge on the film industry for its perceived hypocrisy and superficiality.

In the climactic final act, Sidney confronts the killer in a thrilling showdown at Hollywood High. In a surprising twist, the identity of the killer is revealed to be Roman Bridger, who had been seeking revenge against his mother's tormentors by targeting those associated with the film industry.

The movie ends with Sidney emerging victorious but shaken by the events that have transpired. The film concludes on a somber note, reflecting on the darker side of Hollywood and the consequences of violence and trauma.

Overall, Scream 3 expands on the franchise's themes of horror, suspense, and social commentary, while maintaining the signature self-aware humor and wit that defines the series.

documents.title: The Kid
documents.tagline: Nobody ever grows up quite like they imagined.
documents.overview: Powerful businessman Russ Duritz is self-absorbed and immersed in his work. But by the magic of the moon, he meets Rusty, a chubby, charming 8-year-old version of himself who can't believe he could turn out so badly – with no life and no dog. With Rusty's help, Russ is able to reconcile the person he used to dream of being with the man he's actually become.
documents.plot:
Days from turning 40, Russ Duritz is a successful but unsympathetic image consultant in Los Angeles and has a strained relationship with his father. Returning home one day he finds a toy plane on his porch and a strange boy indoors, whom he chases through the streets.
After seeing the boy enter a diner, Russ finds no sign of him inside. Thinking he is hallucinating, he visits a psychiatrist, but finds the same boy on his couch eating popcorn and watching cartoons when he returns home. The boy says his name is Rusty and that he was just searching for his toy plane.
Seeing a resemblance, Russ compares memories and birthmarks and realizes Rusty is actually himself as a kid. After questioning Russ, Rusty tells him, "I grow up to be a loser." Rusty dreams of owning a dog named Chester and flying planes, but Russ gave up on those dreams.
Russ's co-worker Amy thinks that Russ and Rusty are father and son and accuses him of being a dead-beat dad. Rusty assures her he is not his son and implores Russ to tell her the truth, but he thinks she'd never believe them. Amy realizes the truth while watching the two argue, as they are nearly identical.
In response to Rusty's questions about how he became Russ, he tells him about his scholarship to UCLA and working for six years to get a master's degree and change himself to who he is. Rusty understands Russ's job as an image consultant to be training people to pretend to be somebody else.
Russ cancels his appointments and spends the day with Rusty, trying to figure out what from the past needs to be fixed to get him back home. Driving through a tunnel, Russ recalls a fight he lost with some bullies who were abusing a three-legged dog. They emerge from the tunnel into Rusty's eighth birthday in 1968.
Russ helps Rusty win the fight and save the dog’s life, but realizes that the fight itself was only the first half of the ordeal. Rusty's loving but terminally ill mother is called to take him home early, where his father angrily berates him for causing his mother more stress, convinced he was trying to kill her faster with the stunt he pulled. Rusty breaks down crying in an attempt to tell his dad that he found the screw he lost, but his father refuses to listen and harshly tells him to stop crying and grow up, making Russ realize why he is the way he is today. Tearfully, Russ assures Rusty that he was not responsible for his mother's death, and that his father's outburst was simply because he was scared about the prospect of raising him alone.
When they return to the present time, they celebrate their birthday at the diner and drink milkshakes, but realize their efforts to change the outcome of the day have failed, as their father's outburst left Rusty emotionally scarred in both cases. When a dog named Chester greets Rusty, they find that his owner is an older version of them who owns planes and has a family with Amy.

documents.title: Scary Movie
documents.tagline: No mercy. No shame. No sequel.
documents.overview: A familiar-looking group of teenagers find themselves being stalked by a more-than-vaguely recognizable masked killer! As the victims begin to pile up and the laughs pile on, none of your favorite scary movies escape the razor-sharp satire of this outrageously funny parody!
documents.plot:
Scary Movie is a horror comedy film released in 2000, directed by Keenen Ivory Wayans and written by Shawn Wayans and Marlon Wayans. The movie is a parody of popular horror films, particularly Scream (1996) and I Know What You Did Last Summer (1997).

The story begins with Cindy Campbell (Anna Faris), a high school student who is dating Bobby (Timothy Stack). On the night of their prom, they are involved in a car accident that kills a man. The next day, Cindy receives a mysterious phone call from an unknown number, warning her to "get out while you still can." Unbeknownst to Cindy, this is a reference to the infamous "Ghostface" killer from Scream.

As Cindy tries to move on with her life, she becomes the target of a series of murders and stalkings. She soon discovers that she has become the focus of a serial killer known as Ghostface (Brendan Sexton III), who is using a similar M.O. to the one in Scream.

Meanwhile, Bobby's friend Ray (Reginald VelJohnson) becomes suspicious of Cindy's involvement with the murders and starts investigating her past. He discovers that she was involved in the car accident and believes that she may be connected to the killings.

As the body count rises, Cindy teams up with Ray to uncover the identity of Ghostface. Along the way, they encounter a series of wacky characters, including a bumbling police officer (James Woods) and a creepy hotel clerk (Matthew Lillard).

Throughout the movie, the Wayans brothers cleverly parody various horror tropes, from the "final girl" trope to the use of jump scares. The film's humor is often irreverent and self-aware, with the characters frequently breaking the fourth wall to address the audience.

In the end, Cindy discovers that Ghostface is actually her boyfriend Bobby, who has been using a mask and a fake identity to cover his tracks. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Bobby was the one responsible for the murders all along, and Cindy must use her wits to outsmart him and escape alive.

Overall, Scary Movie is a hilarious and clever parody of horror movies, with plenty of laughs and surprises along the way. The film's success spawned a series of sequels and spin-offs, cementing its place as a cult classic in the world of horror comedy.

documents.title: Scary Movie 2
documents.tagline: No More Mercy. No More Shame. No More Sequels - Honest! - We Lied.
documents.overview: While the original parodied slasher flicks like Scream, Keenen Ivory Wayans's sequel to Scary Movie takes comedic aim at haunted house movies. A group of students visit a mansion called "Hell House," and murderous high jinks ensue.
documents.plot:
Scary Movie 2 is a horror comedy film released in 2001, directed by Keenen Ivory Wayans and written by Shawn Wayans and Marlon Wayans. The movie is the sequel to the 2000 film Scary Movie and stars Anna Faris, Regina Hall, and James Woods.

The plot of Scary Movie 2 takes place after the events of the first film. Cindy Campbell (Anna Faris) is now a high school student who has survived the previous night's terror. However, she soon discovers that the evil spirits from the first film have returned to wreak havoc on her life once again.

As Cindy navigates her way through high school, she begins to experience strange and terrifying events. She starts to suspect that the house where she lives is haunted by malevolent spirits. The main antagonist of the movie is a group of ghosts who are determined to scare Cindy to death.

The ghostly entities are led by a vengeful spirit named Bessie (Linda Cardellini), who was killed in the 1950s and seeks revenge on Cindy's family for their supposed wrongdoings. The spirits also include a group of teenagers from the 1950s, who were killed in a car accident.

As Cindy tries to survive the night, she enlists the help of her friends, including her boyfriend Bobby (Timothy Stack) and her friend Ray (Shawn Wayans). Together, they try to uncover the source of the haunting and put an end to it.

Throughout the movie, the characters frequently break the fourth wall, addressing the audience directly and commenting on the clichés of horror movies. The film also parodies popular horror films from the 1950s and 1960s, including The Innocents, The Haunting, and Psycho.

As the night wears on, Cindy and her friends discover that the source of the haunting is a group of ghosts who are trapped in the house by a supernatural force. They also learn that Bessie's ghost is seeking revenge on Cindy's family for their supposed wrongdoings.

In the end, Cindy and her friends manage to defeat the ghosts and put an end to the haunting. However, not before they experience some terrifying moments and comedic relief. The movie ends with a humorous twist, as Cindy reflects on the events of the night and comments on how it was all just a big joke.

Overall, Scary Movie 2 is a horror comedy film that spoofs popular horror movies from the past while still delivering plenty of laughs and scares.

documents.title: Veer-Zaara
documents.tagline: A Love Legend
documents.overview: Squadron Leader Veer Pratap Singh, a pilot in the Indian air force, rescues the stranded Zaara, a woman from Pakistan, following a bus accident, and their lives are forever bound.
documents.plot:
The government of Pakistan decides to reopen the cases of former Indian prisoners. Saamiya Siddiqui (Rani Mukerji) fights her first case to repatriate Indian Air Force Squadron Leader Veer Pratap Singh (Shahrukh Khan). Veer Pratap Singh has been imprisoned for 22 years under the alias Rajesh Rathore. Saamiya addresses him by his real name. Veer tells his story.
Veer was a squadron leader in the Indian Air Force. Zaara (Preity Zinta) the daughter of Jahangir Hayaat Khan (Boman Irani), a powerful Pakistani politician, is traveling to Kiratpur Sahib to immerse her nanny's ashes. Zaara's bus crashes and she is rescued by Veer. Having fallen in love with her Veer asks Zaara for a day of her life. Veer takes her to his village and introduces her to his adoptive parents Chaudhary Sumer Singh (Amitabh Bachchan), and mother (Hema Malini). Zaara stays there for Lohri.
At the railway station where Razaa Shirazi (Manoj Bajpayee) has come to fetch Zaara Veer reveals his true feelings to Zaara. Zaara's fiancé. Veer and Zaara part ways.
On the day of her engagement Zaara tells her mother (Kirron Kher) that she too loves Veer but her mother insists Zaara marry Razaa. After her engagement, Zaara begins seeing Veer everywhere. Her friend Shabbo (Divya Dutta) calls up Veer. Veer visits Pakistan. Seeing Zaara embrace Veer in front of her entire family, her father suffers a heart attack. Zaara's mother pleads with Veer to leave Zaara.
Veer relents but is arrested by the police who accuse him of being an agent of India's Research and Analysis Wing. Veer discover that this is a ploy hatched by Razaa. When Razaa threatens to harass Zaara Veer agrees to Raaza's proposal to admit that he is secret agent Rajesh Rathore. On the day of Zara-Raaza's wedding, the bus in which Veer is supposed to be returning to India has an accident.
Having heard the story Saamiya travels to Veer's village. His adoptive parents are dead. She meets Zaara and Shabbo. Upon hearing of the bus accident and assuming Veer is dead Zaara had broken off her marriage and moved here. Saamiya reveals the truth to Zaara. They travel back to Pakistan with evidence that Veer was not a secret agent. Veer wins the case. Veer recites the poem "Main Qaidi No. 786." Saamiya drops Veer and Zaara off at the Wagah border. Veer and Zaara go back to Veer's village.

documents.title: Kal Ho Naa Ho
documents.tagline: A story of a lifetime… in a heartbeat.
documents.overview: An uptight MBA student falls for the charismatic new neighbor who charms her troubled family – but he has a secret that forces him to push her away.
documents.plot:
Naina Catherine Kapur is a pessimistic, uptight Punjabi American business student who lives in New York City with her widowed mother Jennifer, a Punjabi Christian, disabled brother Shiv, adopted sister Jiya and paternal grandmother Lajjo, a Punjabi Sikh. Jennifer runs an unsuccessful café with her neighbour, Jaswinder "Jazz" Kapoor. Lajjo is hostile to Jennifer and Jia as she believes that Jiya's adoption led her son (Jennifer's husband and Naina's father) to suicide.
Naina has two best friends: her classmate, Rohit Patel, an Indian Gujarati American, and Jaspreet "Sweetu" Kapoor, Jazz's sister. Her life is dull and overshadowed by the loss of her father until Aman Mathur and his mother move in next door with his uncle, Pritam Chaddha. Aman's cheerfulness gradually wins over Naina's family and he slowly starts to solve their problems. He suggests that they change the café to an Indian restaurant and its success alleviates their financial burdens. Aman encourages Naina to be happy and to live life to the fullest; she ends up falling in love with him.
Rohit also falls in love with Naina and asks Aman's help in expressing his feelings. Naina tells Rohit there is something she must say to him, leading him to think that she reciprocates his feelings. Naina reveals she is in love with Aman instead. Shaken, Rohit calls Aman to tell him what has happened. Naina goes to Aman's house and is shocked to see a wedding photograph of Aman and his wife, Priya. Heartbroken, she leaves.
Aman's mother confronts him about what has happened. He says he loves Naina but has decided to hide it because he is suffering from a fatal heart condition. He is not actually married. Priya is his childhood friend and doctor. Aman vows to bring Naina and Rohit together before he dies. He believes that Rohit will be able to provide for her better than he can. He hatches a plan to transform Naina and Rohit's bond, and gradually their friendship blossoms into love. Naina discovers his plan and chides Aman for trying to ruin her friendship with Rohit. Aman takes out Rohit's diary and confesses his feelings for Naina, saying they are Rohit's. Naina forgives Aman and Rohit.
Rohit proposes to Naina, and she accepts. Lajjo and Jennifer have a serious fight regarding Jiya, who calls on Aman for help. Aman had previously discovered the truth about Jiya's parents and despite Jennifer's objections, he reveals to Lajjo that her son had an extramarital affair and fathered Jiya. When Jiya's biological mother refused to accept her, Jennifer adopted her. Unable to deal with the guilt, Jennifer's husband committed suicide. An emotional Lajjo realises her mistakes and reconciles with Jennifer and Jiya. Naina gains closure after learning the truth about her father's death.
During Naina and Rohit's engagement, Aman has a heart attack. Only his mother knows he has been admitted to the hospital. Naina encounters Priya at a jewellery store, whom she recognises as Aman's wife.

documents.title: Scary Movie 3
documents.tagline: Great trilogies come in threes.
documents.overview: In the third installment of the Scary Movie franchise, news anchorwoman Cindy Campbell has to investigate mysterious crop circles and killing video tapes, and help the President stop an alien invasion in the process.
documents.plot:
Scary Movie 3 is a horror comedy film directed by David Zucker, released in 2003 by Dimension Films. The movie is a parody of popular horror films, particularly The Ring and Signs.

The story begins with Cindy Campbell (Anna Faris), the protagonist, who is now married to Bobby (Derek Richardson) and has a baby. She receives a mysterious videotape that supposedly predicts her death in 7 days, similar to the one sent to Rachel Keller (Naomi Watts) in The Ring. However, this tape contains a different message: it's a recording of Cindy's own funeral.

As predicted, Cindy starts experiencing strange and terrifying events, including unexplained noises, movements, and visions. She soon discovers that she is being stalked by a supernatural entity known as "The Scary Movie Killer" (also referred to as "The Ringmaster").

Meanwhile, Bobby becomes increasingly paranoid and convinced that the tape is real, leading to comedic moments of tension between the couple. Cindy's best friend, Juno (Rachael Harris), tries to help her uncover the truth behind the tape.

As the predicted death date approaches, Cindy delves deeper into the mystery, discovering a connection between the tape and an ancient ritual that unleashes a malevolent entity. The Scary Movie Killer is revealed to be a cult leader who uses the videotape as a tool for summoning the entity.

In a thrilling climax, Cindy and Bobby must work together to stop the cult and destroy the videotape, saving themselves from certain doom. Along the way, they encounter various comedic characters, including a bumbling FBI agent (Timothy Olyphant) and a group of eccentric cult members.

Throughout the movie, Scary Movie 3 pokes fun at popular horror tropes, exaggerating and distorting familiar elements to create a humorous and irreverent take on the genre. The film's success can be attributed to its clever writing, witty dialogue, and impressive parody skills.

Ultimately, Cindy and Bobby succeed in destroying the videotape, saving themselves from death. However, the movie ends with a twist: as they celebrate their victory, Cindy receives another mysterious tape that predicts her next demise...

documents.title: Scary Movie 4
documents.tagline: Bury the grudge. Burn the village.  See the saw.
documents.overview: Cindy finds out the house she lives in is haunted by a little boy and goes on a quest to find out who killed him and why. Also, Alien "Tr-iPods" are invading the world and she has to uncover the secret in order to stop them.
documents.plot:
Scary Movie 4 is a 2006 American parody film directed by David Zucker from a screenplay by Craig Mazin, Jim Abrahams and Pat Proft. The fourth Scary Movie film, it brings back Anna Faris, Regina Hall, Anthony Anderson, Kevin Hart and Leslie Nielsen, with Craig Bierko, Bill Pullman, Cloris Leachman, Michael Madsen, Molly Shannon, Shaquille O'Neal and Dr. Phil McGraw. Its main targets are War of the Worlds, The Grudge, Saw, The Village and Million Dollar Baby, and it opened in April 2006.

In a parody of Saw, Shaquille O'Neal and Dr. Phil wake chained up in a bathroom filling with nerve gas, and fail the puppet Billy's test in absurd fashion. Meanwhile, the recently widowed Cindy Campbell, whose husband George died in a boxing match and whose nephew has gone to military school, takes a job caring for the elderly Mrs. Norris in a house haunted by the ghost of a pale Japanese boy. Next door lives Tom Ryan, a divorced father who has his children Robbie and Rachel for the weekend, and who learns of an awkward secret between George's friends Mahalik and CJ.

Cindy and Tom fall for each other, but their romance is cut short when an enormous alien tripod knocks out the power and starts vaporising residents. Through a garbled exchange in mock Japanese, the ghost tells Cindy that the key to stopping the invasion lies in his father's heart. Tom flees with his children, while Cindy, reunited with her friend Brenda, who has unaccountably survived her earlier death, goes to an isolated village ruled by Henry Hale, where the two are put on trial and forbidden to leave.

At the United Nations, the bumbling President Baxter Harris causes chaos with tasteless jokes and an alien device that strips everyone naked. Tom and his children are caught in a battle between the army and the aliens; Robbie runs off, and Tom and Rachel are seized by a tripod. In the village, the madman Ezekiel kills Henry, and the plot reveals the ghost boy's tangled parentage.

Cindy and Brenda are captured and brought to the bathroom from the prologue, where Cindy survives the puppet's game and works out that the alien leader is the boy's real father. Moved by Tom's devotion to his children, the puppet apologises and calls off the invasion. In an epilogue, Tom wildly declares his love for Cindy on The Oprah Winfrey Show. The film opened to about 40 million dollars and grossed some 178 million worldwide, though reviews were poor, with 34% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Scary Movie 5
documents.tagline: Evil is coming. Bring protection.
documents.overview: Home with their newly-formed family, happy parents Dan and Jody are haunted by sinister, paranormal activities. Determined to expel the insidious force, they install security cameras and discover their family is being stalked by an evil dead demon.
documents.plot:
Scary Movie 5 (stylized as Scary MoVie) is a 2013 American parody film directed by Malcolm D. Lee and written by David Zucker and Pat Proft. The fifth installment in the Scary Movie series and a standalone sequel to Scary Movie 4, it was the second and last entry distributed by The Weinstein Company and the only one without Anna Faris and Regina Hall as Cindy and Brenda. The cast includes Ashley Tisdale, Simon Rex, Erica Ash, Katrina Bowden, Terry Crews, Heather Locklear, Jerry O'Connell, Molly Shannon, Snoop Dogg, Kate Walsh and Katt Williams, along with Charlie Sheen and Lindsay Lohan. It premiered at the ArcLight Cinerama Dome in Hollywood and was released by Dimension Films on April 12, 2013.

In the opening, Charlie Sanders and his girlfriend Lindsay set up more than twenty cameras to film a sex tape, until a paranormal force sends Charlie flying around the room and a possessed Lindsay kills him. His three children disappear, and months later they are found living feral in a cabin in the woods and are eventually handed over to Charlie's estranged brother Dan and his wife Jody. The family moves into a large suburban house fitted with security cameras, and Jody, though reluctant to take in the children at first, soon adapts while she rehearses for the lead role in a ballet production of Swan Lake. Meanwhile, a series of increasingly bizarre paranormal events plagues the house. The children explain that the attacks come from "Mama", their cursed biological mother, who wants them back. The housekeeper Maria tries every ritual she knows to drive out the evil spirits, and Dan, a scientist at a primate research facility, fails to notice that one of his chimpanzees, Caesar, has become far smarter than he is. With help from Jody's friend Kendra from the ballet, a fraudulent psychic and a dream extractor, the couple must find a way to break the curse, which leads them to a mysterious tome called the Book of the Evil. The film spoofs a wide range of recent hits, chiefly Paranormal Activity, Black Swan, Mama and Rise of the Planet of the Apes, along with Sinister, Inception and Evil Dead.

The film was universally panned by critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, only 4% of 51 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 11 out of 100, indicating "overwhelming dislike". It grossed $78.4 million worldwide, making it the worst-reviewed and lowest-grossing film in the series.

documents.title: Primeval
documents.tagline: Inspired by the true story of the most prolific serial killer in history.
documents.overview: A news team is sent to Burundi to capture and bring home a legendary 25-foot crocodile. Their difficult task turns potentially deadly when a warlord targets them for death.
documents.plot:
Primeval is a 2007 American action horror film directed by Michael Katleman, starring Dominic Purcell as Tim Manfrey, Brooke Langton as Aviva Masters and Orlando Jones as Steven Johnson, with Jürgen Prochnow and Gideon Emery. It was partly inspired by Gustave, a real giant man-eating Nile crocodile in Burundi said to measure about 20 feet, and follows an American news team sent to capture him.

After a British forensic anthropologist examining a mass grave in Burundi is dragged into a river and killed, New York television journalist Tim Manfrey, who is in trouble over a story built on falsified evidence, is sent by his boss to Burundi with animal reporter Aviva Masters to cover the legend of Gustave, a colossal crocodile blamed for hundreds of deaths. Joined by cameraman Steven Johnson and herpetologist Matt Collins, who hopes to capture the animal alive, they ignore warnings from a government official called Harry about a ruthless warlord known as "Little Gustave" and head into the bush with two soldiers. In a riverside village they meet the hunter Jacob Krieg, and a shaman tells them that humanity's darkness breeds its own monsters.

Their steel cage, baited with a goat, fails, though Matt hits Gustave with a tracking dart. Steven secretly films the warlord's men executing the shaman and his family, putting the team in danger. Gustave kills a soldier who attacks Aviva, and the other soldier wounds Jacob before being killed by a village boy, Jojo. When the crocodile attacks their stilt house, Jacob, whose wife was killed by Gustave, tries to blow it up with a grenade that fails and is devoured. The next morning, the warlord's men destroy their rescue helicopter and kill Matt, and Steven is chased down by Gustave. Tim realizes that the bodies left by the civil war fed the crocodile's growth, and that Harry is actually Little Gustave. Demanding the execution footage, Harry is tricked into following the dart's signal to Gustave's lair, where Aviva douses him in crocodile pheromones and the beast devours him. Tim drives the crocodile off with a machete, and the survivors escape. The credits note that the real Gustave was believed to still be alive.

Released by Disney on January 12, 2007, the film received negative reviews and grossed about $15.3 million worldwide. Katleman later said that marketing the crocodile like a serial killer, rather than as a monster movie, hurt the film. It is unrelated to the British television series of the same name.

documents.title: Charlie's Angels
documents.tagline: Get some action.
documents.overview: The captivating crime-fighting trio who are masters of disguise, espionage and martial arts are back! When a devious mastermind embroils them in a plot to destroy individual privacy, the Angels, aided by their loyal sidekick Bosley, set out to bring down the bad guys. But when a terrible secret is revealed, it makes the Angels targets for assassination.
documents.plot:
Charlie's Angels is a 2000 action-comedy film directed by McG and written by John Brancato, Michael Ferris, and Shane Black. The movie is a remake of the 1976 television series of the same name.

The story begins with Charlie Townsend (played by John Forsythe), a wealthy businessman who employs three women, known as Angels, to carry out various missions for him. The Angels are: Dylan Sanders (played by Drew Barrymore), a tough and confident operative; Natalie Cook (played by Cameron Diaz), a sweet and innocent-looking but deadly Angel; and Alex Munday (played by Lucy Liu), a quiet and reserved but highly skilled Angel.

The movie opens with the Angels on a mission to stop a group of terrorists who are planning to steal a valuable diamond. The Angels successfully complete their mission, but not before they are ambushed by the terrorists' leader, Warren Stiles (played by Crispin Glover).

After the mission, Charlie reveals that he has been watching the Angels from afar and is impressed with their skills. He decides to take them on as his personal agents, giving them a team of experts to help them complete their missions.

As the story progresses, the Angels are tasked with stopping a group of rogue agents who have stolen a valuable diamond. The Angels soon discover that the diamond is actually a fake, and they must track down the real one before it falls into the wrong hands.

Along the way, the Angels encounter various obstacles and challenges, including a villainous character named Warren Stiles, who is revealed to be working for a wealthy businessman named James Dalton (played by Robert Patrick). The Angels also discover that Charlie's true intentions are not entirely pure, and they begin to question their loyalty to him.

In the end, the Angels successfully complete their mission and stop the villains. However, the movie ends with a twist: Charlie is revealed to be working for a secret organization known as "The Syndicate," which has been manipulating world events from behind the scenes.

Throughout the movie, the Angels are portrayed as strong and independent women who can hold their own in any situation. The film features plenty of action, humor, and style, making it an entertaining watch for audiences.

Overall, Charlie's Angels is a fun and action-packed movie that pays homage to the original television series while also offering something new and exciting.

documents.title: Atonement
documents.tagline: Torn apart by betrayal. Separated by war. Bound by love.
documents.overview: As a 13-year-old, fledgling writer Briony Tallis irrevocably changes the course of several lives when she accuses her older sister's lover of a crime he did not commit.
documents.plot:
Atonement is a 2007 romantic drama film directed by Joe Wright, based on the novel of the same name by Ian McEwan. The story takes place in England during World War II and spans several decades.

The film begins with a framing device, where an elderly Robbie Turner (James McAvoy) reads a letter to his sister, Cecilia (Saoirse Ronan), about their childhood and the events that led to a family tragedy. The story then unfolds through a series of flashbacks, which reveal the complex relationships between the characters.

The narrative centers around Briony Tallis (Keira Knightley), a young and impressionable girl who lives with her older sister Cecilia and brother Robbie on their family's estate in Kent. Briony is a daydreamer and an avid reader of romance novels, which influences her perception of reality.

During a summer vacation, Briony mistakenly accuses Robbie of raping Cecilia, which leads to a devastating consequence: Cecilia flees the country, leaving behind her fiancé, James (Simon Woods), who is killed in action during World War II. The incident also causes a rift between Briony and her family.

The film then follows the story of Robbie, who joins the British Army and becomes embroiled in the war effort. He meets Lola Quincey (Tilda Swinton), a French Resistance fighter, and falls in love with her. Meanwhile, Cecilia is living in America, trying to rebuild her life after the tragedy.

As the war rages on, Robbie and Lola's relationship deepens, but they are separated when Lola is killed during a mission. Robbie returns home, where he finds Briony, who has been struggling to come to terms with her past mistake.

The film's climax reveals that Briony's accusation was not only false but also motivated by jealousy and a desire for attention. In the end, Briony makes amends with Robbie and Cecilia, and the family begins to heal from their wounds.

Throughout the film, Wright masterfully weaves together themes of love, guilt, and redemption, creating a complex and emotionally charged narrative. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of the English countryside and the brutality of war.

The performances by the cast are outstanding, with Keira Knightley delivering a nuanced and heartbreaking portrayal of Briony. James McAvoy brings depth and vulnerability to Robbie, while Saoirse Ronan shines as the adult Cecilia.

Overall, Atonement is a powerful and moving film that explores the long-lasting consequences of a single mistake. With its intricate plot, memorable characters, and stunning visuals, it's a must-see for fans of period dramas and romantic stories.

documents.title: Pride & Prejudice
documents.tagline: A romance ahead of its time.
documents.overview: A story of love and life among the landed English gentry during the Georgian era. Mr. Bennet is a gentleman living in Hertfordshire with his overbearing wife and five daughters, but if he dies their house will be inherited by a distant cousin whom they have never met, so the family's future happiness and security is dependent on the daughters making good marriages.
documents.plot:
Pride & Prejudice is a 2005 period romance directed by Joe Wright in his feature debut, based on Jane Austen's 1813 novel and written by Deborah Moggach. It stars Keira Knightley as Elizabeth Bennet and Matthew Macfadyen as Mr Darcy, with Brenda Blethyn and Donald Sutherland as Mr and Mrs Bennet, Rosamund Pike as Jane, Carey Mulligan, Talulah Riley and Jena Malone as the younger Bennet sisters, and Judi Dench as Lady Catherine de Bourgh. Produced by Working Title Films with StudioCanal, it was shot entirely on location in England.

In late eighteenth-century England, the Bennets and their five daughters live at Longbourn, a modest estate in Hertfordshire that, because it is entailed to the male line, will pass to a cousin on Mr Bennet's death. Mrs Bennet is determined to marry her daughters well and is thrilled when the wealthy bachelor Mr Bingley rents the nearby Netherfield Hall. At a local ball, Bingley and Jane are immediately drawn to each other, while the spirited Elizabeth takes an instant dislike to Bingley's proud friend, Mr Darcy, after overhearing him dismiss her.

Elizabeth rejects a proposal from the pompous clergyman Mr Collins and is charmed by the officer George Wickham, who claims that Darcy cheated him of his inheritance. When Bingley abruptly leaves for London, Elizabeth learns that Darcy persuaded him to abandon Jane. Darcy then confesses his love to Elizabeth and proposes, but she angrily refuses him. A letter from Darcy reveals the truth about Wickham, and when Wickham elopes with Elizabeth's youngest sister Lydia, threatening the family with disgrace, Darcy's secret intervention leads Elizabeth to reconsider her prejudices and recognize her own feelings.

Wright and Moggach set the story in an earlier period and presented a more realistic, "muddy hem" version of Austen's world, emphasizing romanticism and family.

Released in the United Kingdom on 16 September 2005, Pride & Prejudice grossed 131.9 million dollars worldwide on a budget of 28 million dollars and received positive reviews, with praise for Knightley's performance. It earned four Academy Award nominations, including Best Actress for Knightley.

documents.title: The Kingdom
documents.tagline: How do you stop an enemy who isn't afraid to die?
documents.overview: A team of U.S. government agents is sent to investigate the bombing of an American facility in the Middle East.
documents.plot:
The Kingdom is a 2007 American action thriller directed by Peter Berg and starring Jamie Foxx, Chris Cooper, Jennifer Garner and Jason Bateman, with Ashraf Barhom, Ali Suliman and Jeremy Piven. Set in Saudi Arabia, it follows an FBI team investigating a terrorist attack, drawing on the 1996 Khobar Towers bombing, the 2003 Riyadh compound bombings and the 2004 Khobar massacre. It premiered at the Edinburgh International Film Festival before Universal Pictures released it in the United States on September 28, 2007.

In Riyadh, militants disguised as Saudi police storm a compound housing American oil workers and their families, shooting residents before a suicide bomber blows himself up; Sergeant Haytham of the Saudi police manages to stop one gunman. As investigators gather, a second, much larger bomb devastates the site, killing Francis Manner, the FBI's legal attaché, among others. In Washington, Special Agent Ronald Fleury, Manner's friend, suspects that the attack was masterminded by the elusive terrorist Abu Hamza.

Although the Justice and State Departments try to keep the FBI out, Fleury pressures the Saudi ambassador into granting his team a short visit. He brings forensic examiner Janet Mayes, intelligence analyst Adam Leavitt and bomb technician Grant Sykes. In Riyadh they are assigned to Colonel Faris al-Ghazi of the Saudi State Police, while a National Guard general keeps them from the evidence. At a meeting with a Saudi prince, Fleury persuades him to put al-Ghazi in charge, giving the Americans access to the crime scene, and Fleury and al-Ghazi develop a mutual respect.

The investigators find that the second bomb was hidden in an ambulance, leading to a raid on a militant hideout. Ordered home by the embassy, the team's convoy is ambushed and Leavitt is kidnapped. Al-Ghazi and the agents chase the abductors into a dangerous district and a fierce gun battle erupts; Mayes rescues Leavitt moments before his filmed execution.

In a nearby apartment, al-Ghazi realises that an old man is Abu Hamza. Abu Hamza's teenage grandson shoots al-Ghazi, and Fleury and Haytham kill the boy and the terrorist. Al-Ghazi dies in Fleury's arms. Back home, Leavitt asks what Fleury whispered to Mayes after Manner's death, and the film reveals that Fleury's words and those of Abu Hamza to his grandchild were the same: that they would kill them all.

The film received mixed reviews, with 51% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and was banned in Kuwait and Bahrain.

documents.title: Monster-in-Law
documents.tagline: This relationship is going to be a real mother.
documents.overview: Office temp Charlotte Cantilini thinks she's found Mr. Right when she starts dating gorgeous surgeon Dr. Kevin Fields. But there's a problem standing in the way of everlasting bliss: Kevin's overbearing and controlling mother, Viola. Fearing she'll lose her son's affections forever, Viola decides to break up the happy couple by becoming the world's worst mother-in-law.
documents.plot:
Charlie Cantilini is a temp/dog walker/yoga instructor and aspiring fashion designer from Venice Beach, California, who meets doctor Kevin Fields. At first, she believes he is gay, but Kevin later asks her out, and she feels she has finally found the right man.
Things start to sour when Kevin introduces Charlie to his mother Viola, a former newscaster turned talk show host. She was recently replaced by a much younger woman, leading her to have a meltdown and attack 16-year-old music pop star Tanya Murphy, and be committed to a facility for several months.
Loathing Charlie immediately because of her occupation as a temp, Viola becomes more distraught when Kevin proposes to her, fearing she will lose her son the same way she lost her career. Determined to ruin Kevin and Charlie's relationship, she enlists the help of her loyal assistant Ruby, and Kevin's vindictive ex-girlfriend Fiona, who had previously misled Charlie into believing that Kevin was gay.
At the engagement party, Fiona kisses Kevin in his dressing room, deeply hurting Charlie, who feels out of place in Kevin’s world, precisely as Viola and Fiona planned. Viola feigns an anxiety attack and moves in with Charlie while Kevin is away for a medical conference, hoping to drive her crazy with her antics.
Charlie soon realizes Viola's plan and retaliates by destroying her bedroom and tampering with her antipsychotic medication (which Viola had replaced with vitamin C tablets). Charlie eventually confronts her, forcing her to move out. Finding no way to stop the wedding, Viola tricks Charlie into eating nuts during the rehearsal dinner. This causes an extreme allergic reaction, which causes Charlie's face and tongue to swell. Luckily, it subsides by the next morning.
On the day of the wedding, Viola turns up wearing an extravagant white dress instead of the peach-colored one Charlie had specially made for her. This leads to a violent standoff between them, with Viola refusing to accept her and declaring Charlie will never be good enough for Kevin.
Suddenly, Viola's dreadful mother-in-law, Kevin's grandmother Gertrude, arrives, and they have an indignant argument. Gertrude holds Viola responsible for the death of her son, Kevin's father, many years earlier, claiming he died of "terminal disappointment”, while Viola claims Gertrude is responsible, as she “smothered him to death”, because she believed that no woman would ever be good enough for him. Gertrude's resentment of Viola resembles Viola's animosity towards Charlie, who decides to back down because she feels the same thing will happen to them in 30 years.
Charlie leaves to tell Kevin the wedding is off, but Ruby finally gets through to Viola. She resents being compared to Gertrude, but Ruby points out that Viola is far worse as Gertrude never tried to poison her, (referring to the nuts at the rehearsal dinner).

documents.title: Shall We Dance?
documents.tagline: Step out of the ordinary.
documents.overview: Upon first sight of a beautiful instructor, a bored and overworked estate lawyer signs up for ballroom dancing lessons.
documents.plot:
John Clark is a lawyer with a charming wife, Beverly, and a loving family, who nevertheless feels that something is missing as he makes his way every day through the city. Each evening on his commute home through Chicago, John sees a beautiful woman staring with a lost expression through the window of a dance studio. Haunted by her gaze, John impulsively jumps off the train one night, and signs up for ballroom dancing lessons, hoping to meet her.
At first, it seems like a mistake. His teacher turns out not to be the woman in the window, Paulina, but the studio's older namesake, Miss Mitzi, and John proves to be just as clumsy as his equally clueless classmates Chic and Vern on the dance-floor. Even worse, when he does meet Paulina, she icily tells John she hopes he has come to the studio to seriously study dance and not to look for a date. But, as his lessons continue, John falls in love with dancing.
Keeping his new obsession from his family and co-workers, John feverishly trains for Chicago's biggest dance competition. His friendship with Paulina blossoms, as his enthusiasm rekindles her own lost passion for dance. But the more time John spends away from home, the more his wife Beverly becomes suspicious. She hires a private investigator to find out what John is doing, but when she finds out the truth, she chooses to discontinue the investigation and not invade her husband's privacy.
John is partnered with Bobbie for the competition, although his friend Link steps in to do the Latin dances. Link and Bobbie do well in the Latin dances, and while John and Bobbie's waltz goes well, John hears his wife and daughter in the crowd during the quickstep, and is distracted by trying to find them. He and Bobbie fall and are disqualified, and he and Beverly argue in the parking garage. He then quits dancing, much to everyone's dismay.
Paulina, having been inspired by John to take up competing again, is leaving to go to Europe, and is having a going-away party at the dance studio. She sends John an invitation, but he is not convinced to go until his wife leaves out a pair of dancing shoes that she bought him. He goes and meets Beverly at work, convinces her that while he loves dancing, he still loves her just as much, and he teaches her to dance. They go to the party, and John and Paulina have one last dance before she leaves.
The end scene shows everyone afterwards: Link and Bobbie are now together; Chic, who was actually gay, dances at a club with his partner; Miss Mitzi finds a new partner, and they are happy together; John and Beverly are happier than before and dance in the kitchen; Vern, newly married to his fiancée, dances with her at their wedding; the private investigator that Beverly hired, Devine, starts up dance lessons; and Paulina, with a new partner, competes at the Blackpool Dance Festival, the competition that she had lost the year before.

documents.title: The Brave One
documents.tagline: How many wrongs to make it right?
documents.overview: A woman struggles to recover from a brutal attack by setting out on a mission for revenge.
documents.plot:
Radio host Erica Bain and her fiancé Dr. David Kirmani are viciously attacked by three men while walking their dog in Central Park; the men record the assault on their phones and take Erica's engagement ring and her dog. David dies from his injuries, and Erica is unable to continue her life as normal.
Traumatized and living in fear, Erica attempts to purchase a gun legally but is denied a sale due to having no gun license. A nearby black market gun dealer overhears her desperation and offers to sell her a Kahr K9 pistol. Unwilling to wait 30 days for a legal firearm, Erica buys the handgun from him.
One evening while Erica is at a convenience store, a man enters and shoots the store's cashier to death. Hearing Erica's cell phone ring, the man stalks her in the aisles before she kills him with three shots. Another night on a subway car, two men harass the passengers, all of whom leave except Erica. The men then threaten her with a knife, but she kills them both.
Later, Erica attempts to save a prostitute by threatening her pimp. When he attempts to run them down with his car, Erica shoots him in the head, causing his car to run over the prostitute. She is injured but lives.
Fuelled by rage and a need for vengeance, Erica begins to track down the three men who killed David. Meanwhile, she strikes up a friendship with Detective Sean Mercer, who is investigating the vigilante killings around the city. The detective shares the name of a vicious criminal he is unable to prosecute.
When the criminal is found dead near a parking garage, Mercer inspects the area and begins to suspect Erica. He takes her with him to interview the prostitute she had saved, but the prostitute does not let on that she recognizes Erica. Mercer privately indicates to Erica that he suspects her but is struggling with what to do about it.
The police ask Erica to identify one of the suspects in her attack. Though she recognizes the assailant, she does not identify him. She is later informed that the police have found her engagement ring at a pawn shop and goes there to get a name, address, and phone number of who sold it to them. She tracks down one of her attacker's ex-girlfriends, who sends Erica the video recording of her attack and his address. Erica forwards the video to Mercer.
Erica tracks down all three men, confronting and killing two of them before freeing her dog. She struggles with the third attacker, who gains the upper hand just as Mercer arrives. As Mercer attempts to arrest the attacker, Erica retrieves her weapon and prepares to execute him.
Mercer persuades Erica to lower her gun, but after looking into her pleading eyes, hands her his own gun to use instead, so she shoots the attacker dead. He then insists she wound him with her gun, which she does, allowing them to frame her attackers for the vigilante killings. Mercer then places her gun in the last attacker's hand, and Erica walks away through Central Park joined by her dog.

documents.title: Aśoka
documents.tagline: Only the dead have seen the end of war
documents.overview: A young Prince Asoka works to perfect his skills in battle and also deals with family conflict. During a struggle with one of his step-brothers, his mother urges Asoka to escape to stay alive. While away, Asoka meets Kaurwaki and falls in love, but must use his skills as a warrior to protect her. A dangerous and heartbreaking web of conspiracy follows, which leads Asoka to embrace a Buddhist path.

documents.title: The Brothers Grimm
documents.tagline: Eliminating Evil Since 1812.
documents.overview: Folklore collectors and con artists, Jake and Will Grimm, travel from village to village pretending to protect townsfolk from enchanted creatures and performing exorcisms. However, they are put to the test  when they encounter a real magical curse in a haunted forest with real magical beings, requiring genuine courage.
documents.plot:
The Brothers Grimm is a 2005 fantasy adventure film directed by Terry Gilliam that reimagines the famous folklorists as travelling con artists in Napoleonic French-occupied Germany, who encounter a genuine fairy-tale curse requiring real courage rather than their usual fake exorcisms. Matt Damon, Heath Ledger and Lena Headey star, with Peter Stormare, Jonathan Pryce and Monica Bellucci in supporting roles. A British-Czech co-production shot in the Czech Republic, it was written by Ehren Kruger.

In 1811, Will and Jake Grimm and their assistants Hidlick and Bunst use Jake's deep knowledge of folklore to persuade villagers that they can banish the supernatural. Captured by the Italian torturer Mercurio Cavaldi and brought before the French general Delatombe, they are offered amnesty if they investigate the disappearance of young girls from the village of Marbaden. With the help of Angelika, a fur trapper whose younger sisters were the first to vanish, they learn of a tower in the nearby forest built centuries earlier by a vain Thuringian queen trying to escape the plague. That night an enchanted horse swallows a girl and carries her into the forest. Back in the forest, Jake climbs the tower, ringed by twelve crypts, and finds the ancient, decaying Queen, kept alive by a magic mirror that shows her youthful reflection. When a mud creature takes another girl, Sasha, a wolf-like huntsman places her in a crypt. The brothers rescue her and take the huntsman's axe, and Jake concludes that the girls are part of a ritual timed to a lunar eclipse to restore the Queen's youth. Delatombe executes Hidlick and Bunst, denounces the brothers as frauds and orders the forest burned with them inside, but Angelika frees them and recognizes the axe as her father's, revealing that the huntsman is her father under the Queen's spell. Angelika then becomes the twelfth and final victim. The Queen's wind puts out the fire, Will kills Delatombe, and when the Queen bewitches Will, Jake smashes the mirror; Angelika's father leaps from the tower with the rest of it, destroying the Queen. Jake revives Angelika with a kiss, the girls return home, and a raven flies off with a shard of the mirror.

Delayed for months by disputes between Gilliam and the Weinsteins, the film was released on 26 August 2005 and competed at the Venice Film Festival. It received mixed reviews, with a 38% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and grossed $105.3 million worldwide.

documents.title: Seabiscuit
documents.tagline: The hopes of a nation rode on a long shot.
documents.overview: True story of the undersized Depression-era racehorse whose victories lifted not only the spirits of the team behind it but also those of their nation.
documents.plot:
In the early 20th century, as America enters the automobile age, Charles S. Howard opens a bicycle shop in San Francisco. He is soon selling automobiles, becoming the largest car dealer in California and one of the Bay Area's richest men. In the wake of the Great Depression, 16-year-old Canadian John "Red" Pollard's family is financially ruined, and he is sent to live with a horse trainer. Years pass and Pollard becomes a jockey, but amateur boxing leaves him blind in one eye.
After their young son is killed in an automobile accident, Howard's wife leaves him. He obtains a divorce in Mexico, where Pollard is struggling to make his mark as a jockey. Howard meets and marries Marcela Zabala. When he acquires a stable of racehorses, he hires itinerant horseman Tom Smith as his trainer. Smith convinces him to buy a colt called Seabiscuit. Though a grandson of the great Man o' War and trained by the renowned James E. Fitzsimmons, Seabiscuit is viewed as small, lazy, and unmanageable. Smith witnesses Pollard's similarly temperamental spirit, and hires him as Seabiscuit's jockey.
Under Smith's innovative training, Seabiscuit becomes the most successful racehorse on the West Coast and an underdog hero to the public. Howard issues a challenge to Samuel D. Riddle, owner of the East Coast champion and Triple Crown-winning racehorse War Admiral, but Riddle dismisses California racing as inferior. In the prestigious Santa Anita Handicap, Seabiscuit takes the lead, but Pollard's impaired vision prevents him from noticing another horse surging up on the outside. Losing by a nose, Pollard admits his partial blindness to Smith.
Howard declares that Pollard will remain Seabiscuit's jockey, and rallies public support for a match race with War Admiral. Riddle agrees, on the condition that they race with a rope and bell instead of a starting gate. With Seabiscuit at a disadvantage, Smith trains the horse to break fast at the sound of the bell. As the race approaches, Pollard severely fractures his leg in a riding accident. Informed he may never walk again, let alone ride, he recommends that his friend and skilled jockey George Woolf ride Seabiscuit, advising him on the horse's handling and behavior from his hospital bed.
The highly anticipated "race of the century" draws a sellout crowd, with 40 million more people listening on the radio. Seabiscuit takes an early lead until nearing the far turn; following Pollard's advice, Woolf slows Seabiscuit, allowing War Admiral to match Seabicuit's stride. Seabiscuit looks War Admiral in the eye before surging ahead and winning by four lengths, enthralling the nation. A few months later, Seabiscuit injures his leg. Pollard, still recovering from his own injury, tends to the horse as they both heal. When Seabiscuit is fit enough to race again, Howard brings him back to the Santa Anita Handicap; he is reluctant to allow Pollard to ride and risk crippling himself for life. At the urging of Woolf and Marcela, Howard relents.

documents.title: Elizabeth: The Golden Age
documents.tagline: Woman. Warrior. Queen.
documents.overview: When Queen Elizabeth's reign is threatened by ruthless familial betrayal and Spain's invading army, she and her shrewd adviser must act to safeguard the lives of her people.

documents.title: Enchanted
documents.tagline: This fairytale princess is about to meet a real Prince Charming.
documents.overview: The beautiful princess Giselle is banished by an evil queen from her magical, musical animated land and finds herself in the gritty reality of the streets of modern-day Manhattan. Shocked by this strange new environment that doesn't operate on a "happily ever after" basis, Giselle is now adrift in a chaotic world badly in need of enchantment. But when Giselle begins to fall in love with a charmingly flawed divorce lawyer who has come to her aid - even though she is already promised to a perfect fairy tale prince back home - she has to wonder: Can a storybook view of romance survive in the real world?
documents.plot:
Enchanted is a 2007 American musical fantasy comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Giselle, a princess from the magical kingdom of Andalasia, who is engaged to Prince Edward.

The film begins with Giselle's wedding day, where she is about to marry Prince Edward. However, her life takes an unexpected turn when her evil stepmother, Queen Narissa, and her advisor, Morgan, plot to sabotage the wedding. In a dramatic twist, Giselle falls off a castle balcony and lands in the real world of New York City.

In the real world, Giselle meets Robert, a lawyer who is initially unaware of his royal connection. As they spend more time together, Giselle's innocence and naivety clash with the harsh realities of the modern world. Despite this, Robert finds himself falling for Giselle's charm and kindness.

Meanwhile, Queen Narissa and Morgan continue to pursue their evil plans, seeking to capture Giselle and use her as leverage to gain control over Prince Edward's kingdom. As Giselle navigates her new life in New York, she must also confront the reality of her own destiny and the true nature of her relationship with Prince Edward.

As the story unfolds, Robert becomes increasingly entangled in Giselle's world, and they begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their love is threatened by Queen Narissa's schemes, which lead to a dramatic confrontation between the two kingdoms.

In the end, Giselle must make a choice between her life in the real world with Robert or returning to her kingdom as the princess she was meant to be. Ultimately, Giselle decides to stay with Robert and find happiness in the real world, rather than conforming to the expectations of her royal duties.

The film features a range of memorable characters, including Morgan, who provides comedic relief, and the villainous Queen Narissa, whose evil plans drive much of the plot. The movie's blend of fantasy and reality creates a unique and engaging narrative that explores themes of love, identity, and the power of true connection.

Overall, Enchanted is a charming and entertaining film that offers a fresh take on traditional fairy tale tropes. With its witty dialogue, catchy musical numbers, and lovable characters, it has become a beloved classic among Disney fans and beyond.

documents.title: The Darjeeling Limited
documents.tagline: I want us to be brothers again, like we used to be.
documents.overview: Three American brothers who have not spoken to each other in a year set off on a train voyage across India with a plan to find themselves and bond with each other -- to become brothers again like they used to be. Their "spiritual quest", however, veers rapidly off-course (due to events involving over-the-counter pain killers, Indian cough syrup, and pepper spray).
documents.plot:
In India, Peter Whitman boards a train, "The Darjeeling Limited", as it pulls out of a station. On the train, he reunites with his brothers, Francis and Jack; the three have not seen each other since their father's funeral a year earlier.
Francis, the eldest, whose head is covered in bandages after a near-fatal motorcycle accident, wishes to reconcile with his brothers on a journey of spiritual self-discovery. He is also secretly searching for their mother, Patricia, whom the brothers have not seen in many years. With the help of his assistant, Brendan, Francis has drawn up a strict itinerary for the trip, and he confiscates his brothers' passports to prevent them from getting off the train too early. The brothers continue to grieve over their father's death: they carry many pieces of luggage marked with his initials, along with other personal items that belonged to him.
The train takes them through the countryside and to various Hindu and Sikh temples, though tension builds as Peter and Jack become angered with Francis's controlling behavior. Francis eventually reveals that they will be going to see Patricia, who has become a nun and is living at a Christian convent in the Himalayas. Peter and Jack are furious; Francis knew they would not come if he told them this earlier.
Their differences finally come to a head, and the brothers have a physical altercation on the train, upsetting the other passengers. The chief steward, whom the brothers have repeatedly annoyed throughout the journey, has them ejected. Brendan quits his job and reboards the train after giving Francis a letter from Patricia; the letter implies that she does not want to see them. The brothers decide to leave India, go their separate ways, and never return.
After hiking through the wilderness with all their luggage, the brothers see three young boys fall into a river while attempting to pull a raft across it. Jack and Francis rescue two of the boys, but Peter fails to save the third, who dies. They carry the body back to the boys' village, where they spend the night. They attend the funeral the next day and experience a flashback to the day of their father's funeral.
Riding to the funeral in a limousine with Peter's wife, Alice, the brothers get out to pick up their father's Porsche from a repair shop. When the mechanic tells them it is missing a part and the battery is dead, Peter frantically tries to get it moving, but he eventually has to give up, and the three continue on to the funeral in the same limousine. It is revealed that their father died from being hit by a taxi, and that their mother will not be attending the funeral.
Back in the present, the brothers arrive at the airport, but they suddenly decide to rip up their tickets and go visit their mother. They reach the convent, where Patricia is surprised but happy to see them. Francis tells her that his accident was actually intentional.

documents.title: Panic Room
documents.tagline: It was supposed to be the safest room in the house.
documents.overview: Trapped in their New York brownstone's panic room, a hidden chamber built as a sanctuary in the event of break-ins, newly divorced Meg Altman and her young daughter Sarah play a deadly game of cat-and-mouse with three intruders - Burnham, Raoul and Junior - during a brutal home invasion. But the room itself is the focal point because what the intruders really want is inside it.
