documents.title: Penelope
documents.tagline: A fairytale like no other.
documents.overview: Forlorn heiress Penelope Wilhern is cursed, and the only way out is to fall in love with someone of suitable stock. But how can she find her soul mate when she's sequestered inside her family's estate with only her parents to keep her company. This untraditional fairy tale about a girl who bucks convention to create her own happy ending.
documents.plot:
Penelope is a fantasy romantic comedy directed by Mark Palansky from a screenplay by Leslie Caveny, first shown in 2006. Christina Ricci is Penelope Wilhern, an heiress born with a pig's snout because of a family curse, with James McAvoy as Johnny Martin, Catherine O'Hara and Richard E. Grant as her parents Jessica and Franklin, Peter Dinklage as the tabloid reporter Lemon, Simon Woods as the suitor Edward Vanderman III and Reese Witherspoon, who also produced the film, as the delivery girl Annie.

Generations ago, a servant, Clara, became pregnant by the aristocrat Ralph Wilhern, who married another woman at his parents' insistence; after Clara killed herself, her mother, a witch, cursed the family so that the next Wilhern daughter would have the face of a pig until loved by "one of her own kind". After five generations of sons, Penelope is born. Her mortified mother pretends the baby died and hides her in the family's London mansion, and once Penelope turns eighteen, a matchmaker parades blue-blooded suitors before her, convinced that marrying one will break the spell. All flee in horror, Edward among them, and he teams up with Lemon to prove she exists by hiring a gambler posing as the aristocrat Max Campion to photograph her with a hidden camera.

Talking through a one-way mirror, Penelope and "Max" fall for each other. When he sees her face he is startled but not afraid; ashamed, he destroys the camera, but refuses her plea to marry him. Fed up with confinement, Penelope runs away into the city with her face hidden by a scarf, selling photographs of herself to Lemon and befriending Annie. When her face is exposed in a pub, the public adores her, and Edward's father pressures his son into proposing. At the altar, Penelope realises she does not want to marry merely to lift the curse and declares that she likes herself as she is; because she has been loved by one of her own kind, herself, her snout vanishes. Now a schoolteacher, she learns that "Max" is really Johnny Martin and finds him at a Halloween party, where they kiss. The family butler, revealed to be the witch, silences Jessica with a last spell, and Lemon chooses not to photograph the happy couple.

Shot in London and at Pinewood Studios in early 2006 as Witherspoon's first production, Penelope premiered at the Toronto festival in September 2006, with Summit Entertainment later handling its American release. It grossed $21.2 million worldwide and drew mixed reviews, with 53% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Behind Enemy Lines
documents.tagline: His only weapon is his will to survive.
documents.overview: While flying a routine reconnaissance mission over Bosnia, fighter pilot Chris Burnett photographs something he wasn't supposed to see and gets shot down behind enemy lines, where he must outrun an army led by a ruthless Serbian general. With time running out and a deadly tracker on his trail, Burnett's commanding officer decides to risk his career and launch a renegade rescue mission to save his life.
documents.plot: While flying a routine reconnaissance mission over Bosnia, fighter pilot Lt. Chris Burnett photographs something he wasn't supposed to see and gets shot down behind enemy lines, where he must outrun an army led by a ruthless Serbian general. With time running out and a deadly tracker on his trail, Burnett's commanding officer, Admiral Reigart, decides to risk his career and launch a renegade rescue mission to save his life.

documents.title: Highlander
documents.tagline: There can be only one.
documents.overview: He fought his first battle on the Scottish Highlands in 1536. He will fight his greatest battle on the streets of New York City in 1986. His name is Connor MacLeod. He is immortal.
documents.plot:
Highlander is a 1986 American fantasy adventure film directed by Russell Mulcahy and written by Gregory Widen. The movie stars Christopher Lambert as Connor MacLeod, a Scottish Highlander who discovers he is an immortal.

The story begins with Connor, a young man living in Scotland during the Jacobite rising of 1745. He witnesses the Battle of Culloden, where his clan is defeated, and he is mortally wounded. However, instead of dying, Connor is healed by Juan Sanchez Villa-Lobos Ramírez (Sean Connery), an immortal who has been watching over him.

Juan explains to Connor that immortals are born with a "prize," which is the essence of every human being's soul. The prize is what makes them unique and gives them their individuality. Immortals must find and kill other immortals in order to gain their prizes, thereby becoming more powerful and closer to achieving their ultimate goal: the Prize.

Connor learns that he has been chosen as a "Immortal" and that his prize is the soul of an unknown woman. He sets out on a journey across time and space to find her, while also being pursued by other immortals who seek to kill him.

As Connor travels through history, he encounters various characters, including Juan, who becomes his mentor and guide. Along the way, he meets other immortals, such as the Kurgan (Clancy Brown), a ruthless and cunning immortal who seeks to kill Connor and claim his prize for himself.

Throughout the movie, Connor's journey takes him from 18th-century Scotland to modern-day New York City. He faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including battles with other immortals and struggles with his own identity.

As the story unfolds, Connor becomes increasingly obsessed with finding the woman whose soul is his prize. He believes that she holds the key to understanding his purpose as an immortal and that their reunion will bring him peace and fulfillment.

The movie culminates in a final showdown between Connor and the Kurgan. The two immortals engage in a fierce battle, during which they exchange blows and insults. In the end, Connor emerges victorious, but not before the Kurgan reveals that he has been searching for the woman whose soul is Connor's prize.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that the woman Connor was searching for all along is actually his own wife, who had died in childbirth. The movie ends with Connor finally finding peace and understanding, as he realizes that his true prize is not the soul of another person, but rather the love and connection he shares with those around him.

Overall, Highlander is a classic tale of immortality, adventure, and self-discovery. With its unique blend of action, drama, and fantasy elements, it has become a beloved cult classic among fans of science fiction and adventure movies.

documents.title: Gigli
documents.tagline: Life doesn't play by the rules.
documents.overview: Gigli is ordered to kidnap the psychologically challenged younger brother of a powerful federal prosecutor. When plans go awry, Gigli's boss sends in Ricki, a gorgeous free-spirited female gangster who has her own set of orders to assist with the kidnapping. But Gigli begins falling for the decidedly unavailable Ricki, which could be a hazard to his occupation.
documents.plot:
Gigli is a 2003 American romantic comedy crime film written, co-produced and directed by Martin Brest for Revolution Studios. Ben Affleck stars as Larry Gigli, a small-time Los Angeles mobster, and Jennifer Lopez as Ricki, a fellow enforcer sent to keep an eye on him, with Justin Bartha as Brian, Lenny Venito as Louis, Al Pacino as Starkman, Christopher Walken as Detective Stanley Jacobellis and Lainie Kazan in a supporting role.

Larry Gigli is a low-level hoodlum eager to prove that he is tougher and more capable than he really is. His boss, Louis, orders him to kidnap Brian, the intellectually disabled younger brother of a federal prosecutor, so that the prosecutor can be pressured into helping the New York mob boss Starkman stay out of prison. Larry lures Brian away by promising to take him "to the Baywatch", the television series he is obsessed with, but Louis does not trust him to handle the job alone and sends a woman calling herself Ricki to supervise. Larry is instantly attracted to her and resents taking orders from her, and his advances are rebuffed when she tells him that she is a lesbian. Hiding out in Larry's apartment, the trio grows more volatile; Brian keeps demanding to go to "the Baywatch" and runs up huge phone bills calling an Australian operator because he loves the accent. When Louis orders them to cut off Brian's thumb and mail it to the prosecutor, a horrified Larry instead steals a thumb from a corpse in a hospital morgue. As Larry opens up about himself and his frustrations, Ricki softens, and the two sleep together. Summoned before Starkman, they learn that he never approved the kidnapping and is furious, all the more because the thumb does not match Brian's fingerprints and so exposes the bluff. He kills Louis for drawing police attention and is ready to kill them too, until Ricki argues that only they can contain the damage. Spared, the pair decide to leave the mob. Driving along the coast with Brian, they come upon a beach video shoot that looks like Baywatch, and they let him off there, where he is delighted to meet an Australian woman. Larry urges Ricki to drive off without him, but she turns back, and they leave together to start a new life.

Released by Sony on 1 August 2003 amid intense coverage of the stars' off-screen romance, the film was savaged by critics, earning 6% on Rotten Tomatoes and 18 on Metacritic, and grossed $7.3 million on a budget of $75.6 million, one of the costliest flops in history.

documents.title: The Reader
documents.tagline: Behind the mystery lies a truth that will make you question everything you know.
documents.overview: The story of Michael Berg, a German lawyer who, as a teenager in the late 1950s, had an affair with an older woman, Hanna, who then disappeared only to resurface years later as one of the defendants in a war crimes trial stemming from her actions as a concentration camp guard late in the war. He alone realizes that Hanna is illiterate and may be concealing that fact at the expense of her freedom.
documents.plot:
In 1958, 15-year-old Michael Berg becomes sick on a tram ride in an unnamed provincial city. He is helped by 36-year-old tram conductor Hanna Schmitz. Weeks later, he has recovered from scarlet fever and at his mother's insistence visits Hanna with flowers to thank her for her help. They proceed to have a secret summer love affair, and Hanna often asks Michael to read to her. They have a brief cycling holiday in the country where Michael starts to notice some oddities in Hanna's behaviour. However, as their sexual relationship deepens it grows more tumultuous, when his attempts to form a deeper connection are rebuffed by her secretive nature. As a good reliable worker, Hanna is soon promoted, whereupon she abruptly leaves without explanation. Michael visits Hanna to apologize following an argument, but is confused and devastated to find her apartment vacant.
In 1966, Michael is a student at Heidelberg University Law School and observes a war crime trial of several former female SS guards accused of letting 300 Jewish women and children perish in a burning church during a death march near Kraków in Poland. He is horrified to learn that Hanna is one of the defendants. Survivor Ilana Mather provides testimony, including that Hanna forced some of the prisoners to read to her. Hanna admits that she and the co-defendants each chose 10 women monthly for extermination at Auschwitz in Nazi-occupied Poland.
Ilana's mother Rose testifies that when the church caught fire during a bombing, the guards refused to unlock the doors. The official SS report stated that the guards did not know about the fire until the following day, but Hanna reveals that they in fact kept the doors locked so that the prisoners could not escape. Her co-defendants all state she was in command and wrote the report, but she denies this, insisting they agreed on the contents of the report together. When the lead judge asks for a handwriting sample, Hanna quickly condemns herself by admitting she authored the report alone. Recalling their time together, Michael is initially confounded by her testimony, finally deducing that she is deeply ashamed of being illiterate.
Michael informs his law professor, who states that he should inform the court. Deeply conflicted, he attempts to visit Hanna in prison but changes his mind. Hanna receives a sentence of life imprisonment, while her co-defendants are sentenced to just over four years each.
Michael attempts to move on and marries, but cannot commit fully to the relationship and grows distant from his family, culminating in divorce and estrangement from his daughter Julia. Throughout the 1980s, he records himself on tape reading various books and regularly mails them to Hanna. Borrowing the same books from the prison library, Hanna slowly teaches herself to read and write. She starts writing to Michael, but he never replies.

documents.tagline: They proved the Vegas Blackjack System was beatable...by beating the hell out of it.
documents.overview: Ben Campbell is a young, highly intelligent, student at M.I.T. in Boston who strives to succeed. Wanting a scholarship to transfer to Harvard School of Medicine with the desire to become a doctor, Ben learns that he cannot afford the $300,000 for the four to five years of schooling as he comes from a poor, working-class background. But one evening, Ben is introduced by his unorthodox math professor Micky Rosa into a small but secretive club of five. Students Jill, Choi, Kianna, and Fisher, who are being trained by Professor Rosa of the skill of card counting at blackjack.
documents.plot:
"21" is a 2008 American drama film directed by Robert Luketic, starring Jim Sturgess, Kevin Spacey, Kate Bosworth, and Aaron Yoo.

The movie follows the story of Ben Campbell (Jim Sturgess), a young mathematics student who dreams of attending Harvard University. However, his family cannot afford the tuition fees, and he is forced to drop out of college. One day, while working as a waiter at a casino, Ben meets a group of students from MIT, led by Mitchell "Mitch" Rosenthal (Kevin Spacey), who are using card counting techniques to gain an advantage in blackjack.

Ben is initially hesitant but eventually joins the group and learns the complex strategy of card counting. As he becomes more confident in his abilities, Ben starts to use this technique at various casinos, including the Bellagio, where he meets a beautiful woman named Jill Taylor (Kate Bosworth).

As Ben's skills improve, he attracts the attention of casino security, who are determined to catch him and put an end to his card counting activities. Meanwhile, Mitch becomes increasingly obsessed with winning big and starts to take risks that put the entire group in danger.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Ben is caught by the casino security and forced to leave the game. However, he refuses to give up and continues to use his skills to win money for himself and the group. The tension builds as the stakes get higher, and the group faces numerous challenges, including rival card counters and casino security.

In the end, Ben's skills are put to the test when he is invited to play in a high-stakes game at the Bellagio. With the help of his friends and his own determination, Ben emerges victorious, but not without facing some unexpected consequences.

Throughout the movie, the director explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the risks associated with taking advantage of casino games. The film features impressive performances from its cast, particularly Kevin Spacey as the charismatic and ruthless leader of the group.

Overall, "21" is a gripping drama that showcases the complexities of card counting and the high-stakes world of professional gaming. With its engaging storyline and memorable characters, it's no wonder this movie has become a cult classic among fans of thrillers and dramas.

documents.title: Desperado
documents.tagline: When the smoke clears, it just means he's reloading.
documents.overview: Mariachi plunges headfirst into the dark border underworld when he follows a trail of blood to the last of the infamous Mexican drug lords, Bucho, for an action-packed, bullet-riddled showdown. With the help of his best friend and a beautiful bookstore owner, the Mariachi tracks Bucho, takes on his army of desperados, and leaves a trail of blood of his own.
documents.plot: El Mariachi plunges headfirst into the dark border underworld when he follows a trail of blood to the last of the infamous Mexican drug lords, Bucho, for an action-packed, bullet-riddled showdown. With the help of his friend and a beautiful bookstore owner, El Mariachi tracks Bucho, takes on his army of desperados, and leaves his own trail of blood.

documents.title: Alien Resurrection
documents.tagline: It's already too late.
documents.overview: Two hundred years after Lt. Ripley died, a group of scientists clone her, hoping to breed the ultimate weapon. But the new Ripley is full of surprises … as are the new aliens. Ripley must team with a band of smugglers to keep the creatures from reaching Earth.
documents.plot:
Alien Resurrection is a 1997 science fiction action film directed by Jean-Pierre Jeunet, produced by 20th Century Fox, and written by Joss Whedon. The movie takes place 200 years after the events of Alien 3 (1992) and serves as a sequel to the original Alien trilogy.

The story begins in the year 2447, where humanity has colonized other planets. A group of scientists from the Weyland-Yutani Corporation, led by Dr. Charles Bishop Weyland (Lance Henriksen), have discovered a way to clone the alien creatures that terrorize the human colonies. The corporation plans to use these clones as a new source of labor and resources.

The movie follows Ellen Ripley (Sigourney Weaver), who has been in stasis for 200 years, awaiting her execution for killing the alien queen in Alien 3. However, she is rescued by a group of rebels, led by Vriess (Dominique Pinon), who plan to use her as part of their mission to stop Weyland-Yutani's sinister plans.

Ripley soon discovers that the corporation has created a new breed of alien, known as the "Newborn," which is more aggressive and deadly than its predecessors. The Newborns are also capable of regenerating their bodies at an alarming rate, making them nearly impossible to kill.

As Ripley joins forces with Vriess and his team, including Call (Winona Ryder), a young clone who possesses some human-like qualities, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Weyland-Yutani's plans. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, deadly alien creatures, and rival corporations seeking to exploit the Newborns for their own gain.

Throughout the movie, Ripley struggles with her past and her newfound connection to Call, who is revealed to be a clone of herself created by Weyland-Yutani. This revelation raises questions about identity, humanity, and what it means to be alive.

As the story unfolds, Ripley and her team face off against Bishop (Lance Henriksen), who has become a cyborg and serves as Weyland-Yutani's top agent. The final confrontation takes place on a space station, where Ripley and her allies must fight for survival against an army of deadly Newborns.

In the end, Ripley manages to defeat Bishop and destroy the Newborns, but not before Call sacrifices herself to save Ripley. The movie concludes with Ripley, now an old woman, reflecting on her past and the events that have shaped her into the person she is today.

Alien Resurrection received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, with some praising its visuals and action sequences, while others found it lacking in terms of storytelling and character development. However, over the years, the movie has developed a cult following and is now regarded as a unique entry in the Alien franchise.

documents.title: Om Shanti Om
documents.tagline: For some dreams, one lifetime is not enough.
documents.overview: Reincarnated 30 years after being killed in a suspicious on-set fire, a small-time actor is determined to punish the person who ignited the blaze.
documents.plot: In the early 70s, aspiring actor Om Prakash Makhija, and a famous starlet Shantipriya, are murdered. Thirty years later, his reincarnation Om Kapoor sets out to discover the mystery of their demise.

documents.title: Broken Embraces
documents.tagline: Passion, obsession, wealth, jealousy, family, guilt, and creativity.
documents.overview: Harry Caine, a blind writer, reaches this moment in time when he has to heal his wounds from 14 years back. He was then still known by his real name, Mateo Blanco, and directing his last movie.
documents.plot: Harry Caine, a blind writer, reaches this moment in time when he has to heal his wounds from 14 years back. He was then still known by his real name, Mateo Blanco, and directing his last movie.

documents.title: Untraceable
documents.tagline: A cyber killer has finally found the perfect accomplice: You.
documents.overview: Special Agent Jennifer Marsh works in an elite division of the FBI dedicated to fighting cybercrime. She thinks she has seen it all, until a particularly sadistic criminal arises on the Internet. This tech-savvy killer posts live feeds of his crimes on his website; the more hits the site gets, the faster the victim dies. Marsh and her team must find the elusive killer before time runs out.
documents.plot:
Untraceable is a 2008 American psychological thriller directed by Gregory Hoblit and starring Diane Lane, Colin Hanks, Billy Burke and Joseph Cross, with Mary Beth Hurt in a supporting role. Distributed by Screen Gems and set in Portland, Oregon, it centres on a serial killer who builds lethal contraptions linked to a website, so that the more people watch his live stream, the faster his victims die. The film was released in the United States in January 2008 and grossed about 53 million dollars worldwide against a 35 million dollar budget.

Lane plays Jennifer Marsh, a widowed FBI special agent who lives with her young daughter and her mother in a Portland suburb and works night shifts in the bureau's cybercrime division alongside her colleague Griffin Dowd, played by Hanks. Their work usually involves identity theft and online fraud, until an anonymous tip leads them to a website called KillWithMe.com, which streams a video of a kitten being tortured to death. The site cannot be shut down, because every time a server is taken offline a mirror instantly replaces it.

Soon the anonymous webmaster moves on to human victims. Each captive is placed in a death trap that accelerates as the visitor count rises, turning every curious viewer into an accomplice. One man is slowly injected with an anticoagulant, another is cemented to the floor beneath heat lamps. Public warnings only attract more visitors, and the media frenzy feeds the site's popularity. Working with Portland detective Eric Box, played by Burke, Jennifer races to identify the killer, who turns out to be motivated by revenge over the way the internet and media exploited his father's suicide. As the investigation closes in, the killer turns his attention toward the agents themselves, putting Jennifer and her family in danger.

The film offers a commentary on voyeurism and the public's appetite for violent spectacle online, though it also relies heavily on the grisly methods of its murders.

Untraceable was poorly received by critics, many of whom felt it indulged in the very torture voyeurism it set out to condemn and compared it unfavourably with the Saw series, although Lane's performance was generally praised.

documents.title: Napoleon Dynamite
documents.tagline: He's out to prove he's got nothing to prove.
documents.overview: A listless and alienated teenager decides to help his new friend win the class presidency in their small western high school, while he must deal with his bizarre family life back home.
documents.plot:
Socially awkward 16-year-old Napoleon Dynamite lives in Preston, Idaho, United States, with his grandmother, Carlinda, and his technology-addicted older brother, Kip. Napoleon's school days are spent doodling mythical creatures, dealing with bullies, and playing tetherball by himself.
Carlinda breaks her tailbone in a quad bike accident and asks Napoleon's and Kip's uncle Rico to look after things while she recovers. Flirtatious, middle-aged Rico arrives in the camper van he lives in, and teams up with Kip to sell items door-to-door in a get-rich-quick scheme. Kip wants to pay for his online girlfriend, LaFawnduh, to visit from Detroit. Former high-school athlete Rico dwells on his past and dreams of going back in time. He believes wealth will help him get over his breakup with his girlfriend and failed dreams of NFL stardom. Meanwhile, Napoleon takes a job on a chicken farm, but makes very little money.
Napoleon befriends Deb, a shy girl who sells headshots and knick-knacks to raise money for college, and Pedro, a bold transfer student from Juárez, Chihuahua, Mexico. Pedro is rebuffed when he asks the popular and snobby Summer Wheatly to accompany him to the high school dance; Deb gladly accepts. Pedro encourages Napoleon to find a date and he picks popular classmate Trisha. As a gift, he draws an unintentionally bad picture of her and delivers it to Trisha's mother, one of Rico's customers. Rico tells Trisha's mother embarrassing stories about Napoleon to evoke sympathy. She buys his wares and makes Trisha accept Napoleon's invitation. Trisha goes to the dance with Napoleon but abandons him to hang out with Summer and her boyfriend, Don Moser. Pedro allows Napoleon to dance with Deb.
Pedro runs against Summer for class president. The two factions put up flyers and hand out trinkets to attract voters. To demonstrate their "skills" and increase their respect at school, Napoleon and Pedro enter a Future Farmers of America competition, grading milk and cow udders. They win medals, but it does little for their popularity. Pedro becomes stressed to the point where he becomes feverish and shaves his head, subsequently wearing a wig. He later makes a piñata of Summer for fellow students to whack, but is reprimanded by the principal and forced to remove all his campaign flyers. To deal with the bullying, Pedro and Napoleon enlist Pedro's cousins to chase off the bullies.
Napoleon buys an instructional dance videotape, D-Qwon's Dance Grooves. Kip's girlfriend, LaFawnduh, arrives and gives him an urban makeover, outfitting him in hip-hop regalia. Seeing that Napoleon is learning to dance, LaFawnduh gives him a mixtape.
Rico continues to spread embarrassing rumors about Napoleon to prospective customers. He tries to sell Deb a breast-enhancement product, claiming it was Napoleon's suggestion, causing her to break off their friendship. Napoleon confronts Rico and tells him to leave, but Rico refuses.

documents.title: The Quiet American
documents.tagline: In war, the most powerful weapon is seduction.
documents.overview: In early 1950s Vietnam, a young American becomes entangled in a dangerous love triangle when he falls for the beautiful mistress of a British journalist. As war is waged around them, the trio sinks deeper into a world of drugs, passion, and betrayal where nothing is as it seems.
documents.plot:
The Quiet American is a 2002 political drama directed by Phillip Noyce, starring Michael Caine, Brendan Fraser and Đỗ Thị Hải Yến, with Rade Šerbedžija and Tzi Ma in supporting roles. The screenplay by Christopher Hampton and Robert Schenkkan adapts Graham Greene's 1955 novel of the same name. Unlike the 1958 film version, which reversed Greene's warning about foreign intervention into an anticommunist message, the 2002 adaptation is faithful to the novel's portrait of the moral responsibility of American agents involved in violence in Vietnam.

The story is set in Saigon in 1952, during the First Indochina War between French colonial forces and the Communist-led Viet Minh. Thomas Fowler, a world-weary British journalist in his fifties who narrates the film, prides himself on remaining an uninvolved observer of the conflict. He lives with Phuong, a young Vietnamese woman, but cannot marry her because his Catholic wife in England refuses him a divorce. His comfortable life is disrupted when he befriends Alden Pyle, a young, earnest American who claims to be working for an economic aid mission.

Pyle falls in love with Phuong and openly courts her, offering her the marriage and security that Fowler cannot, and a rivalry develops between the two men that remains strangely polite. At the same time Fowler grows suspicious of Pyle's activities. He discovers that the idealistic American is deeply devoted to the theories of a writer who believed Vietnam needed a "Third Force," neither colonial nor communist, and that Pyle is in fact a CIA operative working to create such a force by supporting a renegade militia leader, General Thé. When a bombing in a crowded Saigon square kills and maims many civilians, Fowler realizes the extent of Pyle's involvement and must decide whether he can remain neutral any longer, a choice complicated by his personal stake in Phuong.

The film was completed in 2001, but its release was delayed after the September 11 attacks because of concerns about its critical depiction of American foreign policy; Caine campaigned for it to be shown. It received positive reviews, with an 87 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 84, and critics praised its fidelity to Greene. Caine received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor for his performance as Fowler.

documents.title: The Spiderwick Chronicles
documents.tagline: Their World Is Closer Than You Think
documents.overview: Upon moving into the run-down Spiderwick Estate with their mother, twin brothers Jared and Simon Grace, along with their sister Mallory, find themselves pulled into an alternate world full of faeries and other creatures.
documents.plot:
The Spiderwick Chronicles is a 2008 American fantasy adventure film directed by Mark Waters and written by Karey Kirkpatrick, David Berenbaum and John Sayles, based on the book series by Tony DiTerlizzi and Holly Black. It stars Freddie Highmore in the dual roles of the twins Jared and Simon Grace, Mary-Louise Parker as their mother Helen and Sarah Bolger as their sister Mallory, with David Strathairn as Arthur Spiderwick and Joan Plowright as his daughter Lucinda, and the voices of Nick Nolte as Mulgarath, Seth Rogen as Hogsqueal and Martin Short as Thimbletack.

In 1928, the naturalist Arthur Spiderwick completes a field guide documenting the hidden world of fairies and magical creatures he has observed. Fearing that the evil shapeshifting ogre Mulgarath will use its secrets to gain power over all creatures, he hides the book away. Eighty years later, the recently divorced Helen Grace moves with her children, thirteen-year-old Mallory and nine-year-old twins Jared and Simon, into the dilapidated Spiderwick estate in New England. Jared, angry about the move and wishing he could live with his father in New York, discovers a secret study and finds Arthur's field guide, despite a warning not to read it.

No one in the family believes Jared's stories about magical beings until strange events begin to occur. Thimbletack, a house brownie who has guarded the book for decades, reveals that opening it has alerted Mulgarath, who wants the guide at any cost. The house is protected by a circle of mushrooms, but when Simon is abducted by Mulgarath's goblins, Jared sets out to rescue him and meets Hogsqueal, a hobgoblin who wants revenge on the ogre. As the family realizes the danger is real, the children must work together to protect the book, uncover what happened to Arthur Spiderwick and defend their home from Mulgarath's army.

The film combines live action with computer-generated creatures, and it explores themes of family, divorce and trust between siblings.

The Spiderwick Chronicles was released in February 2008 and grossed about 162.8 million dollars worldwide. It received generally positive reviews, with 81 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 62.

documents.title: Welcome to the Sticks
documents.overview: Although living a comfortable life in Salon-de-Provence, a charming town in the South of France, Julie has been feeling depressed for a while. To please her, Philippe Abrams, a post office administrator, her husband, tries to obtain a transfer to a seaside town, on the French Riviera, at any cost. The trouble is that he is caught red-handed while trying to scam an inspector. Philippe is immediately banished to the distant unheard of town of Bergues, in the Far North of France...
documents.plot:
Welcome to the Sticks (French: Bienvenue chez les Ch'tis) is a 2008 French comedy film directed and co-written by Dany Boon, who stars alongside Kad Merad, Zoé Félix and Anne Marivin, with Line Renaud and Michel Galabru in supporting roles. A comedy about the clash between the sunny south of France and the stereotypically grim north, it became a phenomenon at home and is the highest-grossing French film ever released in France.

Philippe Abrams runs the post office in Salon-de-Provence and is desperate to obtain a transfer to a seaside town on the Riviera to please his discontented wife, Julie. Believing that disabled applicants are favoured, he fakes a disability during an inspection, is caught, and is punished with a two-year posting to Bergues, a small town near Dunkirk in the Nord-Pas-de-Calais. Southerners regard the region as a frozen, rainy backwater inhabited by uncouth Ch'tis who speak an incomprehensible dialect, and Philippe heads north full of dread, leaving his wife and young son behind.

His first night is spent at the home of Antoine Bailleul, a postman who also plays the town's carillon and who lives with his domineering mother. Despite a rocky start, the two become close friends, and Philippe is gradually won over by the warmth of his colleagues and neighbours. He joins Antoine on his rounds, accepting drinks at every door, learns to enjoy strong Maroilles cheese and local beer, and even attends an RC Lens football match. Julie, however, refuses to believe that he could be happy there, so he tells her what she expects to hear, describing the north as miserable.

When Julie announces she is coming to support him, Philippe confesses his lies to his friends. Annoyed at first, they agree to help by acting like barbarians and lodging her in a bleak former mining village presented as Bergues. Julie is shaken but resolves to stay, until she discovers the deception. Philippe admits how happy he has been, and she accepts it. Meanwhile, Philippe urges the timid Antoine to stand up to his mother and win back his former girlfriend Annabelle, whom he proposes to from the bell tower. When Philippe is finally transferred south years later, he weeps at leaving, just as a local saying predicted.

Released in February 2008, the film earned around 193 million dollars in France and positive reviews.

documents.title: Disturbia
documents.tagline: The quieter the street, the darker the secrets....
documents.overview: Kale is a 17-year-old placed under house arrest after punching his teacher. He is confined to his house, and decides to use his free time spying on his neighbors. Things start to get weird when guests enter the Turner's house and don't come back out. Kale and his friends, Ronnie and Ashley, start to grow more and more interested in what is actually happening within the house of Robert Turner.
documents.plot: Kale has a life most teenagers would envy. He spends his days endlessly playing video games, surfing the net, eating junk food and watching cable. He has complete free reign of the house, and a beautiful young hottie named Ashley has just moved in next door. There’s only one problem—he’s not allowed to leave the house. Kale’s under court-ordered house arrest for three months, and if he takes one step beyond a 100-foot perimeter of the house, his next confinement will be in a real prison.

documents.title: American Wedding
documents.tagline: Forever hold your piece.
documents.overview: With high school a distant memory, Jim and Michelle are getting married -- and in a hurry, since Jim's grandmother is sick and wants to see him walk down the aisle -- prompting Stifler to throw the ultimate bachelor party. And Jim's dad is reliable as ever, doling out advice no one wants to hear.
documents.plot:
American Wedding is a 2003 American romantic comedy film directed by Ron Howard and written by Greg DePaul and Andrew Jacobson. The movie is the third installment in the American Pie franchise.

The story begins with Jim Levenstein (Jason Biggs), now engaged to his high school sweetheart, Michelle Flaherty (Alyson Hannigan). However, their wedding plans are put on hold when Michelle's parents, Harry (Ted Danson) and Nancy (Molly Shannon), announce that they want to meet Jim before the big day.

As Jim tries to navigate this new development, he also has to deal with his friends' attempts to help him prepare for marriage. His friend Oz (Erik Stolhanske) is particularly enthusiastic about the wedding, while another friend, Kevin (Thomas Ian Nicholas), is more skeptical.

Meanwhile, Michelle's parents are trying to get to know Jim better, but their interactions are often awkward and humorous. Harry, in particular, is a lovable but eccentric character who becomes fast friends with Jim's father, Frank (Greg Kinnear).

As the wedding date approaches, Jim starts to feel the pressure of meeting his future in-laws' expectations. He also has to deal with some unexpected surprises, including a surprise visit from an old flame, Audrey (Jennifer Coolidge), and a series of mishaps that threaten to derail the wedding.

Despite these challenges, Jim and Michelle's love for each other remains strong, and they work together to overcome their differences and make their relationship work. The movie culminates in a hilarious and heartwarming ceremony, where Jim and Michelle finally tie the knot.

Throughout the film, there are plenty of comedic moments, thanks to the witty banter between the characters and the absurd situations they find themselves in. However, American Wedding also has its share of heartfelt moments, particularly when it comes to the relationships between the characters.

Overall, American Wedding is a fun and entertaining movie that explores the ups and downs of marriage and relationships. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and hilarious antics, it's a great addition to the American Pie franchise.

documents.title: American Pie Presents: Band Camp
documents.tagline: This One Time at Band Camp...
documents.overview: Everyone has 'moved on', except for Sherman and Jim Levenstein's still understanding father. Little Matt Stiffler wants to join his older brother Steve's business and, after everything Matt has heard from Jim's band-geek wife, he plans to go back to band camp and make a video of his own.
documents.plot:
Matt Stifler, the younger brother of Steve Stifler, is eager to enter a family business of making pornographic films to prove his "Stifmeister" behavior to his older brother, Steve.
After Matt pulls a prank on the school band that goes too far, the school's guidance counselor Chuck "The Sherminator" Sherman, who attended high school with Steve, punishes Matt by sending him to band camp. Matt is initially dismissive of the idea, but is soon persuaded to agree, his interest piqued by the purportedly notorious sexual behavior of band camp girls.
Upon arrival, Matt is highly disrespectful of the rules and to everyone at Tall Oaks, and even gets his school's band in trouble. Jim's dad, Noah Levenstein, the camp's MACRO (Morale and Conflict Resolution Officer), recommends he try to fit in to win the band's trust. Matt conspires with his nerdy roommate Ernie to film the other band members in a bid called 'Bandeez Gone Wild' using hidden cameras. During a scuffle in the lunchroom, Matt accepts a duel with the rival band leader Brandon Vandecamp, wherein the performers show off their music skills, with Brandon playing the snare drum, and Matt playing the triangle. When it seems Matt has lost, he leaves the stage and comes back playing the bagpipes, also wearing a kilt, to the tune of "Play That Funky Music" to win the duel. Matt befriends Elyse; they are later attracted to each other and kiss while watching clouds.
A day before the finals, the East Great Falls cheerleading squad arrives and catches Matt in a band camp uniform. They tease him, taking a photo and planning to share it online. Matt later offers to show them his film 'Bandeez Gone Wild' in exchange for deleting the photo. While Matt is showing them his video, Elyse turns up after he had unintentionally stood her up. Disappointed with him for making the video, she leaves. The various school bands compete for points throughout camp, with East Great Falls leading on the last day, but an ill-fated prank Matt meant for the rival team causes the band to lose and Elyse to lose her opportunity for a scholarship.
Once the new term starts, Matt visits Chuck, who reveals that he and Steve's other friends could not stand him. Matt soon begins to fix his mistakes by deleting the naked videos he took of others at band camp, reconciling with his band camp buddies, and then persuading the school band to play Elyse's piece, Instrumental of Tal Bachman's Aeroplane, for the Conservatory head. Due to blatant plagiarism, Brandon was disqualified, so Elyse won the scholarship, while Matt successfully won her affection, getting healed in the process.

documents.title: American Pie Presents: Beta House
documents.tagline: The most outrageous slice of pie!
documents.overview: Erik, Ryan, and Cooze start college and pledge the Beta House fraternity, presided over by none other than legendary Dwight Stifler. But chaos ensues when a fraternity of geeks threatens to stop the debauchery and the Betas have to make a stand for their right to party.
documents.plot:
American Pie Presents: Beta House is a 2007 American comedy film directed by Jesse Dylan and written by Adam Herz. The movie is part of the American Pie franchise, which follows the lives of a group of high school friends as they navigate love, relationships, and growing up.

The plot takes place after the events of American Wedding (2003) and follows Jim Levenstein (Eddie Kaye Thomas), who has just been accepted into a prestigious college called Beta House. The movie begins with Jim arriving at Beta House, where he meets his new roommate, Matt (John White), and becomes fast friends with him.

However, things take a turn when the house is taken over by a group of misfits, led by a charismatic but troubled student named Steve Stills (Adam Pally). As Jim tries to navigate this new environment, he finds himself caught up in a series of wacky misadventures and pranks with his new friends.

Meanwhile, Jim's on-again, off-again girlfriend, Michelle Flaherty (Amanda Crew), is dealing with her own issues as she navigates college life. The movie also features appearances from several familiar faces from the American Pie franchise, including Stifler (Seann William Scott) and Oz (Erik Stolhanske).

As the story unfolds, Jim becomes increasingly frustrated with Steve's antics and tries to assert his authority in the house. However, things escalate when Steve starts a series of pranks that put the entire house at risk.

In the end, Jim must confront Steve and find a way to restore order to Beta House. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and growing up.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, including several memorable scenes featuring Stifler's antics and Oz's deadpan reactions. The film also explores themes of identity, belonging, and finding one's place in the world.

Overall, American Pie Presents: Beta House is a lighthearted, entertaining comedy that provides plenty of laughs and nostalgic value for fans of the franchise.

documents.title: The Spirit
documents.tagline: My city screams.
documents.overview: Down these mean streets a man must come.  A hero born, murdered, and born again.  A Rookie cop named Denny Colt returns from the beyond as The Spirit, a hero whose mission is to fight against the bad forces from the shadows of Central City.  The Octopus, who kills anyone unfortunate enough to see his face, has other plans; he is going to wipe out the entire city.
documents.plot:
The Spirit is an American neo-noir superhero film of 2008 written and directed by Frank Miller from Will Eisner's comic series. Gabriel Macht plays Denny Colt, a slain policeman reborn as the masked crime-fighter the Spirit, with Samuel L. Jackson as the villain the Octopus, Scarlett Johansson as his accomplice Silken Floss, Eva Mendes as the jewel thief Sand Saref, Sarah Paulson as Dr Ellen Dolan, Dan Lauria as Commissioner Dolan, Paz Vega as the assassin Plaster of Paris and Jaime King as Lorelei, the Angel of Death.

Alerted to a case involving the Octopus, the Spirit races across the rooftops of Central City to a swamp where the femme fatale Sand Saref has shot a detective. Sand and her husband had recovered two chests from the water; she escaped with one, but the Octopus seized the other. The Octopus beheads Officer Liebowitz, his cloned henchmen attack, and the two foes fight as Floss flees with the chest. The Spirit wakes the next day in the care of his lover Ellen, his gunshot wounds healed, holding a locket torn from Sand's neck that he once gave her: they were childhood sweethearts, and she left the city fifteen years earlier after her police officer father was killed. The Octopus finds his chest holds the Golden Fleece rather than the Blood of Heracles he wanted, while Sand, now one of the world's great jewel thieves, has the vase of blood.

Captured in the Octopus's lair, the Spirit learns that the villain created an immortality serum, first tested on Colt's corpse, which explains his return from the dead and Death's grudge against him; the Octopus has injected himself too but needs the demigod's blood to perfect it. The Spirit escapes by seducing Plaster of Paris, who stabs him when he mentions Sand. Collapsing into the harbour, he faces Lorelei but swims back to life. At an exchange between Sand and Floss, the Octopus tries to destroy the Spirit with ever larger guns until police storm in; Sand shoots the vase of blood, and the Spirit, saved by a bulletproof vest, blows the Octopus up with a grenade while the Golden Fleece shields them. He returns Sand's locket and persuades Dolan to let her go, while Floss leaves with one of the Octopus's severed, crawling fingers, and the Spirit reconciles with Ellen.

Released by Lionsgate in December 2008, the film grossed $38.4 million worldwide and was panned by critics, with 14% on Rotten Tomatoes, who found its visuals distinctive but its plot nearly incomprehensible.

documents.title: Four Brothers
documents.tagline: They came home to bury mom... and her killer
documents.overview: Four adopted brothers return to their Detroit hometown when their mother is murdered and vow to exact revenge on the killers.
documents.plot:
Four Brothers is a 2005 American action drama film directed by John Hillcoat and written by David McKenna. The movie stars Mark Wahlberg, Tyrese Gibson, André Benjamin, Garrett Hedlund, and Terence Howard.

The story begins with the death of the four brothers' father, William "Big Daddy" Wharton (Don Johnson), who was a Vietnam War veteran and a former police officer. The family is shocked by his sudden passing, which sets off a chain reaction of events that exposes long-buried secrets and unresolved conflicts within the family.

The movie then shifts to the present day, where we meet the four brothers: Bobby (Mark Wahlberg), Angel (Tyrese Gibson), Jeremiah (André Benjamin), and Jack (Garrett Hedlund). Each brother has a unique personality and struggles with their own demons. Bobby is a cop in Detroit; Angel is a small-time crook; Jeremiah is a preacher; and Jack is a young, troubled teenager.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Big Daddy's death was not an accident, but rather a murder orchestrated by a group of ruthless gangsters who have been terrorizing the city. The brothers soon discover that their father's killer is none other than their own uncle, Frank Wharton (Terence Howard), who has been seeking revenge against his family for years.

The four brothers embark on a perilous journey to avenge their father's death and bring justice to those responsible. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including corrupt police officers, gangsters, and even some of their own family members.

As the plot thickens, we see flashbacks of Big Daddy's past, which reveal his complicated relationships with his sons and his struggles as a veteran trying to adjust to civilian life. These flashbacks provide insight into the brothers' motivations and help explain why they are so driven to seek revenge against Frank Wharton.

The movie builds towards an intense showdown between the four brothers and their uncle, which culminates in a bloody and violent confrontation. In the end, only one brother is left standing, and he must come to terms with the consequences of his actions and the true cost of seeking revenge.

Throughout the film, director John Hillcoat uses gritty realism and stunning cinematography to bring the story to life. The movie's score, composed by Mark Isham, adds to the tension and emotional depth of the narrative.

Overall, Four Brothers is a gripping and intense action drama that explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption. With its strong performances, engaging storyline, and visceral action sequences, it has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: Howards End
documents.tagline: Based on the Novel by E.M. Forster
documents.overview: A saga of class relations and changing times in an Edwardian England on the brink of modernity, the film centers on liberal Margaret Schlegel, who, along with her sister Helen, becomes involved with two couples: wealthy, conservative industrialist Henry Wilcox and his wife Ruth, and the downwardly mobile working-class Leonard Bast and his mistress Jackie.
documents.plot:
In Edwardian Britain, Helen Schlegel becomes engaged to Paul Wilcox during a moment of passion while staying at the Wilcox family's country home, Howards End. The Schlegels are an intellectual Anglo-German bourgeois family, while the Wilcoxes, led by hard-headed businessman Henry, are conservative and wealthy. Helen and Paul quickly decide against the engagement, but she has already sent a telegram informing her sister Margaret, leading to an uproar when the sisters' Aunt Juley arrives and causes a scene.
Months later in London, the Wilcoxes take a flat across the street from the Schlegels, whom they had met the previous year in Germany, and Margaret resumes her acquaintance with Ruth, Henry's wife. Howards End is owned by Ruth, and is her beloved childhood home, inherited from her family. The two women grow close as Mrs. Wilcox's health declines and, unbeknownst to Margaret, Ruth bequeaths Howards End to her on her deathbed. However, the Wilcoxes refuse to believe Ruth would leave the house to a relative stranger, and burn her informally-written directions. Henry develops an attraction to Margaret, assisting her in finding a new home and eventually proposing marriage, which she accepts.
The Schlegels have befriended Leonard Bast, a self-improving young clerk who lives with Jacky, a woman of dubious origins. The sisters pass along advice from Henry that the insurance company Leonard works for is heading for bankruptcy. As a result, Leonard quits and settles for a much lower-paying job, which is eventually eliminated leaving him without employment. Helen is later appalled to learn Henry's advice was wrong – Leonard's first employer was perfectly sound but will not re-employ him – and is enraged by Henry's indifference.
Months later, Henry and Margaret host the wedding of his daughter Evie at his Shropshire estate. Margaret is shocked when Helen arrives with the impoverished Leonard and Jacky. Considering Henry responsible for their plight, Helen demands his help, but Jacky drunkenly exposes Henry as a former lover from years ago. Henry is ashamed to be revealed as an adulterer, but Margaret forgives him and agrees to send the Basts away. Helen, upset with Margaret's decision to marry a man she now loathes, leaves for Germany, but not before giving in to her attraction for Leonard and having sex while out boating. Fearing the Basts will be penniless, Helen instructs her brother Tibby to give them over £5000 of her own money, but Leonard returns the cheque uncashed out of pride, and because of his own feelings for Helen.
Margaret and Henry marry, arranging to use Howards End as storage for Margaret's and her siblings' belongings. After months of hearing from Helen only through postcards, Margaret grows concerned. Helen returns to England when Aunt Juley falls ill, but avoids seeing her family.

documents.title: The Countess
documents.tagline: She sacrificed all for love and others for beauty
documents.overview: Kingdom of Hungary, 17th century. As she gets older, powerful Countess Erzsébet Báthory (1560-1614), blinded by the passion that she feels for a younger man, succumbs to the mad delusion that blood will keep her young and beautiful forever.
documents.plot:
The Countess is a 2009 French-German historical drama written and directed by Julie Delpy, who also composed its score and stars in the title role. Based on the life of the notorious Hungarian noblewoman Elizabeth Báthory, it co-stars Daniel Brühl as István Thurzó and William Hurt as his father, Count György Thurzó. It was Delpy's third feature as a director, and she described it as less a gothic tale than a drama about the psychology of people who are given power.

Elizabeth Báthory is born in 1560 into one of the most powerful noble families of Hungary and is raised from childhood to accept harshness and cruelty as part of her station. As a teenager she becomes pregnant by a young peasant, whom she is forced to watch being tortured and killed, and her child is taken from her immediately after birth. She is later married to Count Ferenc Nádasdy and has children with him. When Nádasdy dies of an illness contracted during the wars against the Ottomans, Elizabeth inherits his vast estates and becomes one of the wealthiest and most powerful people in the kingdom, to the point that the Habsburg ruler Matthias is deeply in debt to her.

At a ball, Elizabeth meets István, the twenty-one-year-old son of Count Thurzó, and the two fall passionately in love. György Thurzó, however, forces his son to break off the relationship and marry the daughter of a wealthy merchant. Devastated, the aging Elizabeth becomes convinced that their age difference destroyed the affair. When she is splashed with blood after striking a servant girl and is told by her flattering attendants that her skin looks younger, she begins to believe that bathing in the blood of virgins can preserve her youth and beauty. Her servants start abducting and killing young peasant women to obtain their blood, until the disappearances can no longer be ignored and Thurzó, who has political and financial reasons to bring her down, leads an investigation into her crimes.

Delpy approaches the legend as a psychological drama about power, vanity and the fear of aging. Found guilty, Elizabeth is spared execution because of her noble birth and is instead walled into her room at Čachtice Castle for the rest of her life.

The Countess premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival on 9 February 2009. It received largely negative reviews; Variety's Boyd van Hoeij wrote that although some individual moments work, the screenplay lacks psychological connective tissue.

documents.title: In Bruges
documents.tagline: Shoot first. Sightsee later.
documents.overview: Ray and Ken, two hit men, are in Bruges, Belgium, waiting for their next mission. While they are there they have time to think and discuss their previous assignment. When the mission is revealed to Ken, it is not what he expected.
documents.plot:
Carrying out his first order, inexperienced hitman Ray shoots a priest during confession, but accidentally kills an altar boy standing in the line of fire. He and his mentor Ken are sent by their boss, Harry, to hide in Bruges, where they are to sightsee and await further instruction. Ken finds the city beautiful and relaxing, while Ray is bored and hates it.
They chance upon a film shoot involving a dwarf actor named Jimmy; this amuses Ray. Ray is attracted to Chloë, a local drug dealer moonlighting as a production assistant. He takes her to a restaurant, where he gets into an argument with a Canadian couple over smoking indoors and punches them. Chloë takes Ray to her apartment where they begin to have foreplay, but her ex-boyfriend Eirik appears and threatens Ray with a handgun. Ray effortlessly disarms the small-time criminal and fires the gun, loaded with blanks, in Eirik's face, blinding him in one eye. Chloë admits that she and Eirik rob tourists, but insists she had told Eirik that Ray was not a target. As Chloë drives Eirik to the hospital, Ray pockets the gun and helps himself to a handful of live rounds as well as Chloë's stash of drugs. He and Ken spend a debauched night with Jimmy, who takes cocaine and rants about a coming war between blacks and whites.
Harry calls Ken and reveals that the trip was an attempt to give Ray a good experience before he dies. He orders Ken to kill Ray, on the principle that killing a child, even accidentally, is unforgivable. With a handgun supplied by Harry's local contact Yuri, Ken tracks Ray to a park and reluctantly prepares to kill him. Ray, however, distraught at his killing of the boy, prepares to kill himself with Eirik's loaded gun. Seeing this, Ken stops Ray, informs him of Harry's order and tells him to leave Bruges to have a fresh start. He gives Ray some money and puts him on a train to another city, while confiscating his gun to prevent a further suicide attempt. Ken phones Harry to tell him the truth, and Harry immediately sets out for Bruges, furious at the insubordination. He picks up a pistol and a box of dumdum bullets at Yuri's, and Eirik learns of his intention.
Meanwhile, police stop Ray's train in the Belgian countryside; they detain Ray for attacking the Canadians and escort him back to Bruges. Chloë bails him out and the two share a drink on the market square beneath the Belfry of Bruges. Meanwhile, Harry spots Ken at a café. As the two have drinks, Harry boasts that if he himself had killed a child, he would have immediately taken his own life. Ken argues that Ray is trying to better himself and deserves a chance at redemption, but Harry is not convinced. Ken suggests they ascend the bell tower for a shootout away from bystanders. At the top, Ken says he accepts whatever punishment Harry intends. A conflicted Harry cannot bring himself to kill Ken, so he shoots him in the leg as punishment for not killing Ray. Eirik crosses the market square and sees Ray and Chloë on a date.

documents.title: Fast Food Nation
documents.tagline: Do you want lies with that?
documents.overview: A dramatised examination of the health issues and social consequences of America's love affair with fast food.
documents.plot:
Fast Food Nation is a 2006 drama directed by Richard Linklater, who wrote it with Eric Schlosser as a loose adaptation of Schlosser's 2001 non-fiction book. It tells interlocking stories about the fast food industry. Greg Kinnear plays Don Anderson, Ashley Johnson plays Amber, Catalina Sandino Moreno plays Sylvia, Wilmer Valderrama plays Raúl and Bobby Cannavale plays Mike. Bruce Willis, Kris Kristofferson and Ethan Hawke also appear.

Don, marketing director of the Mickey's burger chain, helped create its hit "Big One". When independent tests find fecal matter in the meat, he travels to the fictional town of Cody, Colorado, to inspect Uni-Globe, the chain's main meat supplier. Shown only spotless areas, he seeks out Rudy, a rancher who once supplied the plant, and learns that safety rules are ignored to keep up production, letting manure reach the meat. A Mickey's executive, Rydell, admits knowing but does not care.

Amber, a cheerful Mickey's employee saving for college, lives with her mother Cindy. Her uncle Pete urges her to leave town and pursue a real future. Amber falls in with young activists who plan to free cattle from Uni-Globe, but when they tear down a fence, the animals refuse to leave their pen. Meanwhile, Raúl, his girlfriend Sylvia and her sister Coco cross illegally from Mexico and seek work at the plant. Raúl becomes a cleaner and Coco works on the processing line, while Sylvia, unable to bear the conditions, takes a job as a hotel maid. Coco develops a drug habit and begins an affair with Mike, their exploitative supervisor. When a co-worker's leg is mangled in a machine, Raúl is badly injured trying to save him, and Sylvia is told he was on amphetamines. With Raúl unable to work, Sylvia sleeps with Mike to get a job at the plant. She is assigned to the kill floor, and as cattle are slaughtered around her, she breaks down in tears at what her life has become.

Schlosser preferred a fictional feature to a documentary, and he and Linklater modeled its structure on Winesburg, Ohio. The film was shot in Texas, Colorado and Mexico. It premiered in competition at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival and was released by Fox Searchlight on November 17, 2006, grossing about $2.2 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 49% approval, judging the book more effective than the film, while A. O. Scott of The New York Times called it a rich critique of American life, as necessary and nourishing as a meal.

documents.title: Holes
documents.tagline: Some secrets are too big to keep hidden.
documents.overview: A wrongfully convicted boy is sent to a brutal desert detention camp where he must dig holes in order to build character. What he doesn't know is that he is digging holes in order to search for a lost treasure hidden somewhere in the camp.
documents.plot: After being wrongfully convicted for stealing a pair of shoes, Stanley Yelnats is sent away to Camp Green Lake, a boys detention facility where inmates are forced to dig holes all day in the hot desert sun as a form of character building. As he endures the brutal routine, Stanley begins to uncover a hidden truth behind the camp, one that connects to a dangerous secret—and possibly Stanley’s family itself.

documents.title: Step Up 2: The Streets
documents.tagline: It's not where you're from. It's where you're at.
documents.overview: When rebellious street dancer Andie lands at the elite Maryland School of the Arts, she finds herself fighting to fit in while also trying to hold onto her old life. When she joins forces with the schools hottest dancer, Chase, to form a crew of classmate outcasts to compete in Baltimore s underground dance battle The Streets.
documents.plot:
Step Up 2: The Streets is a 2008 American dance drama film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by John Stockwell. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2006 film Step Up, which was also produced by Summit Entertainment.

The story takes place in Baltimore, Maryland, where Tyler Gage (played by Jeremias Foote) is now living with his mother, who has just been released from prison. Tyler's life is turned upside down when he meets Nora (played by Cassie Scerbo), a beautiful and talented dancer at the local community center.

Nora is struggling to find her place in the world after being kicked out of her previous dance studio for not conforming to their rules. She finds solace in dancing on the streets with her friends, who are part of an underground dance crew called "The Streets." The group's leader, a charismatic and talented dancer named Andree (played by Chris Brown), becomes Nora's mentor and friend.

As Tyler and Nora spend more time together, they begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their relationship is put to the test when Tyler's past comes back to haunt him in the form of his ex-girlfriend, Eva (played by Brenda Song). Eva is now dating a wealthy businessman who wants her to leave her dance career behind.

Meanwhile, The Streets are facing a threat from a rival dance crew called "The Kings," who are led by a ruthless and arrogant dancer named Chase (played by Robert Buckley). The Kings are determined to take over the streets and eliminate The Streets as a threat.

As tensions between The Streets and The Kings escalate, Tyler and Nora find themselves at the center of the conflict. They must use their dance skills to outdo The Kings and prove that they have what it takes to be part of the dance community.

In the end, Tyler and Nora's relationship is put to the test as they face off against Chase and his crew in an epic dance battle. With the help of Andree and The Streets, they manage to defeat The Kings and emerge victorious.

The movie ends with Tyler and Nora sharing a romantic moment, and The Streets celebrating their victory. The film concludes on a high note, with the message that dance has the power to bring people together and transcend social boundaries.

Overall, Step Up 2: The Streets is a fun and energetic movie that showcases the beauty of street dancing. With its talented cast, catchy soundtrack, and pulse-pounding dance sequences, it's sure to get you moving and grooving along with the characters.

documents.title: [REC]
documents.tagline: One witness. One camera
documents.overview: A television reporter and cameraman follow emergency workers into a dark apartment building and are quickly locked inside with something terrifying.
documents.plot:
[REC] is a Spanish horror film directed by Jaume Balagueró and Paco Plaza, released in 2007. The movie takes place in modern-day Barcelona, Spain.

The story begins with Angela Vidal (Manuela Velasco), a television reporter who is assigned to cover a typical day at the local fire station. She is accompanied by her cameraman, Pablo (David Verdu), and her producer, Isabella (Leticia Dolz). The crew arrives at the fire station, where they meet the firefighters, including Urtain (Carlos Lasplena) and his team.

As Angela begins to film the day's activities, she meets Tomás (Christian Stürmer), a firefighter who is recovering from an injury. She also meets Isabella's boyfriend, Pablo's brother, and his girlfriend, but they are not part of the main storyline.

The story takes a turn when Angela discovers that one of the firefighters has been bitten by a mysterious creature while responding to a call. The creature is later revealed to be a zombie-like being infected with a deadly virus. As the day progresses, more and more people become infected, and the situation spirals out of control.

Angela's producer, Isabella, becomes increasingly unhinged as she realizes that the fire station is under attack by the infected. She tries to escape, but her attempts are thwarted by the growing chaos. Meanwhile, Angela and Tomás try to find a way to stop the outbreak and save as many people as possible.

As the night wears on, the situation becomes more desperate. The firefighters are vastly outnumbered, and the infected continue to spread. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Urtain, one of the firefighters, has been hiding a dark secret: he is actually the source of the outbreak.

In the climactic final act, Angela and Tomás make a desperate bid to escape the fire station. They fight their way through hordes of infected, using whatever they can find to defend themselves. In the end, only one person survives: Angela.

The movie ends with Angela, traumatized by what she has witnessed, being taken away from the fire station in an ambulance. As she looks back at the burning building, it is clear that she will never be the same again.

[REC] is a tense, suspenseful horror film that explores themes of isolation, paranoia, and the breakdown of social order in the face of catastrophic disaster. The movie's use of found footage adds to the sense of realism and immediacy, making the viewer feel like they are experiencing the events firsthand.

documents.title: Blindness
documents.tagline: Your vision of the world will change forever.
documents.overview: When a sudden plague of blindness devastates a city, a small group of the afflicted band together to triumphantly overcome the horrific conditions of their imposed quarantine.
documents.plot:
The film begins with a young professional suddenly going blind in his car while at an intersection, with his field of vision turning white. A seemingly kind passerby offers to drive him home. However, he then steals the blind man's car. When the blind man's wife returns home, she takes him to an ophthalmologist who can identify nothing wrong and refers him for further evaluation.
The next day, the doctor goes blind, and recognizes that the blindness must be caused by a communicable disease. Around the city, more citizens are struck blind, causing widespread panic, and the government organizes a quarantine for the blind in a derelict asylum. When a hazmat crew arrives to pick up the doctor, his wife lies that she has also gone blind in order to accompany him.
In the asylum, the doctor and his wife are first to arrive and agree they will keep her sight a secret. They are joined by several others, including the driver, the thief, and other patients of the doctor. At this point, the "white sickness" has become international, with hundreds of cases reported every day. The government is resorting to increasingly ruthless measures to try to deal with the epidemic, including refusing aid to the blind.
As more blinded people are crammed into what has become a concentration camp, overcrowding and lack of outside support cause hygiene and living conditions to quickly degrade. The doctor serves as the representative of his ward, and his sighted wife does what she can to assist her fellow inmates without revealing her ability. Anxiety over the availability of food undermines morale and introduces conflict between the prison's wards, as the soldiers who guard the camp become increasingly hostile.
A man with a handgun appoints himself "king" of his ward, and takes control of the food deliveries, first demanding the other wards' valuables, and then for the women to have sex with their men. In an effort to obtain necessities, several women reluctantly submit to being raped. One of the women is killed by her assailant, and the doctor's wife retaliates, killing the "king" with a pair of scissors. Independently, other raped women sneak to the dead king's ward and set it on fire, which rapidly engulfs the building, with many inmates dying in the ensuing chaos. The survivors who escape the building discover that the guards have abandoned their posts, and they venture out into the city.
Society has collapsed, with the city's population reduced to an aimless, zombie-like struggle to survive. The doctor's wife leads her husband and a few others from their ward in search of food and shelter. She discovers a well-stocked basement storeroom beneath a grocery store, barely escaping with aid from her husband when the throng around her smell the fresh food she is carrying.
The doctor and his wife invite their new "family" to their apartment, where they establish a mutually supportive long-term home.

documents.title: No Man's Land
documents.tagline: A lot can happen between the lines
documents.overview: Two soldiers from opposite sites get stuck between the front lines in the same trench. The UN is asked to free them and both sides agree on a ceasefire, but will they stick to it?
documents.plot:
No Man's Land (Serbo-Croatian: Ničija zemlja) is a 2001 war film set during the Bosnian War, written and directed by Danis Tanović in his feature debut. Described as a parable, it was a co-production between companies in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Slovenia, Italy, France, Belgium and the United Kingdom. Branko Đurić stars as Čiki, a Bosniak soldier, and Rene Bitorajac as Nino, a Bosnian Serb, with Filip Šovagović as Cera, Georges Siatidis as Sergeant Marchand, Simon Callow as Colonel Soft and Katrin Cartlidge as the journalist Jane Livingstone.

At the height of the war, two wounded soldiers from opposing sides, Čiki and Nino, find themselves trapped together in a trench in the no man's land between the front lines, where they must wait for darkness. At first they trade insults and threats, but gradually they begin to find some common ground. The situation becomes even more precarious when Cera, another wounded Bosniak soldier, regains consciousness and discovers that Bosnian Serb troops have placed a land mine beneath his body, set to explode if he moves. Sergeant Marchand, a French officer with the United Nations Protection Force, tries to help the three men despite orders from his superiors to stay out of it, since UNPROFOR's mandate is to protect humanitarian convoys and remain neutral. Only when a British reporter arrives and media pressure mounts does the UN high command spring into action to try to save the soldiers. As the day wears on, the exhausted and frightened Čiki and Nino continue to quarrel, their hostility escalating even after help arrives, while a mine expert struggles with the device beneath Cera. The film builds toward a bleak conclusion that exposes the absurdity of the conflict and the hollowness of the international response, in which saving face proves more important than saving lives.

No Man's Land won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film and the Golden Globe for Best Foreign Language Film, as well as the award for best screenplay at the 2001 Cannes Film Festival and from the European Film Academy. It received widespread acclaim, holding a 93% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it bleak and darkly humorous in illustrating the absurdity of war, and a Metacritic score of 84. It earned about $4.9 million worldwide.
production_companies: The Centre du Cinema et de l'Audiovisuel de la Communauté Française de Belgique
Direction du Développement et de la Coopération (DDC), Département Fédéral des Affaires Etrangères

documents.title: My Big Fat Greek Wedding
documents.tagline: Love is here to stay... so is her family.
documents.overview: A young Greek woman falls in love with a non-Greek and struggles to get her family to accept him while she comes to terms with her heritage and cultural identity.
documents.plot:
My Big Fat Greek Wedding is a 2002 romantic comedy directed by Joel Zwick and written by Nia Vardalos, adapted from her one-woman stage show. Vardalos stars as Toula Portokalos, with John Corbett, Lainie Kazan, Michael Constantine, Gia Carides, Louis Mandylor, Andrea Martin and Joey Fatone. Produced in part by Tom Hanks, Rita Wilson and Gary Goetzman, the American and Canadian co-production premiered at the American Film Market in February 2002 and was released in the United States by IFC Films on 19 April 2002.

In Chicago, thirty-year-old Fotoula "Toula" Portokalos belongs to a large, loud and overbearing Greek-American family. Her father, Gus, is desperate for her to marry a Greek man and start a family, and he is fond of tracing every word in English back to Greek. Toula works as a hostess at the family's restaurant, Dancing Zorba's, and longs for independence. One day she is smitten with Ian Miller, a high-school teacher who comes to the restaurant. With the help of her mother, Maria, she persuades Gus to let her take computer classes at a local college.

As her confidence grows, Toula changes her appearance, trading her thick glasses for contact lenses and adopting a brighter style. She takes a job at her aunt Voula's travel agency, where Ian notices her and asks her out. Their romance blossoms, but Toula keeps it secret, knowing her father will object to her dating a non-Greek. When the family finds out, Gus is furious, but Ian, a gentle vegetarian from a reserved and very small family, is determined to win them over. He agrees to be baptized into the Greek Orthodox Church and endures the boisterous affection of Toula's countless relatives. As the wedding approaches, the clash between the exuberant Portokalos clan and Ian's bewildered parents provides comedy, while Toula comes to accept both her heritage and the life she wants.

Made for about $5 million, the film became a surprise phenomenon through word of mouth, grossing over $368 million worldwide and becoming one of the most profitable independent films ever. It received positive reviews, and Vardalos was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay. Sequels followed in 2016 and 2023.
