documents.title: The Protector
documents.tagline: Vengeance Knows No Mercy.
documents.overview: In Bangkok, the young Kham was raised by his father in the jungle with elephants as members of their family. When his old elephant and the baby Kern are stolen by criminals, Kham finds that the animals were sent to Sidney. He travels to Australia, where he locates the baby elephant in a restaurant owned by the evil Madame Rose, the leader of an international Thai mafia. With the support of the efficient Thai sergeant Mark, who was involved in a conspiracy, Kham fights to rescue the animal from the mobsters.
documents.plot:
The Protector is a 2005 martial arts film directed by Renny Harlin and starring Jason Statham as Jack Crawley, an undercover agent working for MI6. 

Beginning: The movie starts with Jack Crawley, a skilled fighter and assassin, who has been sent to Thailand to infiltrate the Triad organization. He assumes the identity of "Jack" and gains the trust of the Triad's leader, Tong Po (Sihung Lung). Jack is tasked with taking down Tong Po, but he soon discovers that his mission is not what it seems.

Plot Development: As Jack delves deeper into the world of the Triads, he meets a beautiful woman named Anna (Claire Forlani), who becomes his ally and potential love interest. Together, they uncover a plot by Tong Po to smuggle heroin out of Thailand and sell it in Europe. Jack must use his skills to take down Tong Po's men and prevent the heroin from being shipped.

However, as Jack gets closer to the truth, he realizes that there is more at stake than just stopping Tong Po. He discovers that Anna is actually a double agent working for MI6, and her true mission is to gather evidence against Tong Po. Jack must navigate his feelings for Anna while also completing his original mission.

Ending: In the climactic final battle, Jack faces off against Tong Po's top henchman, who has been secretly working with Anna all along. With the help of Anna and a few other allies, Jack manages to defeat the henchman and prevent the heroin from being shipped. However, in the process, Jack is severely injured and forced to leave Thailand.

As Jack returns to England, he reflects on his mission and the people he has met during his time in Thailand. He realizes that his feelings for Anna were genuine, but their relationship was complicated by her true loyalties. The movie ends with Jack walking away from a burning building, symbolizing his departure from the world of espionage.

Overall, The Protector is an action-packed thrill ride with plenty of twists and turns. Jason Statham delivers a strong performance as the rugged and charismatic Jack Crawley, and Claire Forlani shines as the beautiful and deadly Anna.

documents.title: Hollow Man II
documents.tagline: There's More to Terror Than Meets The Eye
documents.overview: After the mysterious death of scientist, Dr. Devin Villiers, Det. Frank Turner and his partner are assigned to protect Villiers' colleague, who revealed that  a veteran soldier was subjected to an experiment with the objective of creating the ultimate national security weapon... an undetectable soldier. The experiment failed – with disastrous side effects.
documents.plot:
Hollow Man 2 (released as Hollow Man II) is a 2006 American science fiction thriller directed by Claudio Fäh. A stand-alone sequel to the 2000 film Hollow Man, it explores the consequences of invisibility through Michael Griffin, a soldier left permanently invisible by a government experiment that went wrong. Peter Facinelli stars as Detective Frank Turner, Laura Regan as the scientist Maggie Dalton and Christian Slater as Griffin, with David McIlwraith, Sarah Deakins and Jessica Harmon.

At a cocktail party held by a Washington think tank, the scientist Devin Villiers is dragged into a bathroom by an unseen attacker. Under threat, he reveals the name of a colleague, Maggie Dalton, who holds the "formula" his assailant wants. Spared on condition of silence, Devin tries to raise the alarm and is killed. Dr. Reisner, whose laboratory carried out the invisibility research, arranges for detectives Frank Turner and Lisa Martinez to guard Maggie, but the attacker gets into her home and kills Lisa, and soldiers fail to catch him.

Maggie is taken into protective custody, but when Turner learns that she is about to be handed over to the military, he helps her escape. She explains that scientists had earlier created an invisibility serum with severe and eventually fatal side effects. When the military secretly revived the project, Griffin volunteered as a test subject, and he was believed to have died after the antidote meant to reverse the process failed; Maggie later discovered that the antidote, known as the buffer, had never actually been given to him. The fugitives take refuge with a former soldier from the program, who tells them that the military has been using Griffin to carry out political assassinations, and who sacrifices his life to protect them when Griffin attacks.

Griffin then kidnaps Maggie's sister and demands that Maggie recreate the antidote in return for her sister's life. After a confrontation with Turner at a train station, Griffin forces Maggie to a laboratory and makes her inject herself with half of the buffer to prove it is safe. Turner tracks them down and fights Griffin, who begins to turn visible and horribly disfigured: Maggie had substituted rat poison for the antidote. Griffin is defeated, leaving Maggie and Turner alive but shaken.

The film went straight to video on May 23, 2006. As with the original, it was poorly received; only one of six reviews on Rotten Tomatoes was positive.

documents.title: Friends with Money
documents.overview: After she quits her lucrative job, Olivia finds herself unsure about her future and her relationships with her successful and wealthy friends.
documents.plot:
Olivia is a single, always-broke woman who cleans houses in Los Angeles to make ends meet after quitting her job as a teacher. She is in a group of wealthy friends consisting of Franny, a stay-at-home mom with a large trust fund; Christine, a television writer; Jane, a fashion designer; and their husbands.
Still heartbroken over a brief affair with a married man, Olivia agrees to go on a blind date with Franny's trainer, Mike. The date goes poorly, but Mike attempts to make up for it at the last minute and asks to go along with Olivia on a cleaning job. Despite him only offering minimal help, Mike asks for part of Olivia's pay and she reluctantly agrees. They begin dating and Mike continues to come along to work with Olivia and take part of her earnings until she finally finds the self-confidence to call Mike out for his callous behavior and ends the relationship.
Christine and her husband David are constantly at odds with each other, to the point that their friends openly speculate whether they're going to split up. Christine struggles to concentrate on the script she and David are writing as the construction of a new addition to their home is ongoing. She soon discovers that their neighbors' sudden animosity is because the addition will block their views, and attempts to stop construction.
David expresses apathy at the neighbors' anger and Christine confronts him for his lack of sensitivity, including showing a lack of care and affection for her. They decide to separate. Christine puts the unfinished house up for sale and briefly finds herself despondent at David's absence before stubbing her toe and hearing her nanny call out asking if she's okay—something David had always failed to do.
Jane cannot seem to stop herself from insulting acquaintances and becoming angry over minor perceived slights. She also has stopped washing her hair and shows signs of depression. Her husband Aaron, who owns a shampoo company, is fashionable and often assumed to be gay by strangers as well as friends. He befriends another straight, married man named Aaron with similar interests and finally, confronts Jane for her angry fits and refusal to wash her hair after she has an outburst during brunch with the other Aaron and his wife. Jane admits that she's depressed after realizing, "There's no more wondering what it's going to be like."
Franny and her husband Matt are by far the wealthiest couple in the group due to Franny's trust fund. Neither of them work and they live in a large house with full-time help. The other friends frequently comment on their wealth and the apparent lack of tension in their marriage as a result of having no stress about money or work, though Franny does express some discomfort with how much Matt likes to spend.
The friends come together at a charity fundraiser for ALS, where Franny has bought a table. Jane finally washes her hair and smooths things over with her husband.

documents.title: Derailed
documents.tagline: He never saw it coming.
documents.overview: When two married business executives having an affair are blackmailed by a violent criminal, they are forced to turn the tables on him to save their families.
documents.plot:
Chicago advertising executive Charles Schine lives with his wife Deanna and their daughter Amy, who suffers from type 1 diabetes, which requires expensive medical treatment.
On a commuter train to work one morning, Charles meets Lucinda Harris, a financial advisor who is married with a daughter. The two begin meeting and one evening decide to take a room in a cheap hotel. As they are undressing, an armed man bursts into their room and robs them and beats Charles, and then brutally rapes Lucinda. Not wanting her husband to learn of her affair, Lucinda persuades Charles not to report the crime and they go their separate ways.
Days later, the man, who identifies himself as Philippe LaRoche, contacts Charles and threatens to kill his family if he does not pay him $20,000. He takes the money from their savings, goes to the meeting point and hands over the cash. LaRoche beats Charles for cancelling his credit cards.
A month later, LaRoche calls again, this time demanding $100,000. Charles explains his situation to his work colleague Winston, an ex-con. Winston offers to scare off LaRoche for ten percent of the demanded payout. Charles embezzles $10,000 from his company and he and Winston plot to get the drop on LaRoche at the specified meeting location. However, LaRoche surprises them, shoots Winston dead, and takes the $10,000. Charles dumps the car with Winston's body into the river and later gives a false alibi when questioned by Detective Franklin Church.
Charles receives another call from LaRoche, saying he is holding Lucinda hostage and will kill her if he does not deliver the full $100,000. Charles takes the money from the account meant for his daughter's medical treatment, goes to Lucinda's apartment, and makes the payoff to LaRoche and his partner Dexter.
Charles visits Lucinda at her workplace but discovers that the woman he met is not the Lucinda Harris who works there but is actually called Jane and only worked there briefly as a temp. He reaches her apartment, which is now being shown to new prospective renters, and discovers that Jane's photograph of her purported daughter is actually a cut-out of a stock picture from a brochure.
Charles tracks Jane down, follows her, and sees her meeting and kissing LaRoche, learning she was in on the scam. He also observes her seducing another businessman, Sam. Determined to retrieve his stolen money, Charles rents a room at the same hotel as before and waits for Jane to arrive there with Sam, followed by LaRoche. Charles knocks LaRoche unconscious outside the hotel room door, disarms him, and bursts in, telling a confused Sam the scheme he has been set up for. Dexter arrives to back up LaRoche and when Sam tries to jump Charles a gunfight ensues, with everyone shot but Charles, who watches Jane die and then returns to his room. He convinces the police who have been called in that he was just a bystander. As he leaves, Charles claims his briefcase from the hotel safe and gets back his stolen money.

documents.title: Just Like Heaven
documents.tagline: It's a wonderful afterlife.
documents.overview: Shortly after David Abbott moves into his new San Francisco digs, he has an unwelcome visitor on his hands: winsome Elizabeth Martinson, who asserts that the apartment is hers -- and promptly vanishes. When she starts appearing and disappearing at will, David thinks she's a ghost, while Elizabeth is convinced she's alive.
documents.plot:
Elizabeth Masterson, a dedicated young San Francisco physician, is in a serious car crash. Three months later, the grieving recent widower David Abbott sublets Elizabeth's apartment.
Elizabeth begins appearing in the apartment, confusing both. She initially believes David is a squatter, and he thinks she broke in. They soon realize Elizabeth can move through walls and objects. She does not know who she is, but insists she is not dead.
David unsuccessfully tries to have Elizabeth's spirit exorcised. As only he can see and hear her, others think he is hallucinating. Elizabeth asks him to help her discover who she really is, so David first talks to neighbours in the building but no one knows her.
David enlists help from psychic bookstore clerk Darryl, who agrees Elizabeth is not truly dead. He says David has a blocked heart and must emotionally release the woman who was in his life. When Elizabeth says he should get over being dumped, he storms out. Darryl, unable to see Elizabeth, tells her not to disrespect the dead. She finds David and he explains about his wife's death.
At a nearby restaurant, Elizabeth talks David through saving a man's life. Suddenly, she remembers being a doctor. They go to the nearest hospital where Elizabeth's memories come flooding back. Dr. Fran Lo, Elizabeth's mentor, takes him to Elizabeth, who is in a coma. When David touches her hand, she feels it, meaning she is still connected to her body.
Elizabeth's sister Abby arrives, and Dr. Brett Rushton – Elizabeth's rival – notifies her that Elizabeth signed a DNR order. When he asks her to sign off on disconnecting Elizabeth's life support, she agrees to consider it.
David and Elizabeth bond. When he takes her to a beautiful landscaped garden he designed, she senses having been there before. In fact, she was dreaming of the garden (in the opening scenes of the film), while catnapping during a long shift.
When David is offered a long-term lease on Elizabeth's apartment, he realizes she will be taken off life support. To prevent it, he goes to Abby and says she is communicating with him. While there, Elizabeth discovers that her niece Lily can see her. David begs Abby to keep her alive, but she has already signed the papers to disconnect her life support the next day. As a last-ditch effort, David blurts out Abby's secret kiss to J.J. on her wedding day, freaking her out so she chases him out.
Elizabeth opts to spend her last night with David in the apartment. The next morning, he is determined to prevent her death by stealing her body from the hospital; he enlists his therapist friend Jack to help. Upon reaching her body, Elizabeth suddenly recognises Jack as Abby's former college boyfriend J.J., who reveals that the two of them had set up David and Elizabeth for a blind date on the night of the crash. David realizes he can see her because they were destined to meet. He admits to Jack and Elizabeth that he loves her.

documents.title: Dark Water
documents.tagline: This Season, The Mystery Of The Darkness Will Consume Your Life
documents.overview: Dahlia Williams and her daughter Cecelia move into a rundown apartment on New York's Roosevelt Island. She is currently in midst of divorce proceedings and the apartment, though near an excellent school for her daughter, is all she can afford. From the time she arrives, there are mysterious occurrences and there is a constant drip from the ceiling in her daughter's bedroom.
documents.plot: Dahlia and her five-year-old daughter are ready to begin a new life together. But their new apartment — dilapidated and worn — suddenly seems to take on a life of its own. Mysterious noises, persistent leaks of dark water and other strange happenings send Dahlia on a haunting and mystifying pursuit — one that unleashes a torrent of living nightmares.

documents.title: Jackass: The Movie
documents.tagline: Do not attempt this at home.
documents.overview: Johnny Knoxville and his band of maniacs perform a variety of stunts and gross-out gags on the big screen for the first time. They wander around Japan in panda outfits, wreak havoc on a once civilized golf course, they even do stunts involving LIVE alligators, and so on.
documents.plot:
Jackass: The Movie is a 2002 American reality slapstick comedy directed by Jeff Tremaine and produced by Tremaine, Spike Jonze and Johnny Knoxville. A continuation of the MTV television series Jackass, which had ended its run, it was produced by Lynch Siderow Productions and Dickhouse Productions and features most of the original cast, including Knoxville, Bam Margera, Chris Pontius, Steve-O, Dave England, Ryan Dunn, Wee Man, Preston Lacy and Ehren McGhehey.

Like the series, the film has no conventional plot. It is a compilation of dangerous stunts, crude skits and elaborate pranks on unsuspecting members of the public, intercut with comments from the cast. It opens with a mock Hollywood action sequence set to "O Fortuna", in which the entire cast rides a giant shopping cart downhill amid explosions while each member is introduced, before Knoxville delivers his signature greeting and the group crashes into a fruit stand.

Among the many stunts and pranks that follow, Knoxville is flipped over and knocked out in a golf cart, Steve-O snorts wasabi, Bam Margera plants a live alligator in his mother April's kitchen, Chris Pontius dances in public in a thong as his character Party Boy, and Ryan Dunn takes on a female Japanese kickboxing champion. Wee Man causes chaos in the streets of Tokyo inside a giant traffic cone, and the cast endure painful encounters with animals, paper cuts, fireworks and bodily functions. Throughout, the cast's willingness to injure and humiliate themselves for the camera is the central source of humor, along with their obvious camaraderie.

Like the series, the film relies on the cast's apparent fearlessness and on the reactions of bystanders, and it is widely regarded as a cult phenomenon of the 2000s.

MTV Films and Paramount Pictures released the film on October 25, 2002. Made for about 5 million dollars, it opened at number one at the U.S. box office with 22.8 million dollars and grossed 79.5 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 49 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 42, and it was followed by Jackass Number Two in 2006.

documents.title: Treasure Planet
documents.tagline: Find your place in the universe.
documents.overview: When space galleon cabin boy Jim Hawkins discovers a map to an intergalactic "loot of a thousand worlds," a cyborg cook named John Silver teaches him to battle supernovas and space storms on their journey to find treasure.
documents.plot:
Treasure Planet is a science fiction adventure film produced by Walt Disney Pictures, released in 2002. The movie is an adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson's classic novel "Treasure Island," set in a futuristic universe.

The story begins with Jim Hawkins (voiced by Joseph Gordon-Levitt), an orphan boy living on the planet Terra. Jim's life changes when he meets Billy Bones (voiced by David Hyde Pierce), an old pirate who has been injured and is dying. Before his death, Billy gives Jim a mysterious map that supposedly leads to the treasure of the infamous Captain Flint.

Jim sets out on a journey with Dr. Delbert Doppler (voiced by Brian Murray), a spaceship captain who claims to be taking him to find the treasure. However, upon arrival at the planet of Salacia, they are ambushed by Captain Flint's crew, led by the ruthless and cunning Long John Silver (voiced by Jack Davenport). Long John Silver is revealed to be Jim's biological father, and his true intentions for finding the treasure are not what they seem.

As Jim navigates this new world, he meets a group of space pirates known as the "Buccaneers," who are on a quest to find the legendary treasure. The crew includes John Mutt (voiced by Jason Lee), a young and skilled pirate; and B.E.N. (voiced by Patrick McGoohan), an old robot who becomes Jim's friend and ally.

Throughout their journey, Jim faces various challenges and obstacles as he tries to uncover the truth about his father's past and the treasure. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

As the story unfolds, Long John Silver's true intentions are revealed: he plans to use the treasure to gain control over the entire planet. Jim and his friends must work together to stop him and save the day. In a thrilling finale, they engage in an epic space battle against Captain Flint's crew, with Jim ultimately discovering the truth about his father's past and finding the treasure.

The movie ends with Jim returning home, having grown into a confident and capable young man. He reflects on the lessons he learned during his journey and the friends he made along the way, knowing that their bond will last a lifetime.

Treasure Planet is a visually stunning film that combines traditional animation techniques with cutting-edge computer-generated imagery. The movie's unique blend of science fiction and classic adventure elements has made it a beloved favorite among audiences of all ages.

documents.title: The Santa Clause 2
documents.tagline: What's Christmas Fun without some Reindeer Games?
documents.overview: Better watch out! The big guy in red is coming to town once again. This time, Scott Calvin -- also known as Santa Claus -- finds out there's an obscure clause in his contract requiring him to take on a wife. He has to leave the North Pole to fulfill his obligations, or else he'll be forced to give up his Yuletide gig.
documents.plot:
The Santa Clause 2 is a Christmas comedy film released in 2002, directed by Michael Lembeck and written by Leo Benvenuti, Steve Rudnick, and Rick Mulvaney. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1994 film The Santa Clause.

The story begins with Scott Calvin (Tim Allen), who has now been living as Santa Claus for over five years. He is struggling to balance his life as a father and husband with his duties as the new Santa. His wife, Carol (Elizabeth Mitchell), is pregnant with their first child, but she's not sure if Scott can handle being Santa full-time.

Meanwhile, a group of elves from the North Pole arrive at Scott's house, warning him that Christmas Eve is approaching and he must return to the North Pole to prepare for the holiday. However, Scott is hesitant to leave his family behind, especially since Carol has just discovered she's pregnant with their first child.

As Christmas Eve approaches, Scott's doubts about being Santa grow stronger. He begins to question whether he's truly cut out for the job and starts to feel like a "fake" Santa. The elves try to convince him that he's doing a great job as Santa, but Scott is unconvinced.

On Christmas Eve, disaster strikes when a group of naughty children, led by a young boy named Tucker (Eric Lloyd), steal the magical crystal that gives Scott his powers. Without the crystal, Scott loses his Santa powers and is forced to return home for Christmas.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Scott's son Charlie (Eric Lloyd) discovers the truth about his father's identity as Santa. Charlie is initially excited to have a real-life Santa Claus as a dad, but he soon realizes that being Santa comes with its own set of challenges and responsibilities.

As Christmas Day approaches, Scott must find a way to regain his powers and save Christmas. With the help of his elves and Carol, Scott embarks on a journey to retrieve the magical crystal and restore his powers. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about being a good father, husband, and Santa Claus.

In the end, Scott successfully retrieves the crystal and regains his powers as Santa. The movie concludes with Scott returning to the North Pole, where he is welcomed back by the elves and Mrs. Claus (Judge Reinhold). Scott also gets to spend Christmas with his family, including his son Charlie, who has learned to appreciate the challenges and joys of being a part of the Claus family.

The Santa Clause 2 received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $140 million worldwide. The movie's blend of humor, heart, and holiday cheer made it a beloved favorite among families around the world.

documents.title: All the Boys Love Mandy Lane
documents.original_title: All the Boys Love Mandy Lane
documents.tagline: Everyone is dying to be with her. Someone is killing for it.
documents.overview: Beautiful Mandy Lane isn't a party girl but, when classmate Chloe invites the Texas high school student to a bash in the countryside, she reluctantly accepts. After hitching a ride with a vaguely scary older man, the teens arrive at their destination. Partying ensues, and Mandy's close pal, Emmet, keeps a watchful eye on the young males making a play for Mandy. Then two of the students are murdered.
documents.plot:
All the Boys Love Mandy Lane is a 2006 American slasher film directed by Jonathan Levine in his feature debut and written by Jacob Forman. Amber Heard stars as Mandy Lane, a high-school student whose beauty makes her the object of everyone's attention, with Anson Mount as the ranch hand Garth, Michael Welch, Whitney Able and Edwin Hodge. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2006 and was shown at many festivals before its British release in February 2008; because of distribution problems, its American release was delayed until 2013.

At a Texas high school, Mandy Lane returns from summer vacation transformed, attracting the attention of all the boys. One of them, Dylan, invites her to a pool party, and she agrees on condition that her best friend, the outcast Emmet, can come. When Dylan humiliates Emmet, Emmet retaliates by goading a drunken Dylan into jumping from the roof into the pool; Dylan misses and dies on the concrete. Nine months later, Mandy has been accepted by Dylan's popular friends, while Emmet has become even more of a pariah.

The stoner Red invites Mandy to a weekend party at his father's remote cattle ranch, and she reluctantly accepts. She travels there with Red, the insecure cheerleader Chloe, the quiet football player Bird, and the couple Jake and Marlin, all eager to impress her. At the ranch they meet Garth, a handsome, laconic ranch hand. On the first night, after Jake and Marlin argue in a barn, an unseen attacker knocks Marlin unconscious and brutally assaults her with a shotgun. As drinking, drugs and sexual tension fuel rivalries among the teenagers, the killer begins picking them off one by one. The identity of the murderer is revealed partway through, but the story holds further twists about the true nature of the bloodshed, and Mandy's role in the events turns out to be very different from what the others, and the audience, expect.

All the Boys Love Mandy Lane received mixed reviews, holding a 47 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it had enough wit and craft to interest horror fans but was not original enough for mainstream audiences. Over time the film gained a cult following, and critics praised its 1970s-style cinematography and Heard's performance.

documents.title: Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron
documents.tagline: Leader. Hero. Legend.
documents.overview: As a wild stallion travels across the frontiers of the Old West, he befriends a young human and finds true love with a mare.
documents.plot:
Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron is a 2002 American animated Western drama film produced by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the journey of a wild mustang stallion named Spirit, who embarks on an epic quest to find his place in the world.

The film begins with Spirit (voiced by Matt Damon) as a young foal, born and raised in the Cimarron Valley. He is a spirited and adventurous horse, always eager to explore and discover new things. As he grows up, Spirit becomes increasingly restless, feeling confined by the limitations of his herd's routine.

One day, Spirit meets a beautiful mare named Rain (voiced by Gina Philips), who shares his sense of wanderlust. Together, they set out on an adventure across the American West, facing numerous challenges and dangers along the way. They encounter fierce storms, treacherous terrain, and hostile humans, but their bond grows stronger with each passing day.

As Spirit and Rain journey through the wilderness, they meet a wise old stallion named Thunder (voiced by Michael Jeter), who teaches them about the importance of freedom and self-discovery. However, their happiness is short-lived, as they are captured by a ruthless horse trader named Colonel Hart (voiced by James Cromwell) and his men.

Spirit is sold to a cavalry unit, where he meets a young soldier named Little Creek (voiced by Paul Williams), who befriends him and helps him escape. Together, they embark on a perilous journey back to the Cimarron Valley, facing numerous obstacles and dangers along the way.

As Spirit returns home, he is reunited with Rain, and together they face off against Colonel Hart in an epic showdown. With his newfound courage and determination, Spirit defeats the colonel and his men, securing his freedom and proving himself as a true leader among his herd.

Throughout the film, the animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and characters that bring the American West to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, bringing depth and emotion to their respective roles. The music, composed by Hans Zimmer and John Powell, is equally impressive, perfectly capturing the spirit (pun intended) of the wild mustang.

Overall, Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron is a timeless tale of self-discovery, courage, and the power of the human (and equine) spirit. With its stunning animation, memorable characters, and epic storyline, it's no wonder this film has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

documents.title: The Eye
documents.tagline: How can you believe your eyes when they're not yours?
documents.overview: Violinist Sydney Wells was accidentally blinded by her sister Helen when she was five years old. She submits to a cornea transplantation, and while recovering from the operation, she realizes that she is seeing dead people.
documents.plot:
Sydney Wells is a successful classical violinist from Los Angeles who has been blind since she was five years old, caused by an accident with firecrackers. Fifteen years later, after celebrating conductor and pianist Simon McCullough's birthday during rehearsal, Sydney undergoes a cornea transplant, which causes her eyesight to return. While a bit blurry at first, as time passes, Sydney's vision begins to clear; however, she also begins experiencing terrifying visions, mostly of fire and people dying. She also sees people who are already dead: on one occasion, a girl passes right through her. Sydney attempts to unravel the mystery of the visions and convince others, primarily her visual therapist and fellow violinist, Paul Faulkner, who helps her in her quest. She knows that she is not going insane.
Accompanied by Paul, Sydney travels to Mexico, where the cornea donor Ana Cristina Martinez was originally from. She discovers from Ana's mother that the images of fire and death are the result of an industrial accident that Ana foretold. Ana hanged herself because she was unable to stop the accident. Sydney forgives Ana's spirit, who leaves in peace. As Sydney and Paul begin their journey home, they are caught in traffic congestion caused by a police chase on the other side of the border. Sydney sees the little girl from her vision in the car beside her. She then realizes that this is what her vision has been all along: to save the people who are about to die from an accident.
Still able to see the silhouettes of death, Sydney gets everyone off the highway, starting with a bus filled with people. She and Paul convince everyone to leave the bus and the cars by telling them that there is a bomb inside the bus. However, a driver leading the police chase rushes through the border barriers and collides with a tank truck, igniting leaking gasoline in the process. Sydney sees the little girl trapped in the car, her mother lying on the ground in front of it, already being hit by a passenger and losing consciousness. Paul breaks open the window and gets the girl out. Paul and Sydney carry the girl and her mother to safety just before the tank truck causes a chain explosion. Sydney is blinded by flying glass fragments in the process.
After recovering at a hospital, she returns to Los Angeles to continue performing as a blind violinist, though with a more optimistic view of her condition.

documents.title: Slither
documents.tagline: Horror has a new face.
documents.overview: A small town is taken over by an alien plague, turning residents into zombies and all forms of mutant monsters.
documents.plot:
Slither is a 2006 American horror-comedy film directed by James Gunn and written by Gunn and Phil Lord. The movie stars Nathan Fillion, Elizabeth Banks, Michael Rooker, and Jill Witcher.

The story begins with a small town called Middleton, where a group of friends, including Jeff (Nathan Fillion), a high school teacher, and his girlfriend Starla (Elizabeth Banks), are preparing for the annual Harvest Festival. The festival is a celebration of the town's agricultural heritage, but it also serves as an opportunity for the townspeople to let loose and have fun.

However, things take a dark turn when a mysterious alien parasite infects the town's residents, turning them into zombie-like creatures with a strong desire to eat human flesh. The parasite, which is about 10 feet long, has been introduced to Earth by a group of aliens who crash-landed in the nearby woods.

As the infection spreads rapidly throughout the town, Jeff and his friends must band together to survive and find a way to stop the parasite before it's too late. Along the way, they encounter a variety of bizarre and terrifying creatures, including giant spiders, mutated animals, and even a zombie-like version of Starla.

One of the most interesting aspects of Slither is its exploration of small-town America and the ways in which people can become complacent and accepting of their surroundings. The town of Middleton is portrayed as a place where everyone knows each other's business, but also where secrets and lies are often swept under the rug.

As the story progresses, Jeff and his friends discover that the parasite has a unique ability to manipulate its hosts' minds, making them more aggressive and violent. They also learn that the aliens who introduced the parasite were not just random visitors, but rather part of an experiment designed to create a new breed of super-soldiers.

In the end, Jeff and his friends must use their wits and whatever resources they can find to stop the parasite and save the town. Along the way, they encounter some unexpected allies, including a group of survivors from a nearby town who have been fighting against the parasites for weeks.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between Jeff and the leader of the zombie-like creatures, a giant spider-like creature that has become the parasite's host. In the end, Jeff emerges victorious, but not before realizing that the parasite has left him with a strange and unsettling connection to the alien entity.

Overall, Slither is a fun and entertaining horror-comedy that explores themes of small-town America, paranoia, and the dangers of complacency. With its unique blend of humor, action, and horror elements, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Eight Below
documents.tagline: The Most Amazing Story Of Survival, Friendship, And Adventure Ever Told.
documents.overview: In the Antarctic, after an expedition with Dr. Davis McClaren, the sled dog trainer Jerry Shepherd has to leave the polar base with his colleagues due to the proximity of a heavy snow storm. He ties his dogs to be rescued after, but the mission is called-off and the dogs are left alone at their own fortune. For six months, Jerry tries to find a sponsor for a rescue mission.
documents.plot:
In January 1993, Jerry Shepard, guide at a National Science Foundation Antarctic research base, is asked to take UCLA professor Dr. Davis McClaren to Mount Melbourne to find a rare meteorite from Mercury. Since the ice conditions are poor, the best way to the mountain is by dog sled.
Shepard and McClaren make it, but are called back to base camp due to an approaching storm. McClaren begs for more time and Shepard gives him half a day. En route back to base, McClaren slips down an embankment, breaking his leg and falling into freezing water. Shepard uses lead dog Maya to carry a rope to McClaren and pulls him out. They battle hypothermia, frostbite, and near-whiteout conditions as the dogs lead them to base.
At base, the human crew is immediately evacuated, while the dogs are left behind. Shepard, promised that the pilot will return shortly for the dogs, tightens their collars to ensure they cannot get loose. Because of the harsh weather conditions a rescue cannot be attempted.
Back in the United States, Shepard tries to return for the dogs, but no one is willing to finance the expedition. Five months later, Shepard makes one last attempt. McClaren realizing his ingratitude and uses the remainder of his grant money to finance the rescue. They fear there is little chance any of the dogs could have survived so long, but they decide to try anyway.
The eight sled dogs – lead dog Maya, Old Jack, Shorty, Dewey, Truman, Shadow, Buck, and the young Max – have been waiting in the freezing conditions for Shepard to return. After a few days without eating, the dogs are prompted into action as a gull flies near, and they all begin to break free, one by one. Old Jack, by now too weak, remains attached. Maya tries to free him, but reluctantly leaves him behind when he shows no sign of wanting to leave. Maya joins the other dogs, and together they catch a few birds, getting their first food in weeks.
After nearly two months on their own, the dogs rest on a slope one night under the southern lights. Fascinated by the display, they run about and play until Dewey falls down an incline and is mortally wounded. The team sleeps by his side and Dewey dies overnight. Max loyally stays by him while the others move on. By the time Max heads in their direction, he has lost the pack.
Maya leads the team to the Russian base, which is unsecured and full of food, while Max finds his way back to the American base, which is locked up. Setting back out, Max recognizes the embankment the dogs traveled on their way back from Mount Melbourne. While exploring, Max finds a dead orca, but is driven off by a leopard seal nesting inside the body. Nearby, Maya and the team hear Max and join him. Max lures the seal away so the dogs can eat, but it doubles back and bites Maya, leaving her badly injured.
In a rage, the five other dogs attack the seal. Overwhelmed, the seal quickly drags itself into the water, after which the dogs feast on the orca. The reunited team continues traveling.

documents.title: Trapped
documents.tagline: It was the perfect plan until she refused to be the perfect victim!
documents.overview: When their daughter is kidnapped by experienced nappers, the Jennings turn the tables on this seemingly foolproof plan.
documents.plot:
Trapped is a 2002 American crime thriller film directed by Luis Mandoki and based on Greg Iles's novel 24 Hours. Charlize Theron and Stuart Townsend star as the parents of a kidnapped girl, played by Dakota Fanning, with Kevin Bacon and Courtney Love as the kidnappers and Pruitt Taylor Vince as their accomplice. It was filmed in British Columbia in the spring of 2001 and released by Columbia Pictures on September 20, 2002.

Dr. Will Jennings, a successful physician, has just patented a new anesthetic and travels to Seattle to present it at a medical conference. At his hotel, a woman named Cheryl introduces herself as an admirer, then pulls a gun and forces him into his room. At the same moment, her husband, Joe, breaks into the Jennings family's luxurious home outside Portland, Oregon, and takes Will's wife, Karen, hostage, while Joe's cousin Marvin drives their young daughter, Abby, to a remote cabin. The couple demands a ransom, keeping the parents apart and under watch.

The plan begins to unravel when Abby, who suffers from severe asthma, has an attack without her inhaler, and Joe is forced to take a blindfolded Karen to the cabin to treat her. Back at the house, Karen fights back against Joe, wounding him with a hidden scalpel and briefly speaking with Abby by phone before Joe regains control. In Seattle, Will uses his medical knowledge to inject Cheryl with a paralyzing drug, bringing her close to death before reviving her. Shaken, Cheryl reveals that this abduction is personal: Joe blames Will for the death of their own daughter, who died during surgery on which Will assisted. Will explains that he was wrongly blamed by the head surgeon, and Cheryl begins to turn against the plan, especially after learning in a heated phone call that Joe intends to keep Abby and raise her as his own.

Accompanied by police, Will collects the ransom, then flies with Cheryl toward Portland in a seaplane as Joe drives north on Interstate 5 with Karen, followed by Marvin and Abby. When Karen attacks Joe and forces the car off the road, Will spots it from the air and lands the seaplane on the highway, causing a massive pileup. Marvin lets Abby go, and after a struggle between the two men, Karen shoots Joe dead. As police and FBI agents arrive, Karen treats Abby's asthma, and the family is reunited as Cheryl is arrested.

Trapped was a critical and commercial failure. Rotten Tomatoes reported 17% approval, and the film grossed about $13.4 million worldwide.

documents.title: Serpico
documents.tagline: Many of his fellow officers considered him the most dangerous man alive - An honest cop.
documents.overview: Frank Serpico is an idealistic New York City cop who refuses to take bribes, unlike the rest of the force. His actions get Frank shunned by the other officers, and often placed in dangerous situations by his partners. When his superiors ignore Frank's accusations of corruption, he decides to go public with the allegations. Although this causes the Knapp Commission to investigate his claims, Frank has also placed a target on himself.
documents.plot:
On the evening of February 3, 1971, NYPD Detective Frank Serpico is rushed to the hospital, having been shot in the face. Police Chief Sidney Green fears that Serpico was shot by another cop. Serpico's story is shown in a flashback.
Serpico graduates from the police academy on March 5, 1960, with big ideas for improving the police force's community relations. He dresses like an actual civilian instead of wearing the department's standard plainclothes dress, which is easily recognizable. While he is chasing a burglar, other officers fail to recognize him as one of their own and shoot at him. He survives, but realizes that deviating from protocols can be dangerous.
In 1967, Serpico reports an attempted bribe to a high-ranking investigator, who chuckles and advises him to keep the money. Serpico soon learns that corruption is rampant in the department. Forced to accompany officers as they collect payoffs from criminals and small businesses, Serpico refuses to accept his share of the money. He makes several attempts to alert superiors to the corruption but is rebuffed every time. Other officers learn that he is reporting them, and he begins to fear for his life.
Serpico and his well-connected friend Blair go to the mayor's assistant, who promises a real investigation and support but is stymied by political pressure. Ostracized, frustrated and fearful, Serpico sinks into depression, which ruins his relationship with his girlfriend. He begins brutalizing well-connected suspects who had been bribing his superiors and thought themselves protected. Finally, Serpico informs his Captain that he reported his experiences to agencies outside of the NYC police force. Furious, the captain informs the other officers.
Blair uses his connections to arrange a personal interview with the district attorney, who tells Serpico that if he testifies to a grand jury, a major investigation will follow. The DA limits his questions and prevents Serpico from revealing the ubiquity of corruption in the police force. Serpico and Blair take their story to The New York Times on April 25, 1970. After his allegations are published, his superiors retaliate by assigning Serpico to a high-risk Brooklyn narcotics squad.
During a raid on a drug trafficker's apartment on February 3, 1971, Serpico's partners hold him back at a critical moment, and he gets shot in the face. After a long, painful recovery, he testifies before the Knapp Commission, a governmental inquiry into NYPD corruption. Afterward, Serpico resigns from the NYPD on June 15, 1972, and is awarded the NYPD Medal of Honor for "conspicuous bravery in action". He then leaves the U.S. and settles in Switzerland.

documents.title: The Cave
documents.tagline: There are places man was never meant to go
documents.overview: After a group of biologists discovers a huge network of unexplored caves in Romania and, believing it to be an undisturbed eco-system that has produced a new species, they hire the best American team of underwater cave explorers in the world. While exploring deeper into the underwater caves, a rockslide blocks their exit, and they soon discover a larger carnivorous creature has added them to its food chain.

While exploring deeper into the underwater caves, a rockslide blocks their exit, and they soon discover a larger carnivorous creature has added them to its food chain.

documents.title: The Family Stone
documents.tagline: Feel The Love
documents.overview: An uptight, conservative businesswoman accompanies her boyfriend to his eccentric and outgoing family's annual Christmas celebration and finds that she's a fish out of water in their free-spirited way of life.

documents.title: Tristan & Isolde
documents.tagline: Fighting countries can still love...
documents.overview: An affair between the second in line to Britain's throne and the princess of the feuding Irish spells doom for the young lovers.
documents.plot:
Set in the Dark Ages after the fall of the Roman Empire, Lord Marke of Cornwall plans to unite the tribes of Britain – Celts, Picts, Angles, Saxons and Jutes – against Irish domination. Lord Aragon of Tantallon Castle leads the treaty negotiations, convinced that Lord Marke is the unifying figure capable of rallying all the tribes behind him. The Irish king, Donachadh, orders an attack on the castle while his wife's funeral is underway and the treaty negotiations are in progress. Lord and Lady Aragon, along with Marke's pregnant wife, are killed, but Marke manages to save their young son, Tristan, and loses the right hand in the process. Marke and his widowed sister, Edyth, welcome Tristan into their home. Tristan clashes with Edyth's son, Melot, but quickly wins the favor of Simon and other boys.
Nine years later, Tristan is a highly skilled warrior, loyal like a son to Marke. One day, Tristan, Melot, and Simon uncover an ancient Roman passage connecting the bridge to the Cornish castle's keep, and they pledge to keep its existence secret. During an Irish raid, Tristan, along with other Cornish warriors, attacks an Irish slave caravan. Simon is killed during the attack. Tristan kills Morholt, the leader of the army, his father's killer, and the betrothed of Donachadh's daughter, Princess Isolde.
Tristan is severely wounded in the fight and believed dead, but he is only suffering the effects of Morholt's poisoned sword. Put out to sea on a funeral boat, Tristan washes up on the shores of Ireland and is found by Isolde and her maid, Bragnae. Isolde conceals him from the Irish and tends to his wounds, using her healing skills to nurse him back to health. Warned by Bragnae not to reveal her true identity, Isolde tells Tristan her name is Bragnae and she is a lady-in-waiting at the court. Isolde and Tristan fall in love and begin a romance. The two lovers separate after Tristan's boat is discovered. Tristan returns to Cornwall. An astonished and overjoyed Marke welcomes Tristan back with open arms. Tristan, however, remains melancholy having parted with the woman who saved him.
Donachadh schemes to weaken Britain by dividing the tribes, proposing a peace treaty that offers Isolde's hand in marriage and valuable lands to the victor of a tournament. Tristan of Aragon wins the tournament on behalf of Marke, unaware Donachadh's daughter is the woman he fell in love with. When Tristan finds out the truth, he is heartbroken and bitter over the lie, but accepts it since her marriage to Marke will end the conflict between their people.
Marke and Isolde are married. He is kind to Isolde and genuinely falls in love with her. Isolde grows fond of Marke, but her heart still belongs to Tristan. Tristan has become withdrawn and distant towards Isolde and Marke, the latter of whom does not understand why; becoming especially concerned when Tristan casually disregards Marke's suggestion and encouragement to find a woman of his own to marry.
production_companies: QI Quality International GmbH Co. KG

documents.title: DOA: Dead or Alive
documents.tagline: They're the ultimate fighters. They've got the looks. They've got the moves, and the men fall at their feet.
documents.overview: Four beautiful rivals at an invitation-only martial-arts tournament join forces against a sinister threat. Princess Kasumi is an aristocratic warrior trained by martial-arts masters. Tina Armstrong is a wrestling superstar. Helena Douglas is an athlete with a tragic past. Christie Allen earns her keep as a thief and an assassin-for-hire.
documents.plot:
DOA: Dead or Alive is a 2006 martial arts action film directed by Corey Yuen and written by David Hayter, based on the popular video game series of the same name. The movie stars Nina Dobrev, Daniel Henney, and Jaime King.

The story begins with Casey (Nina Dobrev), an American woman who wins a trip to Japan as part of a reality TV show called "Dead or Alive." The show is hosted by Ryu Hayabusa (Daniel Henney), a Japanese martial artist, and his team. Casey's goal is to win the grand prize of $1 million.

Upon arrival in Japan, Casey meets Ryu and his teammates, including Leon (Tai Chi Master) and Jann Lee (Chris Klein). As the competition progresses, Casey finds herself caught up in a web of intrigue and deception, as she discovers that the show is not what it seems. The contestants are actually being forced to fight each other, with the last person standing winning the grand prize.

As Casey navigates the treacherous world of the Dead or Alive tournament, she must also contend with her own personal demons. Her sister, Samantha (Jaime King), was killed in a brutal attack by Jann Lee, and Casey is determined to avenge her death.

Throughout the movie, Casey forms alliances and friendships with Ryu and Leon, who become her allies in the fight against Jann Lee. The action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, showcasing the martial arts skills of the cast.

As the tournament reaches its climax, Casey faces off against Jann Lee in an epic battle. In the end, Casey emerges victorious, but not without scars. She wins the grand prize, but more importantly, she finds a sense of closure and revenge for her sister's death.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics, with some praising the action sequences and performances, while others found the plot to be predictable and formulaic. Despite this, DOA: Dead or Alive remains a fun and entertaining martial arts film, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

Overall, DOA: Dead or Alive is a thrilling and action-packed movie that explores themes of revenge, redemption, and self-discovery. With its talented cast and impressive fight choreography, it's a must-see for fans of martial arts films.

documents.title: Waking Life
documents.tagline: Dreams. What are they? An escape from reality or reality itself?
documents.overview: Waking Life is about a young man in a persistent lucid dream-like state. The film follows its protagonist as he initially observes and later participates in philosophical discussions that weave together issues like reality, free will, our relationships with others, and the meaning of life.
documents.plot:
An unnamed young man lives an ethereal existence that lacks transitions between everyday events and eventually progresses toward an existential crisis. He observes quietly but later participates actively in philosophical discussions involving other characters—ranging from quirky scholars and artists to everyday restaurant-goers and friends—about such issues as metaphysics, free will, social philosophy, and the meaning of life. Other scenes do not include the protagonist but rather focus on an isolated person, a group of people, or a couple engaging in such topics from a disembodied perspective. Along the way, the film also touches upon existentialism, situationist politics, posthumanity, the film theory of André Bazin, and lucid dreaming, and references various intellectual and literary figures by name.
Gradually, the protagonist realizes that he is living out a perpetual dream, broken up only by occasional false awakenings. So far, he is mostly a passive onlooker, though this changes during a chat with a passing woman who suddenly approaches him. After she greets him and shares her creative ideas with him, he reminds himself that she is a figment of his own dreaming imagination. Afterward, he starts to converse more openly with other dream characters, but begins to despair about being trapped in a dream.
The protagonist's final talk is with a character (played by Linklater) whom he briefly encountered earlier in the film. This conversation reveals this other character's view that reality may be only a single instant that a person interprets falsely as time (and, thus, life); that living is simply the person's constant negation of God's invitation to become one with the universe; that dreams offer a glimpse into the infinite nature of reality; and that to be free from the illusion called life, one need only accept God's invitation.
The protagonist is last seen walking into a driveway, when he suddenly begins to levitate, paralleling a scene at the start of the film of a floating boy in the same driveway. The protagonist uncertainly reaches for a car door handle but is too swiftly lifted above the vehicle and over the trees. He rises into the endless blue expanse of the sky until he disappears from view.

documents.title: The Four Feathers
documents.tagline: Freedom. Country. Honor. Passion. To save his best friend, one man must risk everything he loves.
documents.overview: The story, set in 1885, follows a British officer (Heath Ledger) who resigns his post when he learns of his regiment's plan to ship out to the Sudan for the conflict with the Mahdi. His friends and fiancée send him four white feathers which symbolize cowardice. To redeem his honor he disguises himself as an Arab and secretly saves the lives of those who branded him a coward.
documents.plot:
The Four Feathers is an epic war drama of 2002 directed by Shekhar Kapur, the latest of many screen adaptations of A. E. W. Mason's novel of 1902, here set during the British expedition to relieve General Gordon in the Sudan in 1884-85. Heath Ledger stars as Harry Faversham, with Wes Bentley as his friend Jack Durrance, Kate Hudson as his fiancée Ethne Eustace, Djimon Hounsou as the warrior Abou Fatma, Michael Sheen as William Trench and Kris Marshall as Edward Castleton.

Harry, a young British officer, celebrates his engagement to Ethne at a ball just as his regiment is ordered to the Sudan to rescue Gordon. Doubting the war, he resigns his commission. His father disowns him, and three of his friends and Ethne each send him a white feather, the mark of cowardice; Ethne ends their engagement. When Harry hears that Jack and his old regiment are heading into danger, he travels alone to the Sudan, disguises himself as an Arab and allies with Abou Fatma, a mercenary. Finding the fort at Abu Klea overrun by the Mahdi's forces, he sends Abou to warn the British, but they dismiss him as a spy and flog him.

The regiment is ambushed. The British square repels the first assault, but cavalry they take for reinforcements turn out to be Sudanese fighters in captured British uniforms, among them the disguised Harry. In the chaos, Castleton is killed by his own side's volleys and Jack is blinded when his rifle misfires. Harry rescues Jack and nurses him without revealing his identity, finding Ethne's letters to his friend. Back in England, Jack proposes to Ethne. Learning from Abou that Trench is held in the notorious prison at Omdurman, Harry lets himself be captured to free him. Starved and worked to exhaustion, the two despair until Abou smuggles in a poison that lets them feign death, and after killing the guards who follow them, Harry brings Trench home. Ethne takes back her feather and Harry's father welcomes him home; when the blind Jack touches Harry's face and recognises his rescuer, he releases Ethne, and Harry and Ethne are engaged once more.

Released by Paramount in September 2002, the film earned $29.8 million worldwide, short of its $35 million budget. Critics admired its visuals but not its storytelling, giving it 42% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: The Craft
documents.tagline: Welcome to the witching hour.
documents.overview: A Catholic school newcomer falls in with a clique of teen witches who wield their powers against all who dare to cross them -- be they teachers, rivals or meddlesome parents.
documents.plot:
Sarah Bailey, a troubled teenager with unusual abilities, moves from San Francisco to Los Angeles with her father and stepmother and starts attending an upscale Catholic School. At her new school, she befriends a trio of outcast girls rumored to be witches, each with their own troubles; Bonnie Harper bears burn scars over her body, Nancy Downs lives in a trailer with her mother and abusive stepfather, and Rochelle Zimmerman, a black student, endures racist bullying from a group of white girls. The three girls worship a powerful earth deity they call Manon.
Popular jock Chris Hooker shows interest in Sarah, which she reciprocates. When Bonnie sees Sarah levitating a pencil in class, the outcasts become convinced that she is "the fourth" they need to complete their coven—representing the Four Elements—and make them powerful. While walking home from school, the girls are approached by a vagrant who had earlier frightened Sarah with a snake (since a home invasion) when she moved in. As he chases her, he is struck and killed by a car. The girls believe their combined will caused the accident, strengthening their bond. It is also revealed that Sarah once attempted suicide.
After a date with Chris, Sarah is devastated when he spreads a false rumor that they had sex. Seeking revenge or change, each girl casts a spell: Sarah places a love spell on Chris, Rochelle curses her bully Laura Lizzie, Bonnie wishes for beauty, and Nancy asks for power. The spells succeed: Chris becomes obsessed with Sarah, Bonnie's scars miraculously heal, Laura's hair begins to fall out, and Nancy's stepfather dies of a heart attack, allowing her and her mother to collect his life insurance and move into a luxurious high-rise apartment.
Drunk on power, Nancy urges the others to join her in a ritual called Invocation of the Spirit—despite warnings from Lirio, the owner of a local occult shop and practicing witch. During the ritual, Nancy is struck by lightning. The next morning, she is seen walking on water, surrounded by beached sharks and other dead sea creatures. In the days that follow, Nancy becomes increasingly unstable and reckless, endangering herself and others.
The spells soon bring unintended consequences: Bonnie grows vain and cruel, Rochelle is disturbed to find Laura traumatized by her baldness, and Chris's obsession turns violent. When Sarah rejects his advances, Chris attempts to rape her. To punish him, Nancy uses a glamour spell to impersonate Sarah and tries to seduce him at a party. The real Sarah intervenes, but when Chris realizes Nancy's deception, he accuses her of jealousy. Furious, Nancy kills him by throwing him out a window.
Sarah attempts a binding spell to stop Nancy from causing more harm, but it fails, and the coven turns against her. They invade her dreams, conjure swarms of insects, and make her believe her family has died in a plane crash, driving her toward suicide.

documents.title: Screamers
documents.tagline: The last scream you hear will be your own.
documents.overview: SIRIUS 6B, Year 2078. On a distant mining planet ravaged by a decade of war, scientists have created the perfect weapon: a blade-wielding, self-replicating race of killing devices known as Screamers designed for one purpose only -- to hunt down and destroy all enemy life forms.
documents.plot: SIRIUS 6B, Year 2078. On a distant mining planet ravaged by a decade of war, scientists have created the perfect weapon: a blade-wielding, self-replicating race of killing devices known as Screamers designed for one purpose only -- to hunt down and destroy all enemy life forms.

documents.title: Buffalo Soldiers
documents.tagline: War is hell... but peace is f*#!%!! boring.
documents.overview: A criminal subculture operates among U.S. soldiers stationed in West Germany just before the fall of the Berlin wall.
documents.plot:
In 1989, U.S. Army Supply Specialist (SPC) Ray Elwood is a disillusioned enlisted soldier stationed in Stuttgart, West Germany. With much spare time, he participates in black marketeering and cooking heroin for several corrupt Military Police (MPs) led by the menacing Sergeant Saad. His firm yet empathic Commanding Officer, Colonel Berman, thinks of SPC Elwood as a close friend and has no idea he's stealing Brigade Command supplies and having an affair with his wife. However, Elwood's uneventful existence changes when a new First Sergeant (“Top” / 1SG), Robert E. Lee, joins the Brigade's supply company. Lee is a Vietnam combat veteran who presents a strict and intimidating demeanor, quickly determining that Elwood and his squad are engaged in graft and other criminal activities.
A three-man Army tank crew, under the strong influence of the heroin that Elwood cooked for the MPs, unintentionally kills two soldiers in charge of a weapons truck convoy by randomly crashing through a gas station's gasoline pumps and detonating them. Elwood stumbles across the trucks, discovers and steals the weapons, and hides them in medical equipment boxes stored at a missile base. When later harassed by Lee for his extravagant barracks room, Elwood's attempt at bribery backfires; Lee subsequently revokes Elwood's privileges, destroys his property, and orders a new, inexperienced and by-the-book Soldier, PFC Knoll, to bunk in his room. To get back at Lee, Elwood begins a sexual relationship with his daughter, Robyn. Lee retaliates by making Elwood destroy his beloved Mercedes-Benz Coupé with an M60 machine gun during a live-fire weapons exercise. Lee also boobytraps a locker that is used to hide heroin with a grenade that kills Stoney, one of Elwood's friends.
Elwood sells the stolen weapons to a Turkish gangster, accepting a large amount of raw opium as payment. However, to save Knoll from being killed by Saad in a fight, Elwood is forced to make Saad a business partner in cooking the opium. In order to retrieve the weapons from the missile base and collect the drugs, Elwood sells out Berman so a competing infantry regiment can easily capture their positions during a mobilization/defense operations exercise. Later, Berman reluctantly tells Elwood he has been relieved from Brigade Command but this has given him time to reflect — he will retire from the Army and buy a vineyard in California.
On 9 November, the night the Berlin Wall comes down, Elwood sneaks to the base swimming pool to meet Robyn while the opium is being cooked by his squad and the MPs. Knoll and Lee arrive. Elwood then discovers Knoll is actually an undercover 2nd Lieutenant from the Inspector General's Office and Criminal Investigation Division. While Knoll escorts Robyn away, she tells him her father intends to kill Elwood, something Knoll – as a professional officer – cannot allow.

documents.title: Broken Arrow
documents.tagline: Prepare to Go Ballistic.
documents.overview: When rogue stealth-fighter pilot Vic Deakins deliberately drops off the radar while on maneuvers, the Air Force ends up with two stolen nuclear warheads -- and Deakins's co-pilot, Riley Hale, is the military's only hope for getting them back. Traversing the deserted canyons of Utah, Hale teams with park ranger Terry Carmichael to put Deakins back in his box.
documents.plot:
Broken Arrow is a 1996 American action thriller film directed by John Woo and starring John Travolta, Christian Slater, and Sandra Bullock.

The movie begins with Colonel Mitchell "Mitch" Gary (John Travolta) and Captain Riley Hale (Christian Slater), two top-ranking pilots in the United States Air Force. They are part of an elite unit known as the 366th Tactical Fighter Wing, stationed at Edwards Air Force Base in California. The two men have a long-standing rivalry, with Mitch being the more experienced and respected pilot.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Mitch is shot down by his own wingman, Riley Hale, during a training exercise gone wrong. As Mitch lies dying, he reveals that he has been working on a top-secret project codenamed "Broken Arrow," which involves developing a new, highly advanced missile system capable of delivering nuclear warheads.

Before he dies, Mitch entrusts Riley with the location of the Broken Arrow facility and warns him about the dangers of the project. Unbeknownst to Riley, his brother, Sean (played by Brendan Fraser), is also involved in the project as a scientist.

As Riley tries to make sense of the situation, he discovers that his brother has been working on the Broken Arrow system with Mitch's help. However, their efforts have attracted unwanted attention from rogue elements within the government and military, who seek to exploit the technology for their own gain.

Riley soon finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with a group of ruthless agents led by Colonel Frank Adams (played by Gary Busey). As he tries to protect his brother and prevent the Broken Arrow system from falling into the wrong hands, Riley must also confront his own demons and work to redeem himself in the eyes of his superiors.

Throughout the film, Woo's signature style is on full display, with rapid-fire action sequences, stunning aerial stunts, and a healthy dose of humor. The chemistry between Travolta and Slater is undeniable, and their rivalry adds an extra layer of tension to the story.

As the stakes grow higher, Riley must use all his skills and resources to outwit his enemies and prevent a catastrophic disaster. In the end, he succeeds in destroying the Broken Arrow facility and preventing the misuse of the technology.

The film concludes with Riley reflecting on the events that transpired and the lessons he learned about loyalty, duty, and redemption. The final shot is of the two brothers, Sean and Riley, reunited and at peace, as the camera pans out to reveal the vast expanse of the American desert landscape.

Overall, Broken Arrow is a thrilling action movie with a strong cast, clever plot twists, and impressive aerial sequences. While it may not be Woo's most critically acclaimed film, it remains a beloved classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: S.W.A.T.
documents.tagline: You're either S.W.A.T. or you're not.
documents.overview: Hondo Harrelson recruits Jim Street to join an elite unit of the Los Angeles Police Department. Together they seek out more members, including tough Deke Kay and single mom Chris Sanchez. The team's first big assignment is to escort crime boss Alex Montel to prison. It seems routine, but when Montel offers a huge reward to anyone who can break him free, criminals of various stripes step up for the prize.
documents.plot:
S.W.A.T. is a 2003 American action film directed by Tony Scott, starring Keanu Reeves, Samuel L. Jackson, and Lindsay Lohan.

The movie begins with the introduction of Chris Sanders (Keanu Reeves), a former Marine who joins the Los Angeles Police Department's Special Weapons and Tactics team, also known as S.W.A.T. The team is led by Lieutenant Dan 'Hondo' Harrelson (Samuel L. Jackson), a seasoned veteran with a no-nonsense attitude.

The story takes a turn when Chris is paired with rookie officer Trudy Shaw (Lindsay Lohan) and the two begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their budding relationship is put to the test as they face various challenges on the job.

One of the main plot points revolves around a wealthy businessman named Robert Hawkins (Owen Wilson), who has been kidnapped by a group of terrorists led by Captain Dan 'Mac' MacDougall (Robert Patrick). The team must navigate through the city's streets and buildings to rescue Hawkins, while also dealing with their own personal demons.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Hawkins is not just any ordinary hostage. He possesses information about a deadly virus that could potentially wipe out millions of people. The terrorists plan to use this information to hold the world hostage and demand a massive ransom in exchange for Hawkins' safe return.

The S.W.A.T. team must work together to stop the terrorists and prevent the spread of the virus. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, rival law enforcement agencies, and personal conflicts within the team.

As the stakes grow higher, Chris and Trudy find themselves in a cat-and-mouse game with Mac and his accomplices. The action unfolds at a breakneck pace, with intense shootouts, car chases, and hand-to-hand combat sequences.

In the end, the S.W.A.T. team manages to rescue Hawkins and prevent the virus from being released. However, not before several characters meet their demise, including Mac, who sacrifices himself to save his teammates.

The movie concludes with Chris and Trudy sharing a moment of triumph and intimacy, as they reflect on the events that have transpired. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the S.W.A.T. team standing together, ready to face whatever challenges come their way next.

Overall, S.W.A.T. is an action-packed thrill ride that explores themes of loyalty, duty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, the film has since developed a cult following and remains a beloved entry in the action genre.

documents.title: My Mom's New Boyfriend
documents.tagline: His mom is dating his suspect. Let the surveillance begin.
documents.overview: Henry Durand is a young federal agent who is given a difficult assignment: spy on his mother and her boyfriend who is suspected of leading a gang of art thieves.
documents.plot: After several years away, FBI agent Henry Durand returns to find his mother, Marty, a much different person: Having long mourned for Henry's father, she is now embracing single life. One day, while Marty, Henry and his new fiancée, Emily, are out for a walk, they meet Tommy, a mysterious stranger with whom Marty then becomes involved. However, through his FBI contacts, Henry learns that Tommy is suspected of being an art thief. As a young federal agent, Henry is given a difficult assignment: spy on his mother and her boyfriend who is suspected of leading a gang of art thieves.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG

documents.title: Blue Crush
documents.tagline: Three Friends, One Passion, No Limits.
documents.overview: Nothing gets between Anne Marie and her board. Living in a beach shack with three roommates, she is up before dawn every morning to conquer the waves and count the days until the Pipe Masters competition. Having transplanted herself to Hawaii with no one's blessing but her own, Anne Marie finds all she needs in the adrenaline-charged surf scene - until pro quarterback Matt Tollman comes along...
documents.plot:
Anne Marie, her fourteen-year-old sister Penny, and good friends Eden and Lena live in a small house on the North Shore. They all have been helping to raise Penny since her and Anne Marie's mother moved to Las Vegas with her boyfriend. While Penny is at school, Anne Marie, Eden, and Lena work as maids in a luxury resort hotel and surfing in their spare time. As a child, Anne Marie had been a rising star in women's surfing until a near-fatal wipeout left her with a paralyzing fear of powerful waves. Although she rises every morning before dawn to train for her surfing comeback, this fear continues to hamper her progress. Her friends, especially Eden, encourage her to overcome her trauma, conquer her fear of big waves, and become a professional surfer.
Anne Marie is invited to join the surfing competition at a famed North Shore surf spot, the challenging Banzai Pipeline. If she can do well enough to gain the attention of a sponsor, it can lift her and her friends out of the near-poverty in which they live. As the Pipeline competition gets closer, Anne Marie struggles to keep Penny from running wild and deal with family issues.
Anne Marie meets Matt Tollman, a National Football League quarterback who is in Hawaii for the Pro Bowl. He is instantly attracted to the surfer, especially after she boldly confronts another NFL Pro Bowler who had trashed his hotel room, leaving a mess for Anne Marie and her friends to clean. After a few encounters, Matt says that he wants to learn to surf, and Anne Marie agrees to teach him and several of his teammates to surf for $150 per hour, with Lena, Eden, and Penny acting as coaches. Anne Marie sees Matt again while getting the money from the hotel room, but a call comes for Matt from another woman. Anne Marie asks if it is Matt's wife, but he explains that it is his niece. Later, they sleep together.
Anne Marie's acceptance of an outsider as her boyfriend causes friction between her and some young male surfers on the North Shore. Eden points out to Anne Marie that her current interest in Matt has weakened her commitment to training for the Pipeline contest. Anne Marie also overhears demeaning comments about herself from some of the other football players' wives and girlfriends staying at the hotel.
Anne Marie confronts Matt about the situation and resolves to step up her game, fully committing herself to the Pipeline Masters. On the day of Pipeline, Anne Marie wipes out during her first attempt, but she advances after narrowly beating pro surfer Kate Skarratt. She is shaken, but Matt tells her how he failed in his first game as an NFL quarterback, which helps her regain her wavering confidence.
Determined, although still apprehensive, Anne Marie returns to surfing. Competing in the same set is Keala Kennelly, one of the first professional female surfers. While Keala surfs the first few sets of waves well, Anne Marie is still reluctant to try one, visions of her near-drowning incident holding her back.

documents.title: Eraser
documents.tagline: He will erase your past to protect your future.
documents.overview: U.S. Marshall John Kruger erases the identities of people enrolled in the Witness Protection Program. His current assignment is to protect Lee Cullen, who's uncovered evidence that the weapons manufacturer she works for has been selling to terrorist groups. When Kruger discovers that there's a corrupt agent within the program, he must guard his own life while trying to protect Lee's.
documents.plot: Eraser, an elite federal marshal who "erases" the pasts of jeopardized informers and relocates them into safe anonymity, must protect a moving target who stands to uncover a conspiracy that could shift the balance of power in the world forever.

documents.title: Brick
documents.tagline: A detective story.
documents.overview: A teenage loner pushes his way into the underworld of a high school crime ring to investigate the disappearance of his ex-girlfriend.
documents.plot:
High school student Brendan Frye discovers a note directing him to a pay phone, where he receives a call from his ex-girlfriend Emily Kostich, begging him for help. She mentions a "bad brick", "the Pin", and "Tug" before abruptly hanging up, apparently afraid of a passing black Ford Mustang, from which a distinctively-branded cigarette is thrown. Unable to locate Emily, Brendan enlists his friend Brain for help. An encounter with another ex-girlfriend, Kara, leads him to a party held by flirtatious upper-class girl Laura Dannon and her boyfriend, Brad Bramish. Laura points Brendan to Dode, Emily's drug-addicted new boyfriend, who arranges a meeting with Emily.
Emily dismisses the phone call as a mistake and tells Brendan to let her go. Brendan steals her notepad and finds a note that leads him to her dead body in a tunnel the following morning where he is beaten by an unidentified assailant. Brendan decides to investigate her murder, hiding the body deeper within the tunnel to avoid police involvement. With help from Brain, Brendan realizes that "the Pin" refers to a local kingpin. Brendan picks a fight with Brad, hoping to attract the Pin's attention. Later, a man wearing a beanie attacks Brendan.
Later Brendan sees the black Mustang in a parking lot and is attacked by the beanie-wearing thug as he demands to meet the Pin instead of fighting back. The man, revealed as Tug, the Pin's main enforcer, takes Brendan to the Pin's house. Laura reveals that she was at the Pin's house as well and drives Brendan back to school. She explains that Emily stole a "brick" of heroin after being rejected by the Pin's operation. Laura offers to help Brendan, but he distrusts her.
The next day, the Pin hires Brendan. Dode calls Brendan and says he saw Brendan hide Emily's body and believes Brendan killed Emily. Brendan meets the Pin, who suspects that Tug is planning to betray him. At the Pin's house, Tug tells Brendan that the Pin had bought ten bricks of heroin and eight were sold off wholesale, the ninth was stolen and returned contaminated, and the final brick remains to be sold. The Pin reveals that Tug was also romantically involved with Emily.
Brendan intercepts Dode on the way to the meeting and discovers Emily was pregnant when she died; Dode believes the baby was his. Brendan arrives at the meeting to find Dode demanding money to reveal who killed Emily. Tug goes berserk and shoots Dode in the head, then threatens the Pin, who walks away as Brendan faints. Brendan awakens in Tug's bedroom, and Tug tells him they are at war with the Pin.
Brendan arranges a meeting between the two and waits in Tug's bedroom.
