Laura comforts him as he grieves for Emily, and he recognizes her cigarette as the same brand that was dropped from the Mustang during the call with Emily. At the meeting, chaos erupts when it is discovered that the tenth brick is missing. Tug beats the Pin to death while Brendan flees, escaping just as police arrive.

documents.title: Death to Smoochy
documents.tagline: Get ready for an unexpected hit.
documents.overview: Tells the story of Rainbow Randolph, the corrupt, costumed star of a popular children's TV show, who is fired over a bribery scandal and replaced by squeaky-clean Smoochy, a puffy fuscia rhinoceros. As Smoochy catapults to fame - scoring hit ratings and the affections of a network executive - Randolph makes the unsuspecting rhino the target of his numerous outrageous attempts to exact revenge and reclaim his status as America's sweetheart.
documents.plot: Tells the story of Rainbow Randolph, the corrupt, costumed star of a popular children's TV show, who is fired over a bribery scandal and replaced by squeaky-clean Smoochy, a puffy fuchsia rhinoceros. As Smoochy catapults to fame - scoring hit ratings and the affections of a network executive - Randolph makes the unsuspecting rhino the target of his numerous outrageous attempts to exact revenge and reclaim his status as America's sweetheart.

documents.title: Femme Fatale
documents.tagline: Nothing is more desirable or more deadly than a woman with a secret.
documents.overview: A $10-million diamond rip-off, a stolen identity, a new life married to a diplomat. Laure Ash has risked big, won big. But then a tabloid shutterbug snaps her picture in Paris, and suddenly, enemies from Laure's secret past know who and where she is. And they all want their share of the diamond heist. Or her life. Or both.
documents.plot:
Femme Fatale is a 2002 neo-noir erotic thriller written and directed by Brian De Palma, starring Rebecca Romijn as the thief Laure Ash and Antonio Banderas as Nicolas Bardo, a Spanish paparazzo. The film is built around De Palma's signature visual style and a dreamlike structure, with an elaborate heist sequence set at the Cannes festival.

The story opens during the Cannes Film Festival, where Laure, a mercenary thief, is part of a team attempting to steal diamonds worn as part of a gold costume by a model attending a premiere. Laure seduces the model to get hold of the jewels while her accomplices provide support, but the heist goes wrong and Laure double-crosses her partners, escaping to Paris with the diamonds. There she is mistaken for Lily, a woman who has recently disappeared and who closely resembles her. When Laure witnesses the real Lily take her own life, she assumes her identity and leaves for the United States.

Seven years later, Laure returns to Paris as the wife of Bruce Watts, the new American ambassador to France. Bardo photographs her, and when the picture is published across the city, her former accomplices, one of them just released from prison, discover where she is and set out for revenge. To escape them, Laure manipulates Bardo into helping her stage her own kidnapping and demand a ransom from her husband, and the two begin an affair. When Bardo has second thoughts, the scheme turns deadly, and a final twist forces the audience to reconsider everything that has come before.

The film plays with themes of identity, fate and voyeurism, and its surprise ending, which reframes much of the story, has been widely debated.

Femme Fatale screened out of competition at the 2002 Cannes Film Festival. It was a box office failure, grossing about 16.8 million dollars worldwide, less than its production costs, and received mixed reviews; Rotten Tomatoes gives it 49 percent approval and Metacritic a score of 60. Roger Ebert gave it four stars, and the film has since been reappraised by many critics and is now regarded as a cult classic.

documents.title: Final Destination 3
documents.tagline: This ride will be the death of you.
documents.overview: A student's premonition of a deadly rollercoaster ride saves her life and a lucky few, but not from death itself – which seeks out those who escaped their fate.
documents.plot:
Final Destination 3 is a supernatural horror film directed by James Wong, released in 2006 by New Line Cinema.

The movie begins with Clear Rivers (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), a high school student who survives a roller coaster accident at an amusement park. She had been warned not to get on the ride by her friend, Kevin Williamson (Ryan Merriman), but she ignored him. As a result of this warning, Clear is haunted by premonitions and visions of death.

Clear's friends, including her boyfriend, Wexler (Chad Donella), and her friends from school, are also at the amusement park on the same day as Clear. However, they all die in a series of gruesome accidents, which Clear tries to prevent using her knowledge of impending doom.

The first accident occurs when Wexler is crushed by a falling roller coaster car. The second accident happens when Kevin's girlfriend, Clear's friend, is killed by a malfunctioning funhouse ride. The third accident involves a group of teenagers who are trapped in a burning amusement park building.

As the accidents continue to occur, Clear realizes that she has the ability to see and prevent these events from happening. However, each time she tries to warn her friends or take action to prevent an accident, something goes wrong, and they still die.

Clear becomes increasingly isolated as she struggles to understand why her warnings are not being heeded. She also starts to question whether she is truly able to change the course of events or if she is just seeing things that will inevitably happen.

In the end, Clear realizes that she has been given a chance to cheat death and escape the cycle of premonitions. However, in doing so, she must confront her own mortality and make a choice between saving herself or trying to save others.

The movie ends with Clear escaping the amusement park by jumping off a bridge just as it is about to collapse. She then watches from a distance as the bridge implodes, killing everyone on board. The film concludes with Clear reflecting on the events that have transpired and wondering if she has truly escaped death or if there are still more premonitions waiting for her.

Overall, Final Destination 3 explores themes of mortality, fate, and the consequences of ignoring warnings from others. The movie's twist ending adds to the suspense and surprise, leaving viewers questioning what is real and what is just a product of Clear's imagination.
production_companies: Kumar Mobiliengesellschaft mbH & Co. Projekt Nr. 1 KG

documents.title: Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God
documents.original_title: Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God
documents.overview: Due to a curse from his former master Profion, Damodar survived his death by Ridley Freeborn as an undead entity in pursuit of an evil artifact for some hundred years, so that he might be capable of unleashing unstoppable destruction on Izmir and the descendants of those who caused his demise.
documents.plot:
One hundred years after being defeated by Ridley Freeborn and being cursed by his former master Profion to walk the earth as an undead entity, Damodar is revived. Driven insane by the curse, he seeks revenge against the kingdom of Izmir and the descendants of those who defeated him.
After years of searching with the aid of two dark-talon lizardfolk shamans, he locates the Orb of Faluzure, an ancient artifact linked to the power of Faluzure, a dragon god imprisoned under Saragasso's mountains. With the Orb's power, he heals the curse and prepares to awaken the dragon to destroy Izmir.
Fighter Lord Berek, a former captain of the king's guard, and his wife Melora, a young mage, investigate reports of poison gas emanating from Saragasso's caves and find the still-slumbering dragon. Researching the threat in Izmir's library, Melora reports to Oberon, the head of the Mages' Council, that Faluzure was imprisoned three thousand years before by the Turanians, an ancient civilization who also created the Orb. While trying to locate the Orb through magic, Melora is cursed by Damodar and begins dying slowly.
She hides her illness from Berek, who is appointed by the King to assemble a party of adventurers to infiltrate Damodar's lair: barbarian Lux; Dorian, a Cleric of Obad-Hai; elven wizard Ormaline; and master thief Nim. They resolve to locate the vault of the warlock Malek, a worshiper of the demon Juiblex who was gifted the Pool of Sight, a magical scrying pool; the pool might allow them to penetrate Damodar's defenses and reveal the orb's location.
The party sets out to locate Malek's Vault, while Oberon and the other mages try to decipher the tomes of Turanian magic in their library, to find a way to defeat Faluzure. While traveling through a haunted forest, Berek's party catches the attention of Klaxx the Maligned, a lich who offers his services to Damodar. Damodar does not trust him, but thinks that the Orb makes him more powerful than Klaxx. After confronting a white dragon, and losing Dorian in the fight, Berek's party finds the pool, securing their way to Damodar's castle. Confronting him, Berek steal the Orb, though Ormaline and Nim are badly wounded before the wizard teleports them to the Temple of Obad-Hai. While the clerics treat Ormaline and Nim, Berek returns to Izmir, Lux staying behind to delay demons summoned by Damodar.
Using his shape-changing abilities, Klaxx infiltrates Izmir's castle, kills Oberon, and assumes his shape. When Berek returns with the Orb, Melora uses it to unlock a vault discovered beneath the castle, where the Turanians hid the secrets of their magic. Klaxx reveals himself, stealing the Orb back and killing the King and many others before returning the Orb to Damodar. Faluzure awakens and destroys the Orb, regaining his godly power.

documents.title: Crocodile Dundee in Los Angeles
documents.tagline: He heard there was wildlife in L.A. He didn't know how wild.
documents.overview: After settling in the tiny Australian town of Walkabout Creek with his significant other and his young son, Mick "Crocodile" Dundee is thrown for a loop when a prestigious Los Angeles newspaper offers his honey a job. The family migrates back to the United States, and Croc and son soon find themselves learning some lessons about American life -- many of them inadvertent
documents.plot:
Crocodile Dundee in Los Angeles is a 2001 action comedy directed by Simon Wincer and starring Paul Hogan. It is the third and final installment of the Crocodile Dundee series and a sequel to Crocodile Dundee II (1988). Hogan and Linda Kozlowski return as Michael "Crocodile" Dundee and Sue Charlton, joined by Jere Burns, Jonathan Banks, Alec Wilson and Serge Cockburn as their young son. The film was shot in Los Angeles and in Queensland, and Hogan said the idea for its story came to him while touring the Czech town of Litomyšl in 1993.

Thirteen years after the previous film, Mick lives in the Australian outback with Sue and their son Mikey. Crocodile hunting has been outlawed, so Mick now earns his living wrestling crocodiles for tourists and competing with a rival bushman named Jacko. When Sue is offered the job of Los Angeles bureau chief for a newspaper owned by her father, the family moves across the Pacific. Mick and Mikey soon run into a series of culture-clash misadventures in Southern California, while Mikey wins over his classmates and his teacher with the survival skills he learned in the bush.

Sue's predecessor at the paper died in suspicious circumstances, and Mick becomes an undercover amateur detective to help find out what happened. The trail leads to a film studio that is inexplicably making a sequel to a flop action film called Lethal Agent. Mick grows suspicious when crates of paintings from southern Europe arrive on the set. At first he assumes drugs are being smuggled, but the canvases turn out to be valuable artworks missing from a museum in the former Yugoslavia and thought to have been lost during the war. The production plans to burn them as props on camera after quietly swapping them for copies. With Jacko flown in to babysit Mikey, Mick and Sue try to get hold of one painting as evidence and end up taking on the studio's criminals, using props and a trio of film lions.

The film was released in April 2001 and grossed about $39 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative, calling it an unnecessary sequel that came too long after the earlier films and relied on fish-out-of-water humor that had grown stale.

documents.title: The Longest Yard
documents.tagline: If you can't get out, get even.
documents.overview: Pro quarter-back, Paul Crewe and former college champion and coach, Nate Scarboro are doing time in the same prison. Asked to put together a team of inmates to take on the guards, Crewe enlists the help of Scarboro to coach the inmates to victory in a football game 'fixed' to turn out quite another way.
documents.plot:
The Longest Yard is a sports comedy film directed by Peter Segal, released in 2005. The movie stars Adam Sandler as Paul Crewe, a former NFL quarterback who becomes a coach at a minimum-security prison.

Paul Crewe (Adam Sandler) was once a successful NFL quarterback but lost his job and reputation after being involved in a scandal that led to the death of an opponent on the field. He is sentenced to 3 years in prison for manslaughter. While serving his time, he becomes the coach of the prison's football team, which has not won a game in over 40 years.

Crewe's goal is to lead the team to victory and prove that even in a place like this, there can be redemption and hope. However, he faces opposition from the corrupt warden, George "The King" Weathers (Burt Reynolds), who wants to keep the prison's football team losing so that the inmates will stay docile and obedient.

As Crewe tries to whip his team into shape, he also has to deal with the harsh realities of prison life. He befriends a fellow inmate, Caretaker (Chris Rock), who becomes his assistant coach. Together, they try to motivate their teammates and overcome the obstacles that stand in their way.

Throughout the movie, Crewe's character undergoes significant development as he learns to balance his desire for revenge against Weathers with his newfound sense of purpose and responsibility as a coach. He also starts to form connections with some of the inmates, including Caretaker, who becomes like a protégé to him.

As the team begins to win games, Crewe's reputation grows, and he becomes a symbol of hope for the inmates. However, Weathers will stop at nothing to crush their spirits and maintain his own power over the prison.

In the climactic final game, Crewe's team faces off against Weathers' favorite team, led by the ruthless and arrogant quarterback, Shane Falco (David Spade). The game is intense, with both teams fighting for victory. In the end, Crewe's team emerges victorious, and he finally gets his revenge against Weathers.

The movie ends on a high note, with Crewe's team celebrating their win and Crewe himself finding redemption and a new sense of purpose. He has proven that even in the darkest of places, there is always hope for change and redemption.

Overall, The Longest Yard is a fun and entertaining movie that combines humor, action, and heart. It features strong performances from Adam Sandler and Burt Reynolds, as well as a talented supporting cast.

documents.title: Monster House
documents.tagline: The house is . . . alive!
documents.overview: Monsters under the bed are scary enough, but what happens when an entire house is out to get you? Three teens aim to find out when they go up against a decrepit neighboring home and unlock its frightening secrets.
documents.plot:
Monster House is a 2006 computer-animated comedy-horror film produced by DreamWorks Animation and Amblin Entertainment. The movie follows the story of a mysterious house that seems to have a life of its own.

The story begins with the introduction of three children: DJ (voiced by Spencer Locke), Chowder (voiced by Sam Lerner), and Jenny (voiced by Megan Mullally). They live in the suburban town of Suburbia, where everyone knows each other's business. The house at 1313 Cemetery Lane is a source of fascination for the kids, as it seems to be alive and has a mind of its own.

As the story progresses, we learn that the house was built by a former owner named Mr. Nebbercracker (voiced by Steve Buscemi), who died under mysterious circumstances. The house has been terrorizing the neighborhood ever since, causing chaos and destruction wherever it goes.

DJ, Chowder, and Jenny decide to team up to solve the mystery of the haunted house. They soon discover that the house is actually a monster in disguise, with a personality of its own. The house, which they name "Monster House," has a mind of its own and seems to be alive.

As the kids delve deeper into the mystery, they learn that Monster House was once a normal house built by Mr. Nebbercracker. However, after his death, the house became possessed by the spirit of Mr. Nebbercracker's son, who died in the house many years ago. The son's ghost is trapped inside the house and is seeking revenge on the living.

The kids come up with a plan to help the ghost find peace and move on from the mortal world. They work together to uncover the secrets of Monster House and ultimately succeed in helping the ghost resolve its unfinished business.

In the end, DJ, Chowder, and Jenny are hailed as heroes for solving the mystery of Monster House. The house is no longer a source of terror, but rather a symbol of their bravery and friendship. The movie ends with the kids standing in front of the house, which has been transformed into a beautiful garden, a testament to the power of teamwork and determination.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the characters and the monster house to life. The voice acting is also top-notch, with each character bringing their own unique personality to the story. Overall, Monster House is a fun and spooky animated film that is suitable for both kids and adults.

documents.title: Flightplan
documents.tagline: If someone took everything you live for... how far would you go to get it back?
documents.overview: Flying at 40,000 feet in a state-of-the art aircraft that she helped design, Kyle Pratt's 6-year-old daughter Julia vanishes without a trace. Or did she? No one on the plane believes Julia was ever onboard. And now Kyle, desperate and alone, can only count on her own wits to unravel the mystery and save her daughter.
documents.plot: Flying at 40,000 feet in a state-of-the art aircraft that she helped design, Kyle Pratt's 6-year-old daughter Julia vanishes without a trace. Or did she? No one on the plane believes Julia was ever onboard. And now Kyle, desperate and alone, can only count on her own wits to unravel the mystery and save her daughter.

documents.title: Ong Bak: Muay Thai Warrior
documents.tagline: No computer graphics. No stunt doubles. No wires.
documents.overview: When the head of a statue sacred to a village is stolen, a young martial artist goes to the big city and finds himself taking on the underworld to retrieve it.
documents.plot:
Ong Bak: Muay Thai Warrior is a 2003 martial arts film directed by Prachya Pinkaew, starring Tony Jaa as the titular character. The movie is set in 13th-century Siam (now Thailand) and tells the story of Ong Bak, a young man who seeks revenge against those who killed his father.

The film begins with Ong Bak, played by Tony Jaa, as a young boy who lives with his father, a skilled Muay Thai fighter. When Ong Bak's father is brutally murdered by the corrupt and power-hungry General Mongkut (Sorapong Chatree), Ong Bak vows to avenge his father's death.

Ong Bak sets out on a journey to find General Mongkut, facing numerous challenges and obstacles along the way. He meets a group of traveling performers who take him in and teach him the ways of Muay Thai. As Ong Bak trains with the performers, he also learns about the importance of honor, loyalty, and self-discipline.

As Ong Bak's skills as a fighter improve, he becomes determined to confront General Mongkut and bring justice to his father's memory. The film's action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, showcasing Tony Jaa's impressive martial arts skills.

Throughout the movie, Ong Bak faces various adversaries, including General Mongkut's henchmen and a group of bandits. However, he also encounters a mysterious woman named Lin (Petchtai Wongkamlao), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

As the story unfolds, Ong Bak discovers that General Mongkut is using his power to exploit the poor and vulnerable people in Siam. Ong Bak's quest for revenge becomes a mission to bring justice and protect the innocent.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Ong Bak and General Mongkut, with Ong Bak emerging victorious. In the end, Ong Bak finds some measure of closure and redemption, but not before facing his own personal demons and confronting the harsh realities of the world around him.

Overall, Ong Bak: Muay Thai Warrior is a thrilling and visually stunning film that showcases Tony Jaa's impressive martial arts skills and the rich cultural heritage of Thailand. The movie's themes of honor, loyalty, and self-discipline are timeless and universal, making it a compelling watch for audiences worldwide.

documents.title: The Scorpion King
documents.tagline: Warrior. Legend. King.
documents.overview: In ancient Egypt, peasant Mathayus is hired to exact revenge on the powerful Memnon and the sorceress Cassandra, who are ready to overtake Balthazar's village. Amid betrayals, thieves, abductions and more, Mathayus strives to bring justice to his complicated world.
documents.plot:
The Scorpion King is a 2002 American fantasy adventure film directed by Chuck Russell and written by David Hayter. The movie serves as a prequel to The Mummy Returns, starring Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In ancient Egypt, the story begins with Mathayus (Dwayne Johnson), a young orphan who grows up on the streets of Memphis. He is discovered by a group of mercenaries and trained in combat skills by the leader, General Kane (Steven Brand). Kane becomes like a father to Mathayus, teaching him how to fight and survive.

As Mathayus grows older, he becomes a skilled warrior and earns the respect of his comrades. However, Kane's true intentions are revealed: he plans to overthrow the Pharaoh and take control of Egypt for himself. Mathayus is torn between his loyalty to Kane and his growing sense of morality.

When Kane's plan fails, he is betrayed by his own men and left for dead. Mathayus finds him dying and nurses him back to health. As Kane lies on his deathbed, he reveals that the Scorpion King is a legendary figure who will one day bring about great change in Egypt.

Kane dies, but not before giving Mathayus a magical amulet that allows him to control the sand worms of the desert. With this newfound power, Mathayus sets out to avenge Kane's death and claim his rightful place as the Scorpion King.

Mathayus faces numerous challenges on his journey, including fierce battles with rival warriors and treacherous desert landscapes. Along the way, he meets a woman named Chandra (Kelly Hu), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

As Mathayus draws closer to his goal, he must confront his own demons and learn to harness his newfound powers. In the end, he defeats Kane's successor, General Sargon (Michael Clarke Duncan), and claims the throne of Egypt as the Scorpion King.

The movie ends with Mathayus standing victorious, but also aware that his journey is far from over. He has become a legendary figure, feared and respected by all who know him. The final shot is of the magical amulet, still glowing with power, as the camera pans out to reveal the vast expanse of the desert landscape.

Overall, The Scorpion King is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of loyalty, power, and redemption. Dwayne Johnson's performance as Mathayus brings depth and nuance to the character, making him a compelling hero on screen.

documents.title: Transporter 2
documents.tagline: The Best In The Business Is Back In The Game.
documents.overview: Professional driver Frank Martin is living in Miami, where he is temporarily filling in for a friend as the chauffeur for a government narcotics control policymaker and his family. The young boy in the family is targeted for kidnapping, and Frank immediately becomes involved in protecting the child and exposing the kidnappers.
documents.plot:
Transporter 2 is a 2005 action film directed by Louis Leterrier and starring Jason Statham as the main protagonist, Frank Martin.

The movie begins with Frank Martin (Jason Statham) living a peaceful life in Paris, France. He has retired from his high-stakes transportation business and is now running a small courier service. However, his quiet life is disrupted when he receives a package from an unknown client containing a briefcase that contains the stolen $100 million worth of diamonds.

The client, who remains anonymous throughout the film, instructs Frank to deliver the briefcase to a specific location in Istanbul, Turkey. Unbeknownst to Frank, the briefcase contains more than just diamonds; it also holds the key to a powerful and deadly virus that could wipe out millions of people worldwide.

As Frank embarks on his journey to Istanbul, he is pursued by a team of skilled assassins hired by a mysterious organization known as the "Terrorist". The Terrorist's true intentions are unclear, but their goal is evident: they want to use the virus to hold the world hostage and gain control over global politics.

Throughout the film, Frank faces numerous challenges and obstacles as he navigates through the crowded streets of Istanbul. He encounters a beautiful woman named Lai (Shu Qi), who becomes his ally in the quest to deliver the briefcase. Together, they must evade the Terrorist's henchmen and stay one step ahead of their pursuers.

As Frank gets closer to his destination, he realizes that the Terrorist's true intentions are far more sinister than he initially thought. The virus is not just a simple biological agent; it has the potential to cause widespread destruction and chaos on a global scale.

In the climactic final act, Frank and Lai face off against the leader of the Terrorist organization in an intense hand-to-hand combat sequence. Frank manages to outsmart his opponents and deliver the briefcase to its intended destination, but not before the Terrorist's true identity is revealed: it is none other than Frank's former business partner, who has been seeking revenge against him for years.

The film concludes with Frank returning to Paris, where he is greeted as a hero by Lai. However, the movie ends on a somber note, hinting that Frank's life will never be the same again. The Terrorist's plan may have been foiled, but the world is now aware of the deadly virus, and Frank knows that his skills as a transporter are still in high demand.

Overall, Transporter 2 is an action-packed thrill ride that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. Jason Statham delivers a memorable performance as the charismatic and resourceful Frank Martin, making this film a must-see for fans of the action genre.

documents.title: Click
documents.tagline: What If You Had A Remote... That Controlled Your Universe?
documents.overview: A married workaholic, Michael Newman doesn't have time for his wife and children, not if he's to impress his ungrateful boss and earn a well-deserved promotion. So when he meets Morty, a loopy sales clerk, he gets the answer to his prayers: a magical remote that allows him to bypass life's little distractions with increasingly hysterical results.
documents.plot:
Click is a 2006 American fantasy comedy film directed by Frank Coraci and produced by Adam Sandler Productions. The movie stars Adam Sandler, Kate Beckinsale, Christopher Walken, and Rosario Dawson.

The story revolves around Michael Newman (played by Adam Sandler), a workaholic advertising executive who feels unfulfilled with his life. He is married to Donna (played by Kate Beckinsale) and has two children, Charlie (played by Logan Lerman) and Sarah (played by Cole Hawkins). Michael's job requires him to constantly be on the go, and he often neglects his family in the process.

One day, while working late at the office, Michael meets a mysterious door-to-door salesman named Morty (played by Christopher Walken), who sells him an "Universal Remote Control" that can control not only his TV but also his life. The remote has the power to fast-forward through time, allowing Michael to skip over mundane tasks and experiences.

Initially, Michael uses the remote to speed up his daily routine, skipping over boring meetings, traffic jams, and other tedious activities. However, he soon discovers that the remote's power comes with a price: every time he uses it, he loses a year of his life. The more he uses the remote, the younger he becomes.

As Michael struggles to cope with the consequences of his newfound power, he begins to reevaluate his priorities and relationships. He starts to appreciate the small moments in life and reconnects with his family. However, Morty's true intentions are revealed: he is a collector of souls, and Michael has become his latest acquisition.

In a desperate attempt to break free from Morty's control, Michael must find a way to reverse the effects of the remote and reclaim his life. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about the importance of family, friendship, and living in the present moment.

The movie culminates with Michael using the remote one last time to fast-forward through the final year of his life, allowing him to spend quality time with his loved ones and make amends for past mistakes. In the end, Michael is able to break free from Morty's control and find a sense of peace and fulfillment.

Overall, Click is a heartwarming story about the importance of living in the present moment and appreciating the little things in life. The movie features a talented cast, witty dialogue, and a unique blend of humor and drama that makes it a must-see for fans of Adam Sandler and fantasy comedies.

documents.title: The Core
documents.tagline: Earth has a deadline.
documents.overview: Geophysicist Dr. Josh Keyes discovers that an unknown force has caused the earth's inner core to stop rotating. With the planet's magnetic field rapidly deteriorating, our atmosphere literally starts to come apart at the seams with catastrophic consequences. To resolve the crisis, Keyes, along with a team of the world's most gifted scientists, travel into the earth's core. Their mission: detonate a device that will reactivate the core.
documents.plot:
The Core is a 2003 American science fiction disaster film directed by Jon Amiel from a screenplay by Cooper Layne and John Rogers. Aaron Eckhart, Hilary Swank, Delroy Lindo and Stanley Tucci lead an ensemble that also includes D. J. Qualls, Richard Jenkins, Tchéky Karyo, Bruce Greenwood and Alfre Woodard. Released by Paramount Pictures on March 28, 2003, after being moved from November 2002, it follows a team sent to the centre of the Earth to restart the rotation of its core with nuclear explosions.

When thirty-two people in Boston die at the same moment from failures of their pacemakers, geophysicist Josh Keyes and weapons expert Serge Leveque are brought in to investigate. A series of bizarre incidents linked to the planet's magnetic field leads Josh and the arrogant Dr. Conrad Zimsky to conclude that the inner core has stopped spinning, which will strip away the magnetic shield protecting Earth from lethal solar radiation. The government's solution is to detonate nuclear weapons in the outer core. Zimsky's estranged former colleague Ed "Braz" Brazzelton supplies a tunnelling ship, Virgil, to be piloted by NASA astronauts Robert Iverson and Rebecca Childs, while the hacker "Rat" Finch is recruited to keep news of the crisis off the internet.

Launched through the Mariana Trench, Virgil bores into the crust with a laser drill. In the mantle it plunges into a vast hollow geode, and Iverson is killed freeing the ship; a later breach in a field of diamond formations claims Serge, who sacrifices himself to save the weapon controls. In the outer core the team discovers that the material is less dense than expected and their bombs are too weak. Zimsky confesses that the crisis was likely caused by DESTINI, a secret tectonic weapon he helped develop, and the military wants to fire it again; Rat sabotages the attempt after a surge of microwave radiation destroys the Golden Gate Bridge.

The crew instead seals the bombs into separate compartments, timing the explosions so their shock waves reinforce one another. Braz and then Zimsky give their lives to complete the plan, and the detonations restart the core. Josh and Rebecca power Virgil back to the ocean floor near Hawaii, where whales attracted by their ultrasound signal lead rescuers to them, and Rat leaks the full story to the world.

The film drew mixed reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 39% approval, and grossed about $74.1 million worldwide against an $85 million budget.
production_companies: Munich Film Partners New Century & Company (MFP) Core Productions

documents.title: The Mask of Zorro
documents.tagline: No one has seen his face... but everyone ... knows this mark.
documents.overview: It has been twenty years since Don Diego de la Vega fought Spanish oppression in Alta California as the legendary romantic hero, Zorro. Having escaped from prison he transforms troubled bandit Alejandro into his successor, in order to foil the plans of the tyrannical Don Rafael Montero who robbed him of his freedom, his wife and his precious daughter.
documents.plot:
The Mask of Zorro is a 1998 American swashbuckler film directed by Martin Campbell and produced by Amblin Entertainment. The movie is set in 1820s California, during the Mexican-American War.

The story begins with the introduction of Captain Alejandro Murrieta (Antonio Banderas), a Spanish nobleman who has been wrongly accused of being a bandit and sentenced to death. However, before he can be executed, he escapes from prison and flees to the mountains, where he assumes the identity of Zorro, a legendary masked vigilante.

Meanwhile, in the town of San Juan Bautista, Don Diego de la Vega (Antonio Banderas), the son of the wealthy and influential Don Diego, is struggling to find his place in society. He is expected to take over his father's business, but he feels suffocated by the responsibilities and longs for adventure.

One day, a group of bandits led by Captain Murrieta arrive in San Juan Bautista, seeking revenge against the town that wronged him. Don Diego, who has been watching from afar, decides to take matters into his own hands and assumes the identity of Zorro to protect his father's business and the people he cares about.

As Zorro, Don Diego sets out to avenge Captain Murrieta's family and defeat the bandits. Along the way, he meets a beautiful and feisty woman named Elena Monasterio (Catherine Zeta-Jones), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

Throughout the movie, Don Diego struggles with the dual identity of Zorro and his own sense of self-worth. He must balance his desire for adventure and justice with his responsibilities as a member of society. Meanwhile, Captain Murrieta's true intentions are revealed, and Don Diego must confront him in order to save Elena and the town.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Zorro and Captain Murrieta, with Don Diego ultimately emerging victorious. In the process, he also finds his own identity and purpose as a hero, rather than just a masked vigilante.

The Mask of Zorro features stunning action sequences, memorable characters, and a sweeping narrative that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption. The movie's blend of humor, adventure, and romance has made it a beloved classic among fans of the swashbuckler genre.

documents.title: EuroTrip
documents.tagline: No actual Europeans were harmed in the making of this film.
documents.overview: When Scott learns that his longtime cyber-buddy from Berlin is a gorgeous young woman, he and his friends embark on a trip across Europe.
documents.plot:
EuroTrip is a coming-of-age comedy film released in 2004 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of three friends, Scott, Shane, and Burt, who embark on a journey to Europe after graduation.

The film begins with Scott (played by Matt Damon), Shane (played by Sean Astin), and Burt (played by Ben Stiller) reminiscing about their high school days in New Jersey. They share stories of their past relationships and the girls they had crushes on, including Mandy (played by Eliza Dushku). The friends decide to take a trip to Europe to find Mandy, who has moved to London.

Upon arrival in London, the trio meets up with Mandy's new boyfriend, Neil (played by Bill Paxton), and her eccentric family. However, things quickly go awry as they discover that Mandy is not interested in reuniting with them. The friends decide to continue their journey to Amsterdam, where they hope to find a more receptive audience.

In Amsterdam, the group encounters a series of misadventures, including a wild party at a nightclub and a run-in with a group of eccentric locals. Along the way, Scott develops feelings for Mandy's sister, Jules (played by Lauren Ambrose), while Shane becomes infatuated with a Dutch woman named Sophie.

As the trip progresses, the friends face various challenges, including cultural differences, language barriers, and personal growth. Through their experiences, they learn to let go of their past relationships and focus on the present moment.

The film's climax features the group's final encounter with Mandy, who has grown apart from her family and is struggling to find her place in the world. The friends offer her advice and support, helping her to come to terms with her own identity.

In the end, Scott returns home alone, having found a sense of closure and new beginnings. Shane and Burt part ways, but not before sharing a heartfelt goodbye. The film concludes with Scott reflecting on his journey, realizing that sometimes, you have to take risks and step out of your comfort zone to find yourself.

Overall, EuroTrip is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, love, and self-discovery. With its witty dialogue, memorable characters, and humorous misadventures, the movie has become a cult classic among fans of coming-of-age comedies.

documents.title: Nacho Libre
documents.tagline: He's not lean. He's not mean. He's nacho average hero.
documents.overview: Nacho Libre is loosely based on the story of Fray Tormenta ("Friar Storm"), aka Rev. Sergio Gutierrez Benitez, a real-life Mexican Catholic priest who had a 23-year career as a masked luchador. He competed in order to support the orphanage he directed.
documents.plot:
Nacho Libre is a 2006 American sports comedy film directed by Jared Hess and written by Jared and Jerusha Hess. The movie stars Jack Black, Ana de la Reguera, Héctor Jiménez, and Carlos Santana.

The story begins with Nacho Varga (Jack Black), a cook at a Mexican monastery in Mexico City who secretly dreams of becoming a luchador (Mexican wrestler). Nacho's life is mundane and unfulfilling, working long hours in the kitchen while his fellow monks enjoy their lives as wrestlers. However, when the monastery's beloved priest, Padre Sancho (Héctor Jiménez), announces that he will be retiring due to a heart condition, Nacho sees an opportunity to fulfill his lifelong dream.

Nacho begins training with the monastery's wrestling coach, Esqueleto (Jorge Rivero), and eventually earns the nickname "El Loco" (The Crazy One). He also meets Sister Encarnación (Ana de la Reguera), a beautiful and kind-hearted nun who becomes Nacho's love interest. As Nacho's wrestling career takes off, he must balance his newfound fame with his responsibilities at the monastery.

However, things take a turn when Esqueleto is murdered by a rival wrestler, Ramón "El Diablo" Cortez (Carlos Santana), who seeks to destroy Nacho and claim the monastery's wrestling title for himself. Nacho must use his wits and wrestling skills to outsmart Cortez and save the monastery.

Throughout the movie, Jack Black shines as Nacho Libre, bringing his signature energy and humor to the role. The film is full of hilarious moments, from Nacho's over-the-top wrestling matches to his awkward interactions with Sister Encarnación.

As the story unfolds, Nacho must confront his own identity and purpose. He learns that being a luchador is not just about physical strength but also about using his platform for good. In the end, Nacho defeats Cortez in an epic wrestling match, saving the monastery and finding his true calling as a wrestler.

The movie ends with Nacho returning to the monastery, where he is welcomed back as a hero. He marries Sister Encarnación, and they have a beautiful wedding ceremony. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, showcasing Nacho's growth and newfound sense of purpose.

Overall, Nacho Libre is a fun and entertaining movie that combines humor, action, and heart. Jack Black's performance as the titular character is unforgettable, making this film a must-see for fans of comedy and wrestling.

documents.title: Final Destination 2
documents.tagline: For every beginning there is an end.
documents.overview: When Kimberly has a violent premonition of a highway pileup she blocks the freeway, keeping a few others meant to die, safe...Or are they? The survivors mysteriously start dying and it's up to Kimberly to stop it before she's next.
documents.plot:
Final Destination 2 is a supernatural horror film directed by David R. Ellis and written by J. Mackye Gruber. The movie is the sequel to the 2000 film Final Destination, which was also based on the novel of the same name by Kevin Williamson.

The story begins with Alex Browning (A.J. Cook), the survivor of the first film, who has been experiencing strange and terrifying premonitions since her encounter with Death in the first movie. She is haunted by visions of a car crash that will kill her and several others. Believing that she can cheat death again, Alex decides to test her theory by deliberately putting herself in harm's way.

Alex convinces her friends, including Terri (Ali Larter), Wren (Seann William Scott), and Monty (Chad Donella), to go skydiving with her at a remote airfield. As they jump out of the plane, Alex experiences another premonition, which she believes is warning her that something terrible will happen.

However, instead of dying in the crash, Alex manages to survive by using a parachute that was not attached to the plane. She then sets out to warn her friends about the impending disaster, but they are skeptical and dismissive of her warnings.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alex's premonitions are real, and she is trying to prevent a series of gruesome and deadly accidents from occurring. The group soon discovers that the airfield where they went skydiving was actually a site of a previous plane crash that killed everyone on board.

The movie takes a dark turn as the characters begin to die off one by one, each in a manner that is eerily similar to Alex's premonitions. As the body count rises, it becomes clear that Death has set its sights on this group, and they are powerless to stop it.

In the end, only Terri survives, but not without scars both physical and emotional. The movie ends with Terri, who has finally understood the true nature of Alex's premonitions, setting out to warn others about the impending disaster, leaving the audience wondering if she will be able to prevent another tragedy from occurring.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as the characters are stalked by Death, and the audience is left on the edge of their seats, wondering who will survive and who will become the next victim. The movie's climax features a shocking twist that sets up the events of the third installment in the series.

Overall, Final Destination 2 is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores the theme of fate and mortality. With its clever plot twists and gruesome death scenes, it has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: Wuthering Heights
documents.tagline: Love is a force of nature
documents.overview: Yorkshire moorlands, northern England, in the late 18th century. Young Heathcliff, rescued from the streets of Liverpool by Mr. Earnshaw, the owner of Wuthering Heights, an isolated farm, develops over the years an insane passion for Cathy, his foster sister, a sick obsession destined to end tragically.
documents.plot: A poor boy of unknown origins, Heathcliff, is rescued from poverty and taken in by the Earnshaw family where he develops an intense relationship with his young foster sister, Cathy. Theirs is a passionate tale of elemental love that creates a storm of vengeance.

documents.title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre
documents.tagline: Based on a true story...
documents.overview: After picking up a traumatized young hitchhiker, five friends find themselves stalked and hunted by a chainsaw-wielding killer and his family of equally psychopathic killers.
documents.plot:
The Texas Chainsaw Massacre is a 2003 American horror film directed by Marcus Nispel and written by Scott Kosar, based on the 1974 film of the same name by Tobe Hooper. The movie stars Jessica Biel, Jonathan Tucker, Andrew Bryniarski, Eric Balfour, and Erin Daniels.

The story begins with a prologue that shows a young Sally Hardesty (Erin Daniels) being brutally murdered by Leatherface (Andrew Bryniarski), the main antagonist of the film. The scene is presented in a found-footage style, which sets the tone for the rest of the movie.

The present-day narrative follows Erin Harris (Jessica Biel), a college student who has just graduated and is on her way to visit her sister, Sarah (Mike Vogel), in Austin, Texas. Erin's friends, Kirk (Jonathan Tucker) and Pam (Erin Daniels), are also along for the ride. The group decides to take a detour to visit the grave of Sally Hardesty, who was killed by Leatherface many years ago.

As they approach the grave, they notice that it has been recently disturbed, which sets off a chain of events that leads them into the clutches of Leatherface and his family. The group soon discovers that they are lost in rural Texas and that their car has broken down. They decide to seek shelter at an old gas station, where they meet a local named Franklin (Eric Balfour), who claims to be able to fix their car.

However, it becomes clear that Franklin is not what he seems, and the group soon finds themselves being stalked by Leatherface and his family, including his mother, Grandpa, and brother. The group tries to escape, but they are eventually captured and taken to the family's farmhouse, where they are subjected to a series of gruesome and terrifying events.

As the night wears on, Erin and her friends try to find a way to escape, but Leatherface and his family prove to be relentless in their pursuit of them. The group is eventually killed off one by one, with Erin being the last survivor.

In the end, Erin manages to escape from the farmhouse by hiding in a well, where she is rescued by a local sheriff's deputy. As she reflects on her ordeal, it becomes clear that the events at the farmhouse were just a nightmare, and that Erin had been experiencing hallucinations due to stress and fatigue.

The movie ends with Erin driving away from the farmhouse, leaving behind the horrors of the night before. The final shot is of Leatherface's mask, which is left on the ground, serving as a reminder of the terror that Erin experienced.

Overall, The Texas Chainsaw Massacre (2003) is a tense and suspenseful horror film that pays homage to the original 1974 film while also offering a fresh take on the classic story.

documents.title: Babylon A.D.
documents.tagline: Kill or be Killed.
documents.overview: A veteran-turned-mercenary is hired to take a young woman with a secret from post-apocalyptic Eastern Europe to New York City.
documents.plot:
In a dystopian near future, a Russian mobster, Gorsky, hires the mercenary Toorop to bring a young woman known only as Aurora from Asia to New York City. Gorsky gives Toorop a variety of weapons and a subdermally implanted UN passport. Toorop, the girl, and, her guardian, Sister Rebeka, travel from the Noelite Convent in Kyrgyzstan to reach New York via Russia.
Unlike in the technologically advanced United States, war and terrorist activity have transformed Russia's cities into dangerous, overpopulated slums. The stress of humanity's situation causes Aurora to act out in strange ways and display clairvoyant abilities. On one such occasion, Aurora, seemingly for no reason, panics and runs from a crowded train station just before it explodes in a terrorist attack.
The protagonists must also evade an unknown group of mercenaries claiming to have been sent by Aurora's supposedly dead father. Later, they board a submarine that carries refugees to Canada. To avoid satellite detection, the Captain of the submarine orders his crew to dive and he shoots some of the refugees still trying to get on board. Aurora, infuriated by the loss of life, operates the 30-year-old submarine without training. Sister Rebeka tells Toorop that Aurora could speak nineteen different languages by the age of two, and always seems to know things she has never learned. Three months before leaving with Toorop, she began acting differently. This occurred after a Noelite doctor administered a pill. The doctor told her to go to New York City and arranged for Toorop to escort them.
After arriving in Alaska with help from Toorop's associate, Finn, the protagonists are attacked by weaponized drones. Toorop manages to destroy all the drones, but also gets wounded. The perils cause Finn to betray the group and so Toorop shoots him dead.
Once in Harlem, a news broadcast about the bombing of the Kyrgyzstan convent causes the group to realize there is more going on than they know. Gorsky, working for the Noelites, had planted a tracking device in Toorop's passport and bombed the convent when he knew they were in the United States. The doctor who earlier saw Aurora examines her again in a hotel room. When he leaves, Aurora reveals (without being told) that she is pregnant with twins despite being a virgin.
Looking outside the hotel, Toorop sees Gorsky's men and the Noelite group heavily armed and waiting for them on the street. The High Priestess calls Toorop and asks him to bring Aurora outside. Just before they take her away, Toorop changes his mind and starts a firefight with the two groups to get the two women to safety. Gorsky's men fire guided missiles at Toorop that track his subdermal passport. Rebeka gets killed defending Aurora, who in turn shoots Toorop and says, "I need you to live". Toorop's clinical death causes the guided missile to go off target (missing Toorop) and explode near Aurora instead; she inexplicably survives.

documents.title: Starsky & Hutch
documents.tagline: They're the man.
documents.overview: Join uptight David Starsky and laid-back Ken "Hutch" Hutchinson as they're paired for the first time as undercover cops. The new partners must overcome their differences to solve an important case with help from street informant Huggy Bear and persuasive criminal Reese Feldman.
documents.plot: Join uptight David Starsky and laid-back Ken "Hutch" Hutchinson as they're paired for the first time as undercover cops. The new partners must overcome their differences to solve an important case with help from street informant Huggy Bear and persuasive criminal Reese Feldman.

documents.title: Thank You for Smoking
documents.tagline: Tobacco lobbyist Nick Naylor is trying to SAVE YOUR ASH!
documents.overview: Nick Naylor is a charismatic spin-doctor for Big Tobacco who'll fight to protect America's right to smoke -- even if it kills him -- while still remaining a role model for his 12-year old son. When he incurs the wrath of a senator bent on snuffing out cigarettes, Nick's powers of "filtering the truth" will be put to the test.
documents.plot: Nick Naylor is a charismatic spin-doctor for Big Tobacco who'll fight to protect America's right to smoke -- even if it kills him -- while still remaining a role model for his 12-year old son. When he incurs the wrath of a senator bent on snuffing out cigarettes, Nick's powers of "filtering the truth" will be put to the test.

documents.title: Renaissance
documents.tagline: Paris 2054. Live forever or die trying
documents.overview: To find Ilona and unlock the secrets of her disappearance, Karas must plunge deep into the parallel worlds of corporate espionage, organized crime and genetic research - where the truth imprisons whoever finds it first and miracles can be bought but at a great price.
documents.plot:
Renaissance, also released as Paris 2054: Renaissance, is a 2006 animated tech-noir thriller directed by Christian Volckman and co-produced by France, the United Kingdom and Luxembourg. Rendered in stark black and white using motion capture, it was released in France in March 2006, in Britain in July and in the United States in September by Miramax. The English-language version features the voices of Daniel Craig as Barthélémy Karas, Romola Garai as Ilona Tasuiev, Catherine McCormack as her sister Bislane, Ian Holm as Jonas Muller and Jonathan Pryce as Paul Dellenbach.

In Paris in 2054, Ilona, a 22-year-old researcher at the all-powerful corporation Avalon, is abducted. The case goes to police captain Karas, fresh from ending a hostage crisis by gunning down the kidnappers. He questions Muller, Avalon's former chief scientist, who quit after failing to cure progeria, the ageing disease that killed his brother, and now runs a free clinic; Muller hints that nobody truly leaves Avalon. Dellenbach, one of the company's executives, stonewalls him. A car chase ending at the Eiffel Tower leads Karas to his childhood friend Farfella, now a gangster, who hands over security footage showing Ilona's car being taken by a very old man. Ilona's sister Bislane, also an Avalon employee, breaks into the company archives and finds that Muller and a Dr. Nakata had experimented on children in search of a progeria cure, destroying their records when the subjects began to mutate. To shield her from Avalon, Karas puts her under a false arrest.

Muller finally confesses that he took Ilona because her research had uncovered the secret of eternal life, which he had found himself decades earlier, and he feared what Avalon would do with it. Before he can surrender, a police marksman shoots him by mistake. Karas realises the old man is Muller's brother, immortal but trapped in an aged body. Karas, mortally wounded, rescues Ilona from Avalon's security forces in the sewers, but she refuses to flee and resolves to hand her discovery to Avalon, so he shoots her as she walks away. Dying, he imagines Bislane forgiving him, as Dellenbach watches it all on a live video feed.

Made over six years for about €14 million, the film won the Cristal for best feature at the Annecy animation festival. It grossed only $1.8 million worldwide and drew mixed reviews, with 49% on Rotten Tomatoes and 57 on Metacritic.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union

documents.title: The Descent
documents.tagline: Scream your last breath.
documents.overview: After a tragic accident, six friends reunite for a caving expedition. Their adventure soon goes horribly wrong when a collapse traps them deep underground and they find themselves pursued by bloodthirsty creatures. As their friendships deteriorate, they find themselves in a desperate struggle to survive the creatures and each other.
documents.plot:
The Descent is a 2005 British horror film directed by Neil Marshall and produced by Celador Films. The movie follows a group of six women who embark on a caving expedition in the Appalachian Mountains, only to find themselves trapped and hunted by subterranean creatures.

The story begins with Sarah (Shauna Macdonald), a former rock climber who has lost her sense of purpose after a tragic accident that killed her friends. She joins an all-female caving expedition led by Juno (Natalie Mendoza) to the Appalachian Mountains, where they plan to explore an abandoned cave system.

The group consists of Sarah's friend Rebecca (Saskia Mulder), Juno, Beth (Alex Reid), Chris (Nikki Graham), and Holly (Jenny McAlpine). As they venture deeper into the caves, they discover a hidden underground chamber filled with ancient fossils and strange rock formations. However, their excitement is short-lived, as they soon realize that they are not alone in the cave.

The group begins to experience strange occurrences, including hearing eerie sounds and finding signs of recent habitation. They soon discover that the creatures are humanoid in appearance, but have been mutated by some unknown force to live in the dark depths of the cave system.

As the group tries to find a way out of the caves, they realize that one of their own members has been infected with the creatures' venom, which is slowly turning her into one of them. The group's dynamics begin to deteriorate as tensions rise and paranoia sets in.

The creatures, known as "crawlers," are fast-moving and deadly, using their sharp claws and teeth to attack their prey. The group soon realizes that they must work together to survive, but their efforts are hindered by the claustrophobic environment of the cave system.

As the body count rises, Sarah becomes increasingly determined to find a way out of the caves and rescue her friends. She leads the group on a perilous journey through the tunnels, facing numerous challenges and terrifying encounters with the creatures.

In the end, only two members of the group manage to escape the caves: Sarah and Juno. They emerge from the cave system, battered and traumatized, but alive. The movie ends with Sarah reflecting on her experience, realizing that she has found a new sense of purpose in life and a deeper appreciation for the beauty and danger of the natural world.

Overall, The Descent is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of female empowerment, friendship, and survival in the face of overwhelming odds.

documents.title: Evolution
documents.tagline: Coming to wipe that silly smile off your planet.
documents.overview: A comedy that follows the chaos that ensues when a meteor hits the Earth carrying alien life forms that give new meaning to the term "survival of the fittest." David Duchovny, Orlando Jones, Seann William Scott, and Julianne Moore are the only people standing between the aliens and world domination... which could be bad news for the Earth.
documents.plot:
Evolution is a 2001 American science fiction comedy film directed by Ivan Reitman and written by Peter Farrelly and Bobby Farrelly. The movie stars David Duchovny, Orlando Jones, and Julianne Moore.

The story begins with Dr. Ira Levinson (David Duchovny), a paleontologist who has spent his entire career studying dinosaurs. He is obsessed with the idea of finding a way to bring back these prehistoric creatures to life. After years of research, he finally succeeds in creating a serum that can reanimate dead tissue.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Ira's lab is attacked by a group of thieves who steal his serum and use it to create an army of dinosaurs in modern-day New York City. The dinosaurs, including a Tyrannosaurus Rex, Velociraptors, and Triceratops, wreak havoc on the city, causing destruction and chaos.

Enter Ray Finkle (Orlando Jones), a former minor league baseball player who is now working as a security guard at a museum. He teams up with Ira's daughter, Dr. Maggie Levinson (Julianne Moore), to stop the dinosaurs and find a way to reverse the effects of the serum.

As the story unfolds, Ray and Maggie must navigate through the city, avoiding the dinosaurs and trying to find a way to shut down the serum's effects. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including a group of bumbling scientists who are trying to exploit the situation for their own gain.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, courtesy of Ray's witty one-liners and his fish-out-of-water experiences in the scientific world. The special effects are also impressive, bringing the dinosaurs to life in a way that is both convincing and entertaining.

As the plot reaches its climax, Ray and Maggie finally discover the location of the serum's source: a secret laboratory hidden beneath the city streets. They must use all their wits and cunning to outsmart the villains and shut down the serum, saving the city from destruction.

In the end, Ray and Maggie succeed in stopping the dinosaurs and reversing the effects of the serum. The movie ends with a comedic twist, as Ray is hailed as a hero for his role in saving the city, despite having no scientific expertise whatsoever.

Overall, Evolution is a fun and entertaining movie that combines humor, action, and adventure. While it may not be a masterpiece of science fiction cinema, it is a lighthearted and enjoyable ride that is sure to delight fans of dinosaurs and comedy.

documents.title: Zoolander
documents.tagline: 3% Body Fat. 1% Brain Activity.
documents.overview: Clear the runway for Derek Zoolander, VH1's three-time male model of the year. His face falls when hippie-chic Hansel scooters in to steal this year's award. The evil fashion guru Mugatu seizes the opportunity to turn Derek into a killing machine. It's a well-designed conspiracy and only with the help of Hansel and a few well-chosen accessories like Matilda can Derek make the world safe for male models everywhere.
documents.plot:
Zoolander is a 2001 American comedy film directed, co-produced and co-written by Ben Stiller, who also stars in the title role. A satire of the fashion industry, it follows the vain and dim-witted male model Derek Zoolander, who is manipulated by the fashion mogul Jacobim Mugatu into attempting to assassinate the Prime Minister of Malaysia. Owen Wilson, Christine Taylor, Will Ferrell, Milla Jovovich, Jerry Stiller and Jon Voight co-star, and the film features dozens of celebrity cameos. The character originated in short films written by Drake Sather and Stiller for the VH1 Fashion Awards in 1996 and 1997.

Derek, a three-time male model of the year, is at a low point after the rising star Hansel McDonald beats him for the award, and his roommates and fellow models are killed in a freak gasoline-fight accident. Retiring from modeling, he tries to reconnect with his working-class family in the coal-mining region of southern New Jersey, but his father rejects him. Meanwhile, Mugatu and Derek's agent Maury Ballstein are secretly charged by the fashion industry with finding a model who can be brainwashed to kill the new Malaysian prime minister, whose plans to abolish child labor threaten the industry's supply of cheap workers.

Mugatu offers Derek a comeback as the face of his new fashion line, "Derelicte," and has him conditioned at a day spa to attack on cue when he hears the song "Relax" by Frankie Goes to Hollywood. Time journalist Matilda Jeffries, who wrote a scathing article about Derek, becomes suspicious and investigates, learning that models have been used as assassins for generations. Derek and Matilda seek help from Hansel, and the two rivals settle their feud in a walk-off judged by David Bowie, before racing to stop the assassination at Mugatu's fashion show and expose the conspiracy.

Released two weeks after the September 11 attacks, the film had digital edits removing the World Trade Center from shots of New York, and it was banned in Malaysia and Singapore. It received mixed reviews but grossed about $60 million worldwide, became a major cult favorite and spawned many widely quoted lines, including Derek's signature "Blue Steel" pose. A sequel, Zoolander 2, was released in 2016.
production_companies: MFP Munich Film Partners GmbH & Company I. Produktions KG

documents.title: Surf's Up
documents.tagline: A Major Ocean Picture
documents.overview: Surf's Up is an animated feature that goes behind the scenes of the high-octane world of competitive penguin surfing. The film profiles Cody Maverick, an up-and-coming surfer as he enters his first pro competition.
documents.plot: With a documentary crew in tow, Cody Maverick—a young surfer from Antarctica—travels to the pacific for his first professional competition. Determined to earn respect and live up to his idol, Big Z, Cody pushes himself to the limit. But all that changes when an encounter with a laid-back local forces him to rethink his values.

documents.title: The Dinner Game
documents.tagline: A feast for the senseless.
documents.overview: For Pierre Brochant and his friends, Wednesday is “Idiots' Day”. The idea is simple: each person has to bring along an idiot. The one who brings the most spectacular idiot wins the prize. Tonight, Brochant is ecstatic. He has found a gem. The ultimate idiot, “A world champion idiot!”. What Brochant doesn’t know is that Pignon is a real jinx, a past master in the art of bringing on catastrophes...
documents.plot:
The Dinner Game (Le Dîner de cons, literally "The Dinner of Idiots") is a French comedy of 1998 written and directed by Francis Veber, adapted from his own stage play. Thierry Lhermitte plays the Parisian publisher Pierre Brochant and Jacques Villeret plays François Pignon, the hapless guest he plans to mock, with Francis Huster, Daniel Prévost, Alexandra Vandernoot and Catherine Frot.

Every week Brochant and his fashionable, successful friends hold an "idiots' dinner", to which each must bring an unsuspecting fool, ideally someone obsessed with an absurd hobby, to be quietly ridiculed all evening. Brochant finds a prize candidate: Pignon, a cheerful employee of the Finance Ministry, an institution Brochant, a tax cheat, detests, who builds famous landmarks out of matchsticks. But after inviting Pignon to his apartment, Brochant throws out his back on the golf course, and his wife Christine, disgusted by his cruelty, walks out just before Pignon arrives.

Immobilized, Brochant has to rely on his guest, who bungles everything he touches. Asked to help track down Christine by phone, Pignon reveals Brochant's mistress Marlène, whom he takes for Brochant's sister, and invites her over. Mistaking the briefly returning Christine for the mistress, he advises her on how to win Brochant back, so that she learns of the affair and leaves again. Fearing Christine has returned to her former lover Juste Leblanc, Brochant's old best friend, Brochant coaches Pignon to call him posing as a film producer, but Pignon gives out Brochant's number. Leblanc, unexpectedly sympathetic, comes over to help. To find a womanizer Christine might have fled to, Pignon invites the tax inspector Lucien Cheval, forcing Brochant to hide his valuables; by coincidence Cheval's own wife turns out to be with the same man.

Gradually forced to face his faults, Brochant comes close to reconciling with Christine when Pignon calls her of his own accord, eloquently describing how Brochant has spent the day putting his life in order, and insists he is calling alone. Brochant apologizes for his arrogance. But when Christine calls back, Pignon absent-mindedly picks up the phone, and she hangs up convinced Brochant set him up, leaving Brochant once again calling Pignon an idiot.

The year's top French film at the domestic box office, second only to Titanic, it won three César Awards, including Best Actor for Villeret, and is widely regarded as a cult classic.

documents.title: The Royal Tenenbaums
documents.tagline: Family Isn't A Word ... It's A Sentence.
documents.overview: Royal Tenenbaum and his wife Etheline had three children and then they separated. All three children are extraordinary --- all geniuses. Virtually all memory of the brilliance of the young Tenenbaums was subsequently erased by two decades of betrayal, failure, and disaster. Most of this was generally considered to be their father's fault. "The Royal Tenenbaums" is the story of the family's sudden, unexpected reunion one recent winter.
documents.plot:
The Royal Tenenbaums is a 2001 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Wes Anderson. The movie follows the lives of the dysfunctional Tenenbaum family, who were once considered one of the most talented families in the world.

The story begins with Chas Tenenbaum (Gene Hackman), a successful businessman, who has just been released from prison after serving time for embezzlement. He is reunited with his three adult children: Richie (Ben Stiller), Margot (Gwyneth Paltrow), and Etheline (Anjelica Huston). The family's reunion is complicated by the fact that they have all drifted apart over the years, each pursuing their own unique paths in life.

Richie, a former child prodigy who was once considered one of the greatest tennis players in the world, has become a struggling writer. He is still haunted by his past and struggles to find meaning in his life. Margot, on the other hand, is a successful businesswoman who has built a reputation as a ruthless and cunning executive. Etheline, the family matriarch, is a complex and enigmatic figure who has been hiding secrets of her own.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each member of the Tenenbaum family is struggling with their own personal demons. Richie's struggles with his past are exacerbated by his relationship with his mother, Etheline, who is still reeling from the loss of her husband and the failure of her marriage to Chas. Margot's success is built on a foundation of deceit and manipulation, while Etheline's secrets threaten to destroy the family's fragile relationships.

Throughout the film, Wes Anderson's signature visual style and attention to detail are on full display. The movie features a colorful and eccentric cast of characters, including Margot's love interest, Raleigh St. Clair (Luke Wilson), and Richie's rival, Henry Sherman (Owen Wilson).

As the story reaches its climax, the Tenenbaum family is forced to confront their past mistakes and weaknesses. In a dramatic and emotional confrontation, the family comes together to support each other and find a way forward. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the Tenenbaums finally beginning to heal and rebuild their relationships.

Overall, The Royal Tenenbaums is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of family, identity, and redemption. With its unique visual style and memorable characters, it has become a cult classic and one of Wes Anderson's most beloved films.

documents.title: The Way of the Dragon
documents.tagline: The Colosseum . . the battleground of Bruce Lee and Chuck Norris.
documents.overview: Tang Lung arrives in Rome to help his cousins in the restaurant business. They are being pressured to sell their property to the syndicate, who will stop at nothing to get what they want. When Tang arrives he poses a new threat to the syndicate, and they are unable to defeat him. The syndicate boss hires the best Japanese and European martial artists to fight Tang, but he easily finishes them off.
documents.plot:
In Rome, Chen Ching-hua and her uncle Wang experience trouble with their restaurant from a crime boss who wants their property. When Chen refuses to give it up, the boss sends gangsters there to scare away the customers. Appealing to an uncle in Hong Kong, Chen receives help in the form of a young martial artist Tang Lung. On his first arrival, Tang is disoriented by his new surroundings and appears to be a country bumpkin. Disappointed, Chen asks what help he can be, but Tang confidently assures her that he is capable enough. At the restaurant, Tang learns that the staff have begun to learn karate, much to the annoyance of Quen, an employee who favors kung fu. Tang advises Quen to be open-minded and make use of anything that works.
Before long, the gangsters appear at the restaurant and threaten the customers away while Tang is using the bathroom. Upset by Tang's poor timing, the staff question his skill and the usefulness of his style. When the gangsters later return, the staff engage the thugs in a fight, only to be beaten. However, Tang single-handedly defeats them, causing the staff to decide to train under him. Uncle Wang warns them that the gangsters will seek revenge, but Tang vows to protect the restaurant. Chen and Tang grow closer and she takes him on a tour of Rome, though Tang is unimpressed by the city.
Ho, the crime boss's subordinate, returns with armed men and takes the restaurant staff hostage. Ho gives Tang a ticket to Hong Kong and tells him to go back. However, when his men escort Tang outside, Tang fights back and defeats the thugs with his two nunchakus, followed by the help of the restaurant staff. Tang warns Ho not to return and the thugs leave the restaurant. The staff celebrate their victory, but the gang boss threatens to have Tang killed unless he leaves by Chinese New Year. Uncle Wang urges Chen to convince Tang to leave. When Tang refuses to abandon the restaurant, an assassin tries to kill him from a nearby rooftop with a sniper rifle. Already fidgety from nearby fireworks, Tang survives the attempt. He then tracks down and defeats the assassin after tricking him into wasting his ammunition. When he returns to the apartment, he finds that Chen is gone. Assuming that Ho has kidnapped her, Tang goes to the boss' headquarters with the restaurant staff, defeating his men. Tang issues a final warning to the boss to leave the restaurant alone. The staff again celebrate, but a telegram for Tang cuts this short when they learn that he has been summoned back to Hong Kong. Tang assures them that he will not leave until the situation is resolved.
Ho hires two Japanese and European karate masters to challenge Tang, as well as a world-class martial artist named Colt. He then leads some of the restaurant staff to an isolated spot under the pretence of a truce, where the two martial artists ambush them. They initially defeat the staff until Tang intervenes. Ho lures Tang away to fight Colt at the Colosseum.

documents.title: Kung Fu Hustle
documents.tagline: So many gangsters… so little time.
documents.overview: It's the 1940s, and the notorious Axe Gang terrorizes Shanghai. Small-time criminals Sing and Bone hope to join, but they only manage to make lots of very dangerous enemies. Fortunately for them, kung fu masters and hidden strength can be found in unlikely places. Now they just have to take on the entire Axe Gang.
documents.plot:
Kung Fu Hustle is a 2004 martial arts comedy film directed by Stephen Chow, produced by China Film Co-Production Corporation, and written by Stephen Chow. The film stars Stephen Chow, Zhang Manzi, and Yuen Biao.

The story takes place in the 1940s in the fictional city of Gong Tong, which is modeled after 1930s Shanghai. The film begins with a prologue that sets the tone for the rest of the movie: a flashback to the life of Sing (played by Stephen Chow), a young boy who dreams of becoming a kung fu master.

Sing's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Master Pain (played by Yuen Biao), a renowned kung fu expert, and his sidekick, Thunderleg (played by Zhang Manzi). The two men are on the run from the notorious Triad leader, Boss Wolf (played by Danny Lee).

The story then shifts to the present day, where Sing is now an adult and working as a taxi driver. He lives in a small apartment with his mother, who runs a noodle shop. One day, a group of thugs, led by Boss Wolf, arrive at the noodle shop, seeking revenge against Sing's family.

To protect his mother, Sing teams up with Master Pain and Thunderleg to form an unlikely alliance. Together, they concoct a plan to defeat Boss Wolf and his gang. The trio uses their unique kung fu skills to outsmart and outmaneuver their opponents.

As the story unfolds, Sing becomes more confident in his abilities and begins to develop his own fighting style. He also starts to fall for a local woman named Princess Jasmine (played by Charlene Choi), who is being pursued by Boss Wolf's henchmen.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Sing, Master Pain, Thunderleg, and Boss Wolf's gang. The fight takes place in the streets of Gong Tong, with the trio using their kung fu skills to take down the thugs one by one.

In the end, Sing emerges victorious, having defeated Boss Wolf and saved his mother's noodle shop. He also wins Princess Jasmine's heart, and the two share a romantic moment.

Throughout the film, Stephen Chow showcases his impressive comedic timing and acting skills, as well as his mastery of kung fu. The film's blend of action, comedy, and music makes it a unique and entertaining ride.

Overall, Kung Fu Hustle is a hilarious and action-packed film that pays homage to classic Hong Kong cinema while also introducing new elements to the genre. With its colorful characters, witty dialogue, and impressive fight choreography, this film is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle
documents.tagline: This summer the Angels are back.
documents.overview: The Angels are charged with finding a pair of missing rings that are encoded with the personal information of members of the Witness Protection Program. As informants are killed, the ladies target a rogue agent who might be responsible.
documents.plot:
Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle is a 2003 action comedy film directed by McG and written by John Brancato, Michael Ferris, and Shane Black. The movie stars Cameron Diaz, Drew Barrymore, and Lucy Liu as the iconic Charlie's Angels trio.

The film begins with Dylan Sanders (Drew Barrymore) and Natalie Cook (Cameron Diaz), two of the top Angels, on a mission to stop a group of thieves who have stolen a valuable artifact. However, things take a turn when they discover that the thief is none other than their former partner, Madison Lee (Lucy Liu).

Madison has been working with a new partner, Alex Munday (Derek Zane Unger), and together they plan to steal a valuable diamond necklace. The Angels must use their skills and teamwork to stop them.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Madison's betrayal is not just about personal gain, but also about revenge against her former partners. She has been working with a wealthy businessman, Will Stacks (Derek Zane Unger), who has been using his wealth and influence to manipulate people and get what he wants.

The Angels soon discover that Will is behind the theft of the diamond necklace and that Madison's betrayal was just a ruse to get close to him. The team must now work together to stop Will and his accomplices, including a group of skilled thieves known as "The Shadow Syndicate."

Throughout the film, the Angels face various challenges and obstacles as they try to stay one step ahead of their enemies. Along the way, they also have to deal with their own personal demons and relationships.

In the end, the Angels successfully stop Will and his accomplices, but not before Madison reveals that she has been working undercover to bring down Will from the inside. The film ends with the Angels celebrating their victory and reflecting on the lessons they've learned about teamwork, loyalty, and trust.
