documents.title: Fantastic Four
documents.tagline: 4 times the action. 4 times the adventure. 4 times the fantastic.
documents.overview: During a space voyage, four scientists are altered by cosmic rays: Reed Richards gains the ability to stretch his body; Sue Storm can become invisible; Johnny Storm controls fire; and Ben Grimm is turned into a super-strong … thing. Together, these "Fantastic Four" must now thwart the evil plans of Dr. Doom and save the world from certain destruction.
documents.plot:
Fantastic Four is a 2005 superhero film based on the Marvel Comics team created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. Directed by Tim Story and written by Mark Frost and Michael France, it stars Ioan Gruffudd as Reed Richards, Jessica Alba as Susan Storm, Chris Evans as Johnny Storm, Michael Chiklis as Ben Grimm and Julian McMahon as Victor von Doom, with Kerry Washington. It tells the origin story of the team, who must learn to live with the extraordinary abilities they gain after being exposed to cosmic rays in space. It was the second live-action Fantastic Four film to be produced, after an unreleased version produced by Roger Corman.

Scientist Reed Richards and his friend Ben Grimm persuade Victor von Doom, the head of Von Doom Industries, to give them access to his space station so that Reed can study the effects of a cosmic energy cloud on living samples. Victor brings along his chief geneticist, Susan Storm, who is Reed's former girlfriend, and her reckless brother Johnny. The cloud arrives ahead of schedule, and while Reed, Susan and Johnny rush to help Ben, who is outside on a spacewalk, Victor seals himself behind the station's shields. The storm strikes them all. Back on Earth, the four develop strange powers: Reed can stretch his body like rubber, Susan can turn invisible and project force fields, Johnny can engulf himself in fire, and Ben is transformed into a massive, rock-skinned creature of tremendous strength. After they use their abilities to avert a disaster on the Brooklyn Bridge, the media dubs them the Fantastic Four. Johnny revels in the fame, but Ben is devastated when his fiancée leaves him, and Reed vows to find a cure. Working from his laboratory in the Baxter Building, Reed tries to build a machine that can reverse the changes, while Victor, ruined by the mission's failure and blaming Reed, discovers that the storm has also changed him, turning his body into living metal able to generate electricity. Calling himself Doom, he sets out to drive the team apart and take his revenge, forcing the four to decide whether they can work together as a family.

The film received generally mixed reviews; on Rotten Tomatoes, 28% of 213 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus faulting its goofy attempts at wit, subpar acting and bland storytelling, and Metacritic gave it a score of 40 out of 100. It was nonetheless a commercial success, grossing $333.5 million worldwide, and was followed by the sequel Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer.

documents.title: Demolition Man
documents.tagline: The future isn't big enough for the both of them.
documents.overview: Simon Phoenix, a violent criminal cryogenically frozen in 1996, escapes during a parole hearing in 2032 in the utopia of San Angeles. Police are incapable of dealing with his violent ways and turn to his captor, who had also been cryogenically frozen after being wrongfully accused of killing 30 innocent people while apprehending Phoenix.
documents.plot:
Demolition Man is a science fiction action film directed by Marco Brambilla, released in 1993 by Warner Bros. Pictures.

In the year 2032, the United States has become a utopia where crime and violence have been eradicated through advanced technology and social engineering. The city of San Angeles is a marvel of efficiency and order, with everything controlled and monitored by the government. John Spartan (Sylvester Stallone), a tough and experienced cop, is tasked with stopping a notorious terrorist named Simon Phoenix (Wesley Snipes).

However, just as Spartan is about to apprehend Phoenix, he is cryogenically frozen for 30 years after being mortally wounded in the line of duty. When Spartan is thawed out in 2064, he finds that the world has changed dramatically. The city is now a futuristic metropolis with flying cars and robots, but also a society where people are more complacent and less willing to take risks.

Spartan soon discovers that Phoenix has been thawed out as well and is now a free agent, wreaking havoc on San Angeles. With the help of Dr. Raymond Cocteau (Sandra Bullock), a brilliant scientist who created the cryogenic freezing technology, Spartan must navigate this new world to stop Phoenix and restore order.

As Spartan tries to adjust to his new surroundings, he clashes with the authorities, particularly the self-absorbed and arrogant Chief John Kilbourne ( Nigel Hawthorne). Meanwhile, Cocteau becomes romantically involved with Spartan, but their relationship is complicated by her feelings of guilt over creating a being who was frozen for 30 years.

Throughout the film, Spartan's old-school values and methods are at odds with the new society. He must learn to adapt to this futuristic world and work with Cocteau to stop Phoenix. Along the way, he discovers that Phoenix has a personal vendetta against him and is using his newfound freedom to exact revenge.

The climax of the film features an epic battle between Spartan and Phoenix, with the two former adversaries engaging in a high-tech showdown. In the end, Spartan emerges victorious, but not before realizing that his old ways may be too much for this new world.

Demolition Man received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, but it has since become a cult classic, praised for its witty dialogue and over-the-top action sequences. The film's themes of social commentary and satire are still relevant today, offering a commentary on the dangers of complacency and the importance of individual freedom.

Overall, Demolition Man is an entertaining and visually stunning sci-fi action film that explores the consequences of a utopian society gone wrong.

documents.title: Unbreakable
documents.tagline: Some things are only revealed by accident
documents.overview: An ordinary man makes an extraordinary discovery when a train accident leaves his fellow passengers dead — and him unscathed. The answer to this mystery could lie with the mysterious Elijah Price, a man who suffers from a disease that renders his bones as fragile as glass.
documents.plot:
Unbreakable is a 2000 American superhero thriller written, produced and directed by M. Night Shyamalan. Bruce Willis stars as a man who walks away unhurt from a catastrophic train crash and begins to suspect he has extraordinary powers, with Samuel L. Jackson as the fragile comic-book enthusiast who seeks him out, Robin Wright as his wife and Spencer Treat Clark as his son. Shyamalan structured the story to mirror the three-part arc of a traditional comic book.

In 1961 Philadelphia, Elijah Price is born with broken limbs caused by osteogenesis imperfecta, a disease that makes his bones extremely brittle. Decades later, David Dunn, a former star quarterback now working as a security guard and stuck in an unhappy marriage, is the only survivor of a derailment that kills every other passenger on his train, and he emerges without a scratch.

After a memorial service, David finds a note asking whether he has ever been ill, inviting him to Elijah's comic-art gallery. Elijah lays out his theory that if he lies at one extreme of human fragility, someone must exist at the other who is practically unbreakable. Sceptical, David nonetheless discovers he can lift far more weight than he expected, while his son Joseph becomes convinced his father is a superhero. Elijah suggests that water, which nearly drowned David as a child, is his one weakness, and David admits he faked an injury after a car crash to quit football because his wife Audrey disliked the violence.

With Elijah's encouragement, David comes to see that his instinct for spotting dangerous people is a form of extrasensory perception: by touching strangers he glimpses crimes they have committed. He follows a janitor who has invaded a family's home and holds the children captive, frees them, survives being thrown into a pool and kills the intruder. Renewed, he reconciles with Audrey and quietly shows Joseph a newspaper sketch of the unknown hero.

When David shakes Elijah's hand, he sees that Elijah engineered a series of deadly disasters, including the train crash, in his search for a hero. Embracing the nickname Mr. Glass, Elijah casts himself as the villain, and a closing title reveals that he is committed to a psychiatric institution.

Released on November 22, 2000, the film grossed about $248 million worldwide on a $75 million budget and drew generally positive reviews, holding a 70% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Survival Island
documents.tagline: Looks can kill.
documents.overview: After a yachting accident, a millionaire and his wife are shipwrecked on a desert island along with their former deckhand, Manuel.
documents.plot: After a yachting accident, a millionaire and his wife are shipwrecked on a desert island along with their former deckhand, Manuel.

documents.title: Firewall
documents.tagline: Nothing Is More Dangerous Than A Man With Everything To Lose.
documents.overview: State-of-the-art security system creator, Jack Stanfield has cemented his reputation as a man who's thought of everything. But when a criminal finds a way into Jack's personal life, everything Jack holds dear is suddenly at stake.
documents.plot:
Firewall is a 2006 American action thriller film directed by Richard Loncraine and starring Harrison Ford, Virginia Madsen, and Karl Urban.

The movie begins with Jack Stanfield (Harrison Ford), a former FBI agent who has retired to a quiet life in the suburbs. He works as an insurance investigator for a company called First National Insurance Company, where he is responsible for investigating claims related to arson and other forms of property damage.

One day, Jack's wife, Kate (Virginia Madsen), is kidnapped by a group of professional thieves who are led by Robert 'The Ghost' Devereaux (Ben Kingsley). The kidnappers demand that First National Insurance Company pay $10 million in exchange for Kate's safe return. They also threaten to kill her if their demands are not met.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jack is being forced back into action by his former colleagues at the FBI, who believe that he has valuable skills and knowledge that can help them track down The Ghost and his team. However, Jack is reluctant to get involved, as he wants to protect his family and live a peaceful life.

Despite his initial reluctance, Jack agrees to work with the FBI to track down The Ghost and rescue Kate. He uses his expertise to analyze clues and follow leads, which ultimately lead him to a warehouse where The Ghost's team is hiding.

As Jack gets closer to rescuing Kate, he realizes that The Ghost has set a trap for him. The Ghost reveals that he has been playing a cat-and-mouse game with Jack all along, using his knowledge of Jack's past and his skills as an investigator to manipulate him into doing his bidding.

In the end, Jack is able to outsmart The Ghost and rescue Kate. However, not before realizing that The Ghost was actually working for a larger organization that had been manipulating events from behind the scenes. The movie ends with Jack reflecting on the experience and realizing that he has been given a second chance to make things right.

Throughout the movie, Harrison Ford delivers a strong performance as the protagonist, bringing depth and nuance to the character of Jack Stanfield. The supporting cast, including Virginia Madsen and Karl Urban, also deliver solid performances that add to the tension and suspense of the film.

Overall, Firewall is an action-packed thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and tense action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Norbit
documents.tagline: Have You Ever Made A Really Big Mistake?
documents.overview: A mild-mannered guy who is engaged to a monstrous woman meets the woman of his dreams, and schemes to find a way to be with her.
documents.plot:
Norbit is a 2007 American romantic comedy film directed by Brian Robbins and starring Eddie Murphy. The movie follows the story of Norbit, a shy and awkward young man who falls in love with his childhood sweetheart, Rasputia.

The film begins with Norbit (Eddie Murphy) as a child, living with his mother, Mrs. Johnson (Thandie Newton), and her eccentric boyfriend, Rasputia (Shari Headley). As Norbit grows up, he becomes infatuated with Rasputia, but she treats him poorly and makes him feel like an outcast.

As an adult, Norbit works as a janitor at a nightclub owned by his mother. He is still pining for Rasputia, who has become a successful businesswoman. However, when Rasputia marries the club's owner, Mr. Wong (Rudy Youngblood), Norbit becomes jealous and feels left out.

One day, Norbit meets a beautiful woman named Kate (Meagan Good), who is working at the nightclub. Despite their instant attraction, Norbit is too shy to approach her. Meanwhile, Rasputia continues to treat Norbit poorly, making him feel like an inferior being.

As the story progresses, Norbit's life becomes more complicated when he discovers that Mr. Wong is planning to sell the nightclub and move away. Desperate to save his mother's business, Norbit comes up with a plan to win Rasputia back and prove himself as a worthy partner.

In the end, Norbit's plan succeeds, and he wins Rasputia's heart. However, in a surprising twist, it is revealed that Rasputia has been using her charms to manipulate Norbit all along. Despite this, Norbit realizes that his love for Rasputia was genuine, but he also learns to appreciate himself and find happiness on his own terms.

The movie ends with Norbit and Kate sharing a romantic kiss, while Rasputia is seen walking away alone, having finally realized her true feelings for Norbit. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Norbit has found love and acceptance in the end.

Overall, Norbit is a heartwarming story about self-discovery, love, and acceptance. Eddie Murphy's performance as the titular character brings humor and charm to the film, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Cellular
documents.tagline: If the signal dies so does she.
documents.overview: A young man receives an emergency phone call on his cell phone from an older woman. She claims to have been kidnapped – and the kidnappers have targeted her husband and child next.
documents.plot: A young man receives an emergency phone call on his cell phone from an older woman. She claims to have been kidnapped – and the kidnappers have targeted her husband and child next.

documents.title: Step Up
documents.tagline: Every second chance begins with a first step.
documents.overview: Tyler Gage receives the opportunity of a lifetime after vandalizing a performing arts school, gaining him the chance to earn a scholarship and dance with an up and coming dancer, Nora.
documents.plot:
Step Up is a 2006 American dance drama film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Michael Genet. The movie stars Channing Tatum, Jenna Dewan, and Rob Brown.

The story begins with Tyler Gage (Channing Tatum), a troubled teenager who has just moved to Baltimore from Texas after getting into a fight at his previous school. He is forced to attend a local community college, where he meets Nora Walker (Jenna Dewan), the daughter of a dance instructor, and her friends.

Tyler is initially hesitant to join the school's dance team, but after seeing Nora perform, he becomes fascinated with dance and decides to join the group. However, his lack of experience and rough demeanor make him an outcast among the other dancers.

As Tyler spends more time with the dance team, led by Eva (Izabella Mlinarz), he begins to learn the basics of hip-hop dance from Nora's father, Chet Walker (Will Kemp). He also starts to develop feelings for Nora, but their social differences and his troubled past make it difficult for them to connect.

Meanwhile, Tyler's rival, Chase Collins (Rob Brown), is a talented dancer who is also vying for the top spot on the team. The two dancers engage in a series of intense dance battles, both on and off the stage.

As the competition heats up, Tyler finds himself drawn into the world of competitive dance, where he must confront his own demons and learn to work with others towards a common goal. With Nora's support, he begins to master the art of dance and eventually earns the respect of his teammates.

The movie culminates in a high-stakes dance competition at the school's annual Spring Fling event, where Tyler and Chase face off against each other in an epic dance battle. In the end, Tyler emerges victorious, but not without learning valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and the power of dance to bring people together.

Throughout the movie, the film's soundtrack features a mix of hip-hop and pop music that perfectly captures the energy and spirit of the dance team. The choreography is also noteworthy, with many impressive dance sequences that showcase the talents of the cast.

Overall, Step Up is a fun and inspiring movie that celebrates the beauty of dance and the transformative power of art to bring people together. With its talented cast, catchy soundtrack, and high-energy dance sequences, it's no wonder that this movie became a cult classic among fans of dance and music.

documents.title: Goal!
documents.tagline: Every Dream Has A Beginning
documents.overview: Like millions of kids around the world, Santiago harbors the dream of being a professional footballer... However, living in the Barrios section of Los Angeles, he thinks it is only that--a dream. Until one day an extraordinary turn of events has him trying out for Premiership club Newcastle United.
documents.plot:
Goal!, also known as Goal! The Dream Begins, is a 2005 British sports drama film directed by Danny Cannon from a screenplay by Mike Jefferies, Adrian Butchart, Dick Clement and Ian La Frenais. The first installment of the Goal! trilogy, it stars Kuno Becker as Santiago Muñez, an amateur player who gets an unlikely chance at professional football, with Alessandro Nivola, Stephen Dillane and Anna Friel. Made with the cooperation of FIFA, it features real teams and players, and Adidas reportedly contributed $50 million toward its budget and marketing.

Santiago, an undocumented Mexican immigrant in Los Angeles, plays for a local team while working as a gardener with his father, Hernan, and as a busboy. Glen Foy, a former player and scout, spots him and arranges a trial with Newcastle United. Hernan, who doubts his son's prospects, takes Santiago's savings to buy a truck, but his grandmother, Mercedes, secretly gives him the money to go. In Newcastle, Santiago struggles in the mud and under pressure from teammate Hughie McGowan, but manager Erik Dornhelm grants him a month's trial. Fearing rejection, he hides his asthma from the club nurse, Roz Harmison. Before the decisive reserve match, Hughie destroys his inhaler, and after a poor performance Santiago is let go.

On the way to the airport, his taxi picks up Gavin Harris, a talented but undisciplined recent Newcastle signing, who learns about the asthma and tells Erik. Erik keeps Santiago on condition that he receives treatment, and Santiago moves in with Gavin. Coming on as a substitute against Fulham in his first-team debut, he wins a penalty that secures victory, as Hernan watches proudly on television, though Erik scolds him for selfish play. A night out with Gavin lands the pair in The Sun, Santiago's friend Jamie suffers a career-ending injury, and his friendship with Gavin frays. When Hernan dies of a heart attack, Santiago nearly flies home but stays after talking with Roz, with whom he begins a relationship. Picked to start the final game of the season against Liverpool, he sets up Gavin's late equalizer and then scores a free kick to win 3–2, earning Newcastle a Champions League place.

Buena Vista International released Goal! in the United Kingdom on 1 October 2005. Reviews were mixed, with 42% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 53; critics praised the football sequences but found the story full of sports film clichés.

documents.title: Gridiron Gang
documents.tagline: One goal. A second chance.
documents.overview: Teenagers at a juvenile detention center, under the leadership of their counselor, gain self-esteem by playing football together.
documents.plot:
Gridiron Gang is a sports drama film released in 2006, directed by Rick Family and starring Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, Xander Berkeley, and Kyra Sedgwick. The movie tells the story of Sean Porter (Johnson), a former NFL player who becomes a coach at a juvenile correctional facility in California.

At the beginning of the film, we see Sean Porter, a former NFL linebacker, struggling to find his place after retiring from football. He is arrested for driving under the influence and sentenced to community service at a juvenile correctional facility called Red Rock Juvenile Correctional Facility. While serving his sentence, Sean meets a group of troubled teenagers who are being held at the facility.

Sean sees an opportunity to make a positive impact on these young lives and decides to start a football team within the facility. Despite initial resistance from the facility's administrators, Sean is able to convince them to let him coach the team. He uses his experience as a former NFL player to teach the boys about teamwork, discipline, and responsibility.

As the season progresses, Sean forms strong bonds with his players, many of whom are struggling with personal issues such as poverty, abuse, and neglect. Through football, Sean is able to reach these young men and help them find their sense of purpose and belonging. The team begins to show improvement on the field, but more importantly, they start to develop a sense of unity and camaraderie.

However, not everyone is supportive of Sean's efforts. The facility's administrators are skeptical of his ability to manage the team, and some of the players' parents are opposed to their children participating in football due to concerns about safety and discipline.

Despite these challenges, Sean perseveres and continues to work with his team. He uses his experience as a former NFL player to teach them valuable life skills such as communication, teamwork, and leadership. As the season comes to an end, the Red Rock Juvenile Football Team makes it to the championship game, where they face off against their arch-rivals.

In the final game, Sean's team faces off against their toughest opponents yet, but with Sean's guidance and support, they are able to overcome their challenges and emerge victorious. The win is a testament to the power of football as a tool for redemption and personal growth.

The film ends on a hopeful note, with Sean's players having found a sense of purpose and belonging through football. Many of them have also begun to turn their lives around, with some going on to attend college and pursue careers in sports management or coaching. The movie concludes with Sean reflecting on the impact he has had on his players' lives and the lessons they have learned from him.

Overall, Gridiron Gang is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores the transformative power of football and the human spirit. With outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Dwayne Johnson, the movie is a must-see for sports fans and anyone looking for a story about redemption and personal growth.

documents.title: The Break-Up
documents.tagline: …pick a side.
documents.overview: Pushed to the breaking-up point after their latest 'why can't you do this one little thing for me?' argument, Brooke calls it quits with her boyfriend Gary. What follows is a hilarious series of remedies, war tactics, overtures and undermining tricks – all encouraged by the former couple's friends and confidantes …and the occasional total stranger! When neither ex is willing to move out of their shared apartment, the only solution is to continue living as hostile roommates until one of them reaches breaking point.

documents.title: Air Force One
documents.tagline: Five miles up, The President of the United States is waging war on terrorism. Face to face.
documents.overview: Russian terrorists conspire to hijack the aircraft with the president and his family on board. The commander in chief finds himself facing an impossible predicament: give in to the terrorists and sacrifice his family, or risk everything to uphold his principles - and the integrity of the nation.
documents.plot:
Air Force One is a 1997 American action thriller film directed by Wolfgang Petersen and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer. The movie stars Harrison Ford as President James Marshall, a former Vietnam War hero who becomes the commander-in-chief of the United States.

The story begins with President Marshall's (Harrison Ford) family - his wife, Nancy (Sally Skerritt), and their two children, Sam (Joe Pesci) and Megan (Evelyn Hartt) - on board Air Force One as it takes off from Andrews Air Force Base in Maryland. The plane is headed to a summit meeting with Russian President Kirin (Gary Oldman).

As the plane reaches cruising altitude, a group of heavily armed terrorists, led by the ruthless and cunning Vladimir (Gary Oldman), infiltrate the cockpit and take control of the aircraft. They are seeking to hold the President hostage in exchange for the release of their imprisoned comrades.

The terrorists, who claim to be members of an anti-American organization, begin to make demands, including the withdrawal of U.S. troops from Russia and the recognition of Russian interests around the world. The President, determined to protect his family and the country, refuses to comply with their demands.

As the situation escalates, Air Force One is forced to fly over hostile territory, making it difficult for the President's team to respond effectively. Meanwhile, the terrorists continue to make threats against the passengers and crew, including a threat to kill the children if their demands are not met.

President Marshall, who has experience as a fighter pilot in Vietnam, takes charge of the situation and uses his military training to outsmart the terrorists. He also works closely with Colonel Thomas "Tom" Gillen (David Suchet), the Air Force One's pilot, to try and regain control of the plane.

As the standoff continues, the President's team discovers that Vladimir is actually a former KGB agent who has been planning this operation for years. The President realizes that he must use all his skills and resources to outwit the terrorists and save his family.

In a thrilling climax, President Marshall uses his knowledge of the plane's systems to disable the terrorists' communication equipment, rendering them unable to contact their handlers. He then takes control of the cockpit and engages in a fierce battle with Vladimir, using his combat training to overpower him.

With the terrorists defeated, Air Force One is able to land safely at a nearby airfield, where the President's team is waiting to provide assistance. The movie ends with the President's family safe and sound, while the nation breathes a sigh of relief that the crisis has been averted.

Overall, Air Force One is an action-packed thriller that showcases Harrison Ford's signature blend of heroism and humor. The movie's tense plot and well-developed characters make it a compelling watch, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

documents.title: Head of State
documents.tagline: The only thing white is the house.
documents.overview: When a presidential candidate dies unexpectedly in the middle of the campaign, the Democratic party unexpectedly picks a Washington, D.C. alderman as his replacement .
documents.plot:
Mays Gilliam is the alderman for the 9th Ward in Washington, D.C. After learning he is likely to lose his job and getting dumped by his girlfriend, Kim, Gilliam is unexpectedly chosen as the Democratic Party candidate for the 2004 presidential election after his party's original presidential and vice-presidential nominees die in a plane crash and he is lauded as a hero for saving a woman from an explosion. Assuming the election was already lost to incumbent Republican vice-president Brian Lewis, the Democrats decided to pick a likable but unwinnable minority candidate to improve their chances in the 2008 presidential election.
At first, Gilliam feels he will not be able to succeed as president because he would be representing the entire African-American populace, and does not want to do anything to damage his reputation. However, Gilliam begins to rise in the polls after his brother Mitch persuades him to speak out for what he believes in. He ditches the bland, boring, and uncontroversial speeches prepared for him and begins to talk honestly about major issues such as welfare, healthcare, income inequality, and society overall. Mays even finds time to romance Lisa Clark, a gas station attendant he crosses paths with, and who has been a huge supporter of Mays.
After Lewis runs a series of attack ads including one saying Gilliam supports cancer, Gilliam begins to fight back using what he claimed was "kissing" his opponent (taken from Bugs Bunny–Elmer Fudd cartoons). A part of this strategy includes dubbing a videotape of Osama bin Laden saying he hates America but loves Brian Lewis. This strategy gains Gilliam even more points in the polls.
As election day draws closer, Gilliam eventually learns the reason why he was chosen as the party candidate, fires some disloyal campaign operatives (despite them having reconciled with him afterwards), and chooses his brother as his running mate. He later has a debate with his opponent in which he manages to win the crowd over by speaking the truth about American life. Finally, Gilliam ends up winning the presidency, and proposes to Lisa by saying he wants to make her his First Lady.

documents.title: Serendipity
documents.tagline: Sometimes True Love Can Have More Than One Face.
documents.overview: Although strangers Sara and Jonathan are both already in relationships, they realize they have genuine chemistry after a chance encounter – but part company soon after. Years later, they each yearn to reunite, despite being destined for the altar. But to give true love a chance, they have to find one another again.

documents.original_title: The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants
documents.tagline: Laugh. Cry. Share the pants.
documents.overview: Four best friends (Tibby, Lena, Carmen & Bridget) who buy a mysterious pair of pants that fits each of them, despite their differing sizes, and makes whoever wears them feel fabulous. When faced with the prospect of spending their first summer apart, the pals decide they'll swap the pants so that each girl in turn can enjoy the magic.

documents.title: The Invisible
documents.tagline: Life, death and something in between.
documents.overview: After an attack leaves him in limbo -- invisible to the living and also near death -- a teenager discovers the only person who might be able help him is his attacker.
documents.plot:
The Invisible is a 2007 American supernatural teen thriller directed by David S. Goyer, a remake of the 2002 Swedish film of the same name and based on the Swedish young-adult novel by Mats Wahl. Justin Chatwin, Margarita Levieva, Chris Marquette, Marcia Gay Harden and Callum Keith Rennie star. It is often cited as the start of the modern wave of Hollywood remakes of Swedish films, and it was the last release under Disney's Hollywood Pictures label.

Nick Powell is a high school senior who secretly plans to skip graduation and go to a writing program in London, defying his emotionally distant, controlling mother Diane. His best friend Pete confides that he is being bullied by Annie Newton, a troubled girl who runs with a gang of violent thieves and whose boyfriend Marcus is on parole. After Annie robs a jewellery store and Marcus tips off the police, she is arrested and decides that Pete informed on her. She beats him until he gives up Nick's name, believing Nick is already on a plane. In fact Nick has given away his ticket. Annie and her gang ambush him on his way home from a party, beat him savagely and, thinking him dead, dump his body in a storm drain in the woods.

The next morning Nick goes to school and finds that no one can see or hear him. As police investigate his disappearance, he realises he is not dead but trapped between life and death while his body lies unconscious, and he desperately tries to reach Pete and Annie to save himself. Under police pressure, Marcus forces Pete to help move the body and plots to kill Annie, while the guilt-stricken Pete attempts suicide. Annie, meanwhile, begins to sense Nick's presence and hear fragments of his voice. Visiting his room, she comes to see how alike they were.

Annie confronts Marcus and Pete to learn where the body has been moved. Marcus tells her but shoots her as she leaves; she shoots him in return and calls the police with Nick's location. Nick is rescued and taken to hospital, where Annie dies of her wounds just as he wakes. Later, Nick and Annie's little brother Victor send a model plane carrying a message to her over the river.

The film was not screened for critics and received generally negative reviews. It grossed about $26.8 million worldwide, $20.6 million of it in North America.

documents.title: Lords of Dogtown
documents.tagline: They came from nothing to change everything.
documents.overview: The radical true story behind three teenage surfers from Venice Beach, California, who took skateboarding to the extreme and changed the world of sports forever. Stacy Peralta, Tony Alva and Jay Adams are the Z-Boys, a bunch of nobodies until they create a new style of skateboarding that becomes a worldwide phenomenon. But when their hobby becomes a business, the success shreds their friendship.
documents.plot:
Lords of Dogtown is a 2005 biographical drama film that explores the lives of three young skateboarders who became legends in the sport: Jay Adams, Stacy Peralta, and Tony Alva. The movie delves into their struggles with fame, identity, and the darker side of their success.

At its core, Lords of Dogtown is a story about the fragility of youth and the consequences of chasing one's dreams. The film portrays the characters' tumultuous relationships, substance abuse, and the blurred lines between friendship and rivalry. As they navigate the cutthroat world of professional skateboarding, they must confront their own demons and learn to balance their passion for the sport with the harsh realities of adulthood.

The movie also touches on themes of rebellion and nonconformity, as the characters reject mainstream values and forge their own path in life. Through their experiences, the film highlights the tension between individuality and conformity, as they struggle to maintain their unique identities amidst the pressures of fame and success.

Ultimately, Lords of Dogtown is a poignant exploration of the human condition, capturing the essence of youthful rebellion, self-discovery, and the enduring power of friendship in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Accepted
documents.tagline: When every college turned them down. . . they made one up.
documents.overview: A high school slacker who's rejected by every school he applies to opts to create his own institution of higher learning, the South Harmon Institute of Technology, on a rundown piece of property near his hometown.
documents.plot: A high school slacker who's rejected by every school he applies to opts to create his own institution of higher learning, the South Harmon Institute of Technology, on a rundown piece of property near his hometown.

documents.title: The Hills Have Eyes
documents.tagline: The lucky ones die first.
documents.overview: Based on Wes Craven's 1977 suspenseful cult classic, The Hills Have Eyes is the story of a family road trip that goes terrifyingly awry when the travelers become stranded in a government atomic zone. Miles from nowhere, the Carter family soon realizes the seemingly uninhabited wasteland is actually the breeding ground of a blood-thirsty mutant family...and they are the prey.
documents.plot:
The Hills Have Eyes is a 2006 American horror film directed by Alexandre Aja, based on the 1977 film of the same name by Wes Craven. The movie stars Ted Levine, Dan Byrd, Vinessa Shaw, and Aaron Stanford.

The story begins with a family of five - Big Bob (Ted Levine), Ethel (Kathleen Quinlan), Bobby (Dan Byrd), Brenda (Vinessa Shaw), and Bobby's girlfriend, Lisa (Emmanuelle Vaugier) - who embark on a road trip from California to New Mexico. The family is excited for their vacation, but they are also dealing with personal issues, including Big Bob's infidelity and Ethel's feelings of resentment towards her husband.

As the family drives through the desert, they become lost due to a series of wrong turns. They eventually stumble upon a secluded valley, which they decide to explore. Unbeknownst to them, this valley is home to a group of mutants who have been living in the area for years.

The mutants, led by the deformed and sadistic Papa (Robert Longstreet), begin to stalk and terrorize the family. The mutants are a result of genetic mutations caused by radiation exposure, which has twisted their bodies into grotesque forms. As the family tries to survive, they realize that they are trapped in the valley with no way out.

The plot thickens as the family members start to disappear one by one, and the remaining survivors must fight for their lives against the mutants. The tension builds up as the family is forced to confront their own personal demons and work together to survive.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Papa has a twisted fascination with the family's dynamics and uses this knowledge to torment them further. The family members are subjected to physical and emotional abuse, which pushes them to their limits.

In the end, only two members of the family - Brenda and Bobby - manage to escape the valley by using a makeshift vehicle to flee. However, they are left with severe psychological trauma and a newfound appreciation for the dangers of the world around them.

The Hills Have Eyes received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $60 million worldwide. The movie's graphic violence and gore were widely criticized, but it also sparked a debate about the limits of on-screen violence in horror films.

Overall, The Hills Have Eyes is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of family dynamics, trauma, and survival. While it may not be to everyone's taste due to its graphic content, it is a well-crafted movie that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

documents.title: The Hills Have Eyes 2
documents.tagline: Help isn't coming.
documents.overview: A group of National Guard trainees find themselves battling against a vicious group of mutants on their last day of training in the desert.
documents.plot:
The Hills Have Eyes 2 is a 2007 American horror film directed by Martin Weisz and written by Chris Bowers, Seth Grahame-Smith, and Robert Ben Garant. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1977 film of the same name.

The story begins with a group of teenagers who are on a road trip from California to New Mexico. They stop at a roadside diner where they meet a mysterious woman named Ethel (played by Ted Levine), who claims that she is a member of a family that has lived in the desert for generations. She warns them about the dangers of the area, but they dismiss her warnings and continue on their journey.

As night falls, the group becomes lost in the desert due to a GPS malfunction. They stumble upon an abandoned mine shaft, where they decide to take shelter for the night. Unbeknownst to them, this is the same mine shaft where the original Hills Have Eyes family was brutally murdered by the mutants.

The next morning, the group discovers that Ethel's warnings were not just mere superstition. The mutants have been awakened and are now hunting them down one by one. As the group tries to survive and find their way back to civilization, they realize that the mutants are not just mindless beasts but also seem to be driven by a twisted sense of family loyalty.

As the body count rises, the remaining survivors must confront the harsh reality of their situation. They soon discover that Ethel's family has been living in the desert for generations and have developed a unique culture that is both fascinating and terrifying.

The movie takes a dark turn as the group discovers that the mutants are not just random creatures but also seem to be connected to Ethel's family. The survivors must now confront their own mortality and the true nature of the monsters they are facing.

In the end, only one member of the group manages to escape the clutches of the mutants. As she flees into the desert, she is met with a shocking revelation: Ethel's family has been watching her from the shadows, waiting for her to join their twisted community.

The Hills Have Eyes 2 received mixed reviews from critics but was praised for its gruesome and unsettling atmosphere. The movie's use of practical effects and its willingness to push boundaries made it a standout in the horror genre. However, some critics felt that the movie's plot was predictable and that the characters were underdeveloped.

Overall, The Hills Have Eyes 2 is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of survival, family, and the dangers of the desert. While it may not be as iconic as its predecessor, it remains a solid addition to the Hills Have Eyes franchise.

documents.title: Employee of the Month
documents.tagline: In order to get the girl, he's gotta get his shift together.
documents.overview: When he hears that the new female employee digs ambitious men who are the store employee of the month, a slacker gets his act together but finds himself in competition with his rival, an ambitious co-worker.
documents.plot: When he hears that the new female employee digs ambitious men who are the store employee of the month, a slacker gets his act together but finds himself in competition with his rival, an ambitious co-worker.

documents.title: Turistas
documents.tagline: There are some places tourists should never go
documents.overview: A group of young backpackers' vacation turns sour when a bus accident leaves them marooned in a remote Brazilian rural area that holds an ominous secret.
documents.plot:
Turistas, released in the United Kingdom and Ireland as Paradise Lost, is a 2006 American horror film produced and directed by John Stockwell from a screenplay by Michael Arlen Ross. It stars Josh Duhamel, Melissa George, Olivia Wilde, Desmond Askew, Max Brown and Beau Garrett, with Miguel Lunardi as the surgeon Zamora.

American backpacker Alex is touring Brazil with his sister Bea and her friend Amy. After their bus crashes on a remote road, they team up with two British travelers, Finn and Liam, and Pru, an Australian who speaks Portuguese. The group finds a beach bar full of partying tourists, but after a day in the sun they are drugged and wake up on the empty beach with their money, luggage and passports gone. A young local named Kiko offers to take them to his uncle's house deep in the forest. On the way, he badly injures his head diving into a pool beneath a waterfall. At the isolated house, the travelers find medicine, supplies and a drawer full of other people's passports.

That night, a helicopter brings Zamora, a doctor who arrives with his medical team and armed men. The tourists are beaten and captured, while Kiko escapes. Zamora removes Amy's organs while she is still alive, telling the bound Finn that he is taking back what rich foreigners have taken from Brazil and sending the organs to a hospital in Rio de Janeiro to help the poor. With Kiko's help, the others break out of their cages. Finn is rescued but shot dead as they escape, and Liam stays behind to fight and is captured. The survivors flee through the jungle to an underwater cave, where Zamora kills Kiko and wounds Alex. Separated in the flooded passages, Bea kills an archer working for the gang. When the three survivors come out of the cave, Alex attacks Zamora with a rock, but henchman Jamoru arrives with a rifle. Ordered to kill the tourists, Jamoru instead shoots Zamora and walks away. Villagers take in the survivors. At the airport, Alex advises a pair of arguing tourists to take the plane rather than the bus.

Turistas was the first American film shot entirely in Brazil. It was also the first release from Fox Atomic, a label of 20th Century Fox, which opened it on December 1, 2006. It debuted in eighth place and grossed about $14.7 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said that beautiful scenery and cinematography could not make up for wooden acting and a stale, predictable plot.

documents.title: Enemy of the State
documents.tagline: It's not paranoia if they're really after you.
documents.overview: A hotshot Washington criminal lawyer becomes the target of a rogue security executive videotaped in the act of murdering a congressman when the incriminating tape is surreptitiously slipped into his shopping bag by the videographer, who is fleeing the executive's assassins.
documents.plot:
Enemy of the State is a 1998 American action thriller film directed by Tony Scott and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films. The movie stars Will Smith, Gene Hackman, Jon Voight, and Regina King.

The story begins with Robert Dean (Will Smith), an insurance investigator who works for a large corporation in Washington D.C. He is married to his wife, Dr. Margaret Dean (Regina King), and they have a young son together. However, their happiness is short-lived as Robert's boss, Franklin Haines (Jon Voight), assigns him to investigate the death of a former colleague.

As Robert delves deeper into the case, he discovers that his colleague was murdered by a group of rogue agents working for the National Security Agency (NSA). The agents, led by the ruthless and cunning Agent Albert Gibson (Gene Hackman), are using advanced surveillance technology to monitor and control the population. They have created a system called "The Net," which allows them to track anyone's movements and activities.

Robert soon realizes that he is being watched by the NSA and that his life is in danger. He goes into hiding, but Agent Gibson is relentless in his pursuit of Robert. As the stakes rise, Robert teams up with a computer expert named Kit (Gary Baseman), who helps him understand the extent of The Net's capabilities.

As the story unfolds, Robert discovers that he has been identified as an enemy of the state by the NSA. He learns that his investigation into the death of his colleague was not just a coincidence, but rather a deliberate attempt to expose the agency's wrongdoing. With Kit's help, Robert sets out to take down The Net and bring Agent Gibson to justice.

The plot thickens as Robert and Kit go on the run, using advanced technology to evade the NSA agents. Along the way, they encounter a mysterious woman named Susan (Linda Fiorentino), who becomes entangled in their quest for truth.

As the action unfolds, Robert's personal life begins to unravel. His marriage is put to the test as he struggles to balance his work and family responsibilities with his newfound mission to take down The Net. In a thrilling climax, Robert and Kit face off against Agent Gibson and his team in a high-stakes battle of wits and technology.

In the end, Robert succeeds in destroying The Net and exposing the NSA's wrongdoing. However, not before Agent Gibson reveals that he has been working for a shadowy organization known as "The Syndicate," which is pulling the strings from behind the scenes. As Robert returns to his normal life, he knows that there are still many secrets lurking in the shadows, waiting to be uncovered.

Overall, Enemy of the State is a gripping action thriller that explores themes of government surveillance, corporate greed, and personal freedom. With its breakneck pace and memorable performances, it has become a classic of 90s action cinema.

documents.title: Philadelphia
documents.tagline: No one would take on his case... until one man was willing to take on the system.
documents.overview: Two competing lawyers join forces to sue a prestigious law firm for AIDS discrimination. As their unlikely friendship develops their courage overcomes the prejudice and corruption of their powerful adversaries.
documents.plot:
Philadelphia is a drama film released in 1993, directed by Jonathan Demme and produced by TriStar Pictures. The movie stars Tom Hanks as Andrew Beckett, a young lawyer who is fired from his job at a prestigious law firm due to his AIDS diagnosis.

The story begins with Andrew Beckett (Tom Hanks), a successful and ambitious lawyer working for the law firm of Joseph Miller & Keefe. However, when he contracts HIV through a blood transfusion during a surgery, his life takes a drastic turn. Despite being aware of his condition, Andrew is fired from his job due to the stigma surrounding AIDS at that time.

Andrew seeks help from his friend and colleague, Joe Miller (Denzel Washington), who is also a lawyer at the firm. However, when Joe tries to support Andrew, he is met with resistance from their boss, Alvin "Al" Courtenay (Martin Landau). Courtenay refuses to acknowledge Andrew's condition and instead accuses him of being "unfit for work."

Andrew decides to take on his former employer in a lawsuit, claiming wrongful termination due to his AIDS diagnosis. He hires a new lawyer, Joe Miller, who agrees to take on the case despite the risks involved.

As the trial progresses, it becomes clear that Courtenay's actions were motivated by fear and prejudice against people with HIV/AIDS. The court ultimately rules in Andrew's favor, awarding him $1.4 million in damages.

Throughout the film, Tom Hanks delivers a powerful performance as Andrew Beckett, conveying the emotional toll of being ostracized due to his condition. Denzel Washington also shines as Joe Miller, who becomes a source of support and strength for Andrew during this difficult time.

The movie tackles themes of prejudice, discrimination, and the importance of human rights. The film's portrayal of the AIDS epidemic in the 1990s is both poignant and thought-provoking, highlighting the need for greater understanding and acceptance of people living with HIV/AIDS.

In the end, Andrew Beckett emerges victorious, but not without scars. The film concludes on a hopeful note, as Andrew begins to rebuild his life and find a new sense of purpose. The movie's powerful message about the importance of empathy and compassion resonates long after the credits roll.

Overall, Philadelphia is a masterful drama that explores themes of prejudice, identity, and the human condition. With outstanding performances from Tom Hanks and Denzel Washington, this film remains a powerful and thought-provoking classic of American cinema.

documents.title: Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason
documents.original_title: Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason
documents.tagline: Same Bridget. Brand new diary.
documents.overview: Bridget Jones is becoming uncomfortable in her relationship with Mark Darcy. Apart from discovering that he's a conservative voter, she has to deal with a new boss, a strange contractor and the worst vacation of her life.
documents.plot:
Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason is a romantic comedy of 2004 directed by Beeban Kidron and written by Andrew Davies, Helen Fielding, Richard Curtis and Adam Brooks, based on Fielding's 1999 novel and serving as the sequel to Bridget Jones's Diary (2001). Renée Zellweger returns as Bridget, with Colin Firth as her boyfriend Mark Darcy, Hugh Grant as her former lover Daniel Cleaver, and Jim Broadbent and Gemma Jones as her parents.

Bridget is blissful in her new relationship with Mark, until she meets his young and beautiful assistant, Rebecca Gillies, and her confidence collapses. At work in morning television, she reluctantly agrees to co-host a travel series with Daniel. Hoping for a proposal, she attends a Law Council dinner with Mark that becomes a string of humiliations. After a row, Mark comes to her flat to apologize, tells her for the first time that he loves her and takes her skiing in Lech, Austria, where Rebecca also turns up. A pregnancy scare proves negative.

At a lunch with their parents, Mark's brush-off of questions about marriage wounds Bridget, and when he declines to answer her suspicions about a phone message from Rebecca, she ends the relationship. She heads to Thailand with her friend Shazza and Daniel to film the travel show. After accidentally eating hallucinogenic mushrooms, she grows flirtatious with Daniel again, but the arrival of a prostitute he had ordered convinces her he has not changed. Shazza's young fling, Jed, gives her a decorative snake bowl that ends up in Bridget's luggage, and when airport sniffer dogs find cocaine hidden inside, Bridget is thrown into a crowded cell. She befriends her cellmates, teaching them Madonna's "Like a Virgin". Mark arrives to tell her she will soon be free, but when she lets him believe she slept with Daniel, he coolly leaves.

Back in London, Mark brawls with Daniel in a fountain for abandoning Bridget, and Bridget returns home a minor celebrity. Her friends reveal that Mark personally tracked down Jed and secured the confession that cleared her. Rushing to his house, she finds Rebecca there, but Rebecca confesses that she is attracted to Bridget herself and kisses her; Bridget gently declines. Bridget asks Mark for another chance, and he proposes. At her parents' renewal of their vows, she catches the bouquet.

Shot in London and Austria between October 2003 and February 2004, the film grossed about $265 million worldwide, though critics found it predictable.

documents.title: The Incredibles
documents.tagline: No gut, no glory
documents.overview: Bob Parr has given up his superhero days to log in time as an insurance adjuster and raise his three children with his formerly heroic wife in suburbia. But when he receives a mysterious assignment, it's time to get back into costume.
documents.plot:
The Incredibles is a 2004 animated superhero film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of a family with superpowers, who are forced to hide their abilities and live a normal life.

The film begins with Bob Parr (Mr. Incredible), a former superhero known as Mr. Incredible, who is now a suburban dad living in Municiberg, New Jersey. He works for a company called Supers Inc., which provides superheroes with jobs and benefits. However, Bob's life is not as ordinary as it seems. He longs to return to his superhero days and save the world from evil.

Bob's wife, Helen (Elastigirl), is also a former superhero known as Elastigirl, who has been forced to retire due to her age and the lack of respect for superheroes in society. Their children, Dash and Violet, are also gifted with superpowers - Dash can run at incredible speeds, while Violet can turn invisible and project force fields.

The family's life is disrupted when a mysterious figure named Buddy Pine ( Syndrome) appears, claiming to be a huge fan of Mr. Incredible. However, it soon becomes apparent that Buddy has an ulterior motive - he wants to become a superhero himself and destroy the superheroes who have been deemed "outdated" by society.

Buddy's plan is to use a device called the Omnidroid, which can absorb and neutralize superpowers. The Omnidroid is designed to hunt down and eliminate all superheroes, making it easier for Buddy to become the world's greatest superhero.

As the story unfolds, Bob, Helen, Dash, and Violet must work together to stop Buddy and his Omnidroid. Along the way, they discover that their powers are not just a gift, but also a responsibility. They learn to use their abilities in creative ways to outsmart the villain and save the day.

The climax of the movie features an epic battle between the Parr family and Buddy's Omnidroid. The family uses their unique powers to work together and defeat the robot, saving the city from destruction.

In the end, Bob and Helen are able to reconcile with each other and find a way to balance their superhero lives with their family life. They also learn that being a superhero is not just about having powers, but also about working together as a team and using one's abilities for the greater good.

The Incredibles received widespread critical acclaim for its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and stunning animation. The movie was a commercial success, grossing over $631 million worldwide and spawning two sequels, Incredibles 2 (2018) and a short film, Jack-Jack Attack (2005).

documents.title: Let's Go to Prison
documents.tagline: Welcome to the slammer
documents.overview: When a career criminal's plan for revenge is thwarted by unlikely circumstances, he puts his intended victim's son in his place by putting him in prison...and then joining him.
documents.plot:
After serving three prison sentences, repeat offender John Lyshitski plots revenge on Judge Nelson Biederman III, a tough judge who presided over each of his trials, passing him stiff sentences. John calls the courthouse to determine when he will next preside over a case, only to discover that he died three days before John's release.
John turns his attention to the late judge's obnoxious son, Nelson Biederman IV. At a dedication ceremony for Judge Biederman, he breaks into Nelson's car, emptying his emergency inhaler. After the ceremony, John stalks Nelson in his van; a hyperventilating Nelson frantically searches through a pharmacy's shelves for a new inhaler, with his erratic behavior making the owners think he is a junkie and mistake him for a violent robber. The police arrive and arrest Nelson. John is ecstatic that Nelson has landed in the criminal justice system which he suffered in for so long at the hands of Nelson's father.
Charged with felony assault, Nelson demands that the Biederman Foundation get him acquitted. The board nearly complies, but realizing they were fed up with Nelson's abuse, intentionally provided him with a grossly incompetent defense team at the trial. The jury find Nelson guilty and he is sentenced to three to five years in state prison. John, not satisfied with Nelson merely going to prison, decides to get himself arrested by purposely selling narcotics to undercover cops, despite seeing through the Cheech & Chong ruse. At his trial before the same judge Nelson had, John pleads guilty and convinces her he should be sentenced to three to five years in the same prison as Nelson.
John bribes a prison guard to become Nelson's cellmate, pretends to be his friend, and gives Nelson terrible advice on surviving in prison. Despite being an unhardened and inexperienced prisoner, Nelson gets himself out of the many situations that John's misinformation creates. He meets G-Lords leader Barry, an imposing, brawny African-American gay man who coerces him into a relationship. Despite his intimidating appearance, Barry is a sensitive romantic, supplying potential romantic partners with his finest toilet-made Merlot.
Nelson angers White Kingdom leader Lynard by ratting him out on a prison shanking, who vows to kill him after being thrown in the hole. After Lynard is released, Nelson acquires a syringe containing deadly chemicals to commit suicide; before he can do so, Lynard attacks him in his cell. The syringe falls out of Nelson's pocket, Lynard assumes it is narcotics and injects himself, accidentally killing himself, and Nelson earns the respect of and authority over the White Kingdom.
Nelson reaches his one-year parole hearing relatively unharmed, and as the new leader of the white supremacist gang for "killing" Lynard. Nelson, who initially submits to being Barry's partner out of fear, grows to care for him, willingly playing along with the "relationship" to keep him happy.

documents.title: Goal! II: Living the Dream
documents.tagline: This time the dream is real.
documents.overview: Tempted away from Newcastle United to join Real Madrid, rising star Santiago Munez finds this latest change of fortune the greatest challenge yet - personally as well as professionally. He is reunited with Gavin Harris, though they must compete to be on the team, and estranged from fiancee Roz, whose nursing career keeps her back home.
documents.plot:
Goal II: Living the Dream is a 2007 sports drama directed by Jaume Collet-Serra from a screenplay by Mike Jefferies, Adrian Butchart and Terry Loane. The sequel to Goal! (2005) and the second part of a trilogy, it stars Kuno Becker as the Mexican footballer Santiago Muñez, with Alessandro Nivola, Anna Friel, Stephen Dillane, Leonor Varela, Elizabeth Peña and Rutger Hauer, and features cameo appearances by real Real Madrid players.

Santiago, now a star at Newcastle United, is signed by Real Madrid, where he is reunited with his flamboyant former teammate Gavin Harris. His fiancée, Roz, stays behind in Newcastle to finish her nursing training, and the long-distance relationship soon strains. Santiago makes a winning debut and quickly becomes the club's new star, but fame brings complications. He is approached by Enrique, a younger half-brother he never knew, who shows him a photograph of their mother, Rosa María, who abandoned Santiago as a small child, and he learns that his grandmother knew she was living in Madrid.

Distracted, Santiago is sent off in his first start, and after a drunken night with the television presenter Jordana García he misses the team flight to a Champions League match in Norway, earning the wrath of manager Rudi van der Merwe. He fires his loyal agent Glen Foy, injures his ankle and cancels Christmas plans with Roz, and when a second kiss with Jordana is leaked to the press, Roz breaks off their engagement. Meanwhile Enrique steals Santiago's Lamborghini and crashes it, and Santiago is arrested after taking the blame and assaulting a photographer at the hospital, where he finally sees his mother.

After scoring the goal that sends Madrid into the Champions League final, Santiago visits Rosa, who explains that she fled to Madrid after being attacked, and returned to Mexico to find the family gone to the United States. Reconciled with his mother and Enrique, he asks Rudi to start Gavin in the final against Arsenal to help his friend's career, and apologizes to Roz. Madrid fall behind 2–0, but after coming on, Santiago sets up a goal for Gavin and scores the equalizer, before David Beckham wins the match with a late free kick.

Released in the United Kingdom on February 9, 2007, the film received mixed to negative reviews for its predictable and melodramatic script and grossed only about $7.8 million worldwide, though it later found a cult audience. Goal III followed in 2009.

documents.title: Save the Last Dance
documents.tagline: The Only Person You Need To Be Is Yourself.
documents.overview: After the death of her mother, Sara moves to the South Side of Chicago to live with her father and gets transferred to a majority-black school. Her life takes a turn for the better when befriends Chenille and her brother Derek, who helps her with her dancing skills.
documents.plot:
Seventeen-year-old Sara Johnson, an aspiring ballet dancer in suburban Chicago, auditions for the Juilliard School after asking her mother to attend. Sara performs poorly and is rejected. Soon afterward, she learns that her mother was killed in a car accident while traveling to the audition. Blaming herself, Sara abandons ballet and moves to Chicago's South Side to live with her estranged father, Roy, a jazz trumpeter. Roy initially struggles to communicate with Sara, but they gradually begin rebuilding their relationship.
Sara transfers to a majority-Black high school, where she befriends Chenille Reynolds, a teenage single mother. Chenille takes her to a nightclub called Stepps and introduces her to her brother Derek, an ambitious student who hopes to attend Georgetown University and become a pediatrician. After seeing Sara struggle with hip-hop dancing, Derek offers to teach her. The two begin practicing together, combining elements of ballet and hip hop.
Derek takes Sara to see the Joffrey Ballet, prompting her to discuss her mother's death and her abandoned ambitions. Their friendship develops into a romantic relationship. At Stepps, however, a jealous Nikki interrupts them, and Malakai, Derek's longtime friend, insults Sara by saying that there's no point on trying to be with him. Derek reassures Sara that he is no longer involved with Nikki as Sara accepts his apology. After learning that he has been accepted into Georgetown, he encourages Sara to audition for Juilliard again.
Tensions intensify at school when Nikki picks a fight with Sara. At the clinic, Chenille tells Sara that while she disapproves Nikki's behavior, she understands her resentment of a white girl "stealing" Derek, who is rare in the community. Deeply hurt by Chenille's words and the backlash becoming too much for her to handle, Sara breaks up with Derek.
Meanwhile, Malakai asks Derek to participate in a drive-by shooting scheduled for the night of Sara's audition, and Derek initially agrees. Roy encourages Sara to stop blaming herself for her mother's death and pursue ballet again. Chenille, regretting what she said earlier, confess to Derek that her own frustration with Kenny, the absent father of her child, made her unfairly resentful and envious of his relationship with Sara. She urges Derek to reconcile with Sara and warns that helping Malakai could jeopardize his future. Derek confronts Malakai and refuses to take part in the shooting.
Sara begins her Juilliard audition but becomes unsettled after making a mistake. Derek arrives and encourages her to continue. She completes a routine combining ballet and hip hop and is accepted into the school. The drive-by shooting fails and Malakai is arrested. Sara and Derek reconcile, and the film ends with them joining Chenille and their friends at Stepps to celebrate Sara's acceptance.

documents.title: Mystery Men
documents.tagline: We're not your classic heroes, we're the other guys.
documents.overview: When Champion City's hero Captain Amazing is kidnapped by the recently paroled supervillain Casanova Frankenstein, a trio of average, everyday superheroes -- Mr. Furious, the Shoveler and the Blue Raja -- assemble a new super team to save him.
documents.plot: When Champion City's hero Captain Amazing is kidnapped by the recently paroled supervillain Casanova Frankenstein, a trio of average, everyday superheroes -- Mr. Furious, the Shoveler and the Blue Raja -- assemble a new super team to save him.

documents.title: Lake Placid
documents.tagline: You'll never know what bit you.
documents.overview: When a man is eaten alive by an unknown creature, the local Game Warden teams up with a paleontologist from New York to find the beast. Add to the mix an eccentric philanthropist with a penchant for "Crocs", and here we go! This quiet, remote lake is suddenly the focus of an intense search for a crocodile with a taste for live animals...and people!
